review_comment: Regrettably, my schedule doesn't allow for extensive gaming sessions of this nature. Moreover, the experience is notably enhanced when shared with a companion. It appears that potential buyers may be deterred by the misconception that the game merely entails mundane farming activities. Despite having invested approximately 100 hours into the mobile version, I occasionally find myself adrift within the game's mechanics.

There can be a bit of a learning curve if you've never played, a lot of hindsight moments if you decide to play blind (which can be fun in its own way) but the Stardew wiki is extensive and there are MANY mods available on Nexus mods. I have played exclusively vanilla until about 3 days ago and I am loving the mod expansions (SVE + Ridgeside). Love love love, can't recommend enough. I recommend Nexus for Stardew mods.

review_comment: When I was 13, the first game my parents had to come tell me to turn off and sleep at 2am was Harvest Moon 64. Everything about that game had me absolutely hooked and wanting to progress and see the story unfold while taking care of animals, fishing, farming, and doing side quests. Stardew Valley is the only game that has been able to give me the same feeling (in terms of simulator games). I played other Harvest Moon games, other Story of Seasons games throughout the years, but would never play long because I never felt that same spark. Stardew Valley does everything HM64 does and more. It will forever be one of my favorites as it has continually improved and encompassed what these type of games should be.

review_comment: Stardew is a really good game to play if you want to take things at your own pace. A lot can change depending on how you choose to play or act. There's a lot of replay-ability if you want to start a new farm or make a new profession, or even marry a different NPC. Alone or with friends it's fun. Achievement hunting is definitely doable if you enjoy that, or just want to hang out on your farm. I have very fond memories of when Multiplayer just came out and my husband, Mom and I made a little family farm. I'll never forget the day Mom found Mayor Lewis' lucky purple shorts and when reading that she was supposed to be discreet in the delivery, she ran down the road holding them above her head to give them to him, uncontrollably laughing the entire time. Easily my best Stardew memory. My mom played this game a lot solo, and we only got to play it a bit together before she passed but it brought her a lot of joy. So from the both of us it's a definite recommend.

review_comment: Stardew Valley, an indie farming simulation game, has captured the hearts of gamers worldwide, establishing itself as a beloved classic in the gaming community. This virtual oasis not only offers a tranquil escape from reality but also provides a myriad of engaging activities that cater to diverse player interests. From tending to crops, raising animals, mining in the depths of the earth, fishing in idyllic waters, to forming meaningful relationships with townsfolk, the game offers a rich tapestry of experiences. Its pixel art style, enchanting soundtrack, and charming characters add to the game's allure, creating a cozy and immersive world that players can easily get lost in. Stardew Valley's open-ended gameplay allows for personalization and creativity, granting players the freedom to shape their virtual farm according to their preferences. The game's attention to detail, depth of content, and the sense of accomplishment derived from building and expanding one's farm make it a truly captivating and rewarding experience. Its seamless integration of farming, crafting, exploration, and social interactions ensures that players are constantly engaged and have a wide array of activities to delve into. The game's emphasis on relaxation and self-paced gameplay provides a soothing and therapeutic experience, allowing players to unwind and escape the stresses of everyday life. Furthermore, Stardew Valley's community-focused approach, where players are encouraged to contribute to the well-being of the town and help their neighbors, fosters a sense of camaraderie and belonging. The game's continuous updates and developer support demonstrate a commitment to its player base, ensuring that there is always something new and exciting to discover in the world of Stardew Valley. With its timeless appeal, infinite replay value, and genuine passion poured into every aspect of its design, Stardew Valley stands as a testament to the sheer brilliance and artistry of indie game development, solidifying its place as one of the best games to ever exist.

review_comment: Boy oh boy where do I even begin. Sebastian... honey, my pookie bear. I have loved you ever since I first laid eyes on you. The way you sleep for 13 hours and spend twenty minutes outside your bedroom. Your silky smooth emo haircut, and that gorgeous face. I would do anything for you. I wish it were possible to freeze time so I would never have to watch you move from pelican town. You had a rough childhood, but you never gave up hope. You are even amazing off the court, you're a great husband and father, sometimes I even call you dad. I forvever dread and weep, thinking of the day you will one day leave Pelican. I would sacrifice my own life it were the only thing that could put a smile on your beautiful face. You have given me so much joy, and heartbreak over the years. I remember when you first left pelican and its like my heart got broken into a million pieces. But a tear still fell from my right eye (and my weewee) when I watched you fix your motorbike, because deep down, my glorious king deserved it. I just wanted you to return home. Then allas, you did, my sweet baby boy came home and I rejoiced. 2015 was a hard year for us baby, but in 2016 you made history happen. You came back and I couldn't believe it. I was crying, bawling even, and I heard my glorious king exclaim these words, "PELICAN TOWN THIS IS FOR YOU!" Not only have you changed the game of alternative fashion, queer relationships and the world forever, but you've eternally changed my world. And now you're getting older, but still the goat, my goat. I love you pookie bear, my glorious king, Sebastian.☺️♥️🫶🏻

review_comment: A very close and dear friend gifted this game to me and I have been obsessed ever since. The pixel art is beautiful, the seasons are stunning, and the lore is incredible. I was going through a rough time in my life when I first started playing this game and it always made me feel better, even if I could only play for a few minutes. The attention to every little detail is what amazes me about this game. I thought at first getting to know the villagers was just an annoying task, however, I couldn't have been more wrong. Getting to know the villagers and each of their unique personalities, likes, and dislikes keeps the game entertaining and feeling fresh. The villagers aren't portrayed as perfect pixel people, but rather struggles that many people face on a daily basis (addiction/grief/financial struggles/aging). Each season is uniquely beautiful and has a wonderful event (Dance of the Moonlight Jellies is my personal favorite). The game is so inherently relaxing to me, that I listen to the soundtrack when I'm feeling a great deal of stress. My original game was on the switch until I was gifted it on steam. So, it's gonna take me a while because my previous game was my legacy save. I would recommend this game to anyone and give it a 10/10. Eric Barone, the creator, deserves all the appraise he receives.

review_comment: This game has always been a comfort game for me, It's something i play whenever I'm going through a hard time. I had forgotten about this game a couple years ago and have finally come back to playing it. So far it's been an incredibly enjoyable game and I've made quick progress despite only being on year 1. This game isn't for everyone, and some people may think it's too tedious or repetitive but I think that's the comfort of it. It's easy to catch on what to do and once you get the hang of it everything changes. It's not just a farming game, it has so much story and unique characters, stories, and you can play it however you like! Whether you want to focus on fishing, maybe mining, or Farming! I love the style and art of the game as well, it has just such an enjoyable look to it and the music is easy to listen to and also quite enjoyable. Yes this game may not be for everyone, but for those that like something that's just inbetween story and exploration, this one is just for you. You'll start off limited but you'll find new islands, places, and more! Yes eventually you'll learn everything about the game eventually, but walking away for just a couple months makes playing it again such an amazing experience. Especially with all these recent updates, the game is so different but still the same from what it was. I love this game so much and It's so fun. Just don't forget to make sprinklers when your farm gets bigger. made that mistake one too many times.

review_comment: You start with a child named Atreus. After killing zues in the last installment, you now find yourself in a different realm. You seem to have transported to norse mythology and are hiding from the gods to raise your child. After a short tutorial section you encounter a stranger at your door. He seems pretty weak at first, however you are caught off guard when he reveals his full capability to you. throughout this boss fight you learn he is immortal, however you seemingly kill him by snapping his neck. He knew your past and this is dangerous for what you are trying to so. Despite all this, the main premise of the game is to spread your deceased wifes ashes atop the tallest mountain in the nine realms. As you climb your way up you are met with several creative challenges. These puzzles are a great addition as they test your wit and keep you immersed. I have also yet to mention the introduction to boss fights. They usuall pop out unexpectedly, meaning you never know when you could catch yourself in a tough battle. A great example of this is when you are almost at the top of the mountain. as you go up an elevator you are met with a giant dragon that stops you from progressing. This was one of the coolest fights in the game. Apon reaching the top, you are met with a prisoner of odins. You chop off his head and revive it to aid you on your jeourney as through his wisdom you find out you have climbed the wrong mountain. After this, you have to complete a bunch of tasks to fast travel up the correct mountain, but are faces with many obsticles. One of these are thors sons witch fail at killing you. Kratos spares them and we see them again later. Shortly after this you decide its time for your son atreus to know hes a god. This turns out badly however as he goes on a power trip, pushing a bleeding out god off of a cliff believing he can do whatever he wants. Later, you will find baldur and follow him through another realm. As you try to escape, you start to learn his past. He hates that his mother made him immortal and wishes to become human. When you escape he surprises you and you have another encounter. Baldur goes to punch your son but punches a strange arrow on his quiver that makes him mortal. While the rest of the fight takes place his mother tries futiley to stop you. You end up sparing him but later see him trying to kill his mother. You then kill him. At the post credit scene thor destroys your home and encounters you. The game hen ends.

review_comment: Stardew Valley is a charming and delightful game that captivates players with its relaxing gameplay and heartwarming story. The diverse activities in the game, from farming and fishing to mining and building relationships with villagers, offer a wide range of experiences to enjoy. The soothing soundtrack complements the game perfectly, creating a calming atmosphere as you tend to your farm and explore the world. Stardew Valley is a cozy escape into a world filled with endless possibilities and heartwarming interactions. The game's attention to detail is extraordinary, from the changing seasons to the unique personalities of the villagers you befriend. The sense of progression and accomplishment as you cultivate your farm, participate in festivals, and uncover the secrets of the valley is incredibly rewarding. The game's open-ended nature allows you to play at your own pace, whether you want to focus on farming, mining, fishing, or exploring the caves. With its mix of relaxation and engaging gameplay i'd 100% recommend this game.

The cutscenes though although wonderfully made, could be easily missed if you don't look it up at the wiki. The town starts to repeat itself after like year 3 so unless you got a mod going. review_comment: This is a good game. So why the red then? Because this delightful game has been nearly totally ruined for me by the developer himself. When Stardew valley came out one of the things that made me slam 100 hours into the game was how queer friendly the game was. Clothes weren't gender locked, yet still had a nice variety of presentations, you could marry regardless of sex, and lastly, but to ME most importantly, you could marry polyamourously. Now everything else has been left in, but one day the developer removed the ability to date multiple people, and not only made it so you wouldn't get the positive cut scenes with your lovers, but also went the EXTRA MILE to add a SLUT SHAMING SCENE where all of your consenting, knowing, partners act like you cheated on them out of NOWHERE. Now, I had hoped that this kind of blatant anti queerness in an else wise queer accepting game would be quickly corrected. Yet here we are four ish years later and the dev is still insisting that this "makes the relationships more special" by "limiting it to one per in game life". But this is nothing more than anti poly sentiment that I already get enough of irl. My irl GF's don't feel "less special" just because I have three, they're all compleatly different relationships! Dating Sebastian isn't the same as dating Abby isn't the same as getting to date both at once. Frankly it's bad enough I have to deal with people irl treating me badly for being poly. I don't deserve to be slut shamed in my cute cottage core game. Until this inequality is fixed I won't be able to enjoy the game so thumbs down it is.

review_comment: Portal 2 is basically just two games in one package, where you have the continuation of Portal One as a single-player adventure and the multiplayer story with ATLAS and P-Body. Honestly, finding fault in either of them is hard. The story mode builds upon what Portal One had already established in a great way, flinging you through an old familiar aperture science center but with a new rundown aesthetic, together with your robot NPC companion, who is just one of the funniest little orbs I've encountered to date. As for the multiplayer, let's just put it this way: I played through it with my friend, who made an anatomical observation and determined I had shown symptoms of something called "big brain". Sadly, it seems to have not been a permanent malady; alas, once in a while he will remind me of this diagnosis instead of giving a new complimentary observation. review_comment: Through no fault of your own you awaken the corpse of GLaDoS, the artificial intelligence hell-bent on making life as miserable and scientifically valuable as possible. The reanimated skeleton of Portal’s villain returns 80% corrupted, but still mostly the same. She sneers at you, berates you, calls you fat, ugly, adopted and dumb. She does what she always does: tests you. Everything new to you that is discovered in Portal 2 is inherently old and abandoned: Cave Johnson, the dead CEO of Aperture Science, clings on through whirring tapes, GlaDoS is alive but without a true purpose, and Wheatley is battling demons no-one can validate. Everything within the facility is moving towards a result that is irrelevant because the people to whom it mattered are no longer alive. Aperture Science is a maimed titan clinging on, and your role is to escape it. You are abandoned and forgotten like the machinery you interact with, and there is beyond a shroud of doubt the creeping feeling that you are alone in this. The dread that comes from being within what is ultimately a dying entity is haunting. Furthermore, the sarcastic, dry humour of Portal distances you even further from your surroundings. Not only are you not wanted here, but you are hated for it. Stylistically and narratively Portal 2 is hands down one of the best games ever made. It knows exactly what it is and excels at it.

review_comment: This is a great game. It's a continuation of Portal, but it's so much better and longer. For the first half of the game, you go through test chambers, but this time, you're not alone. One of the personality cores, Wheatly, tags along, pretending to be your helpful companion, to take down GLaDOS. It works, but Wheatly becomes mad with power and takes over the facility, but not before putting GLaDOS' core into a potato battery. Anyway, for the second half of the game, you go through more test chambers, reunite with GLaDOS, go through even more test chambers, and defeat Wheatly before the facility explodes. There's also a brand new Co-Op mode with its own story, and a puzzle editor where you can create your own puzzles, upload them to the Steam Workshop, and play them with friends. Overall, this game offers many hours of fun & challenging gameplay.

review_comment: As someone who has nearly 100 hours in the game (97 as of writing this), I can easily say this is my favorite game of all time. It takes well thought out, extremely fun puzzles, hilarious comedy, and a story that immediately gets you invested and combines them together to make, in my opinion, one of the greatest games in the world. The characters are fun and well written, the puzzles feel really good to solve, and there were certain moments in the game that had me laughing out loud. Not only that, but there were multiple moments in the game that gave me literal chills. The world building is also insanely good with countless stunning set pieces, and it really is crazy to think that this game is 14 years old. The soundtrack of the game also builds crazy suspense and the fact that the music changes depending on the environment really makes it feel like the music fits right into the universe. Overall, portal 2 is an amazing game with near perfect storytelling, game play, visuals, characters, and music to create one of the most mind blowing experiences you will ever get to enjoy.

review_comment: Beautiful sequel! It does not try to amp up the themes that were already masterfully developed in Portal. Instead it provides a flourishing variety of graphical styles and new gameplay that play homage to the first installment while providing a lot of fun and entertainment to the player. While the first game is dark and builds upon the oppressive feeling of loneliness and uncertainty, here you have talkative companions and you feel part of a story with a finale that is more and more anticipated. There is a fantastic comic relief in Wheatley and some psychological introspection about human nature with Glados/Caroline. Moreover the development of the character of Cave Johnson through the recordings and the framed portraits is subtle and remarkable. And the evolution of graphics and technology through the decades as you explore the old labs is really aesthetically pleasing. So in conclusion, really, really recommended game, brilliant and entertaining - just not as iconic, focused, and touching as the first one, which is a masterpiece.

review_comment: I was NOT expecting to love this game as much as I did. I'm a person who gets seriously stressed out when confronted with something I can't figure out, so puzzle games are usually a pass for me. However, this game had intuitive puzzle design that at times felt overwhelming, but when picked apart was really quite simple for the most part. I will say however that the test chambers were quite repetitive, and the segments outside of chambers were the parts that I enjoyed the most. It also felt like the game dragged on a little bit, but 4-5 hours really isn't terrible. I loved the character design and how each one was somewhat lovable/understandable in their own way (even though there were only 3 characters if you count the defects as 1 character). I feel like the game was somewhat lacking in protagonist character design, though, because it really just felt like our character was a vessel for the story to progress, when we should have been an interlocking part. I guess the game leaves it up to the player to be the protagonist's personality? Anyway, final sequence was clever and also somewhat heartwarming. I just love when games go and make their own lyrical soundtracks, it makes everything so much more cinematic (just take a look at Mirror's Edge!). Anyway, all in all pretty fun game and a story that actually wasn't too bad. (Also, the part where he kills you did get a pretty good laugh out of me :))
name: Portal 2

review_comment: A true height of gaming. This has to be Valve's second best series ever (it's not first because of Half-Life). The story is amazing and always fun to come back to. The test chamber creating feature is also really good to mess around with and it's great for using your own creativity. The physics are hilarious, causing lots of unexpected and funny results to all of your actions. The most amazing puzzle game I have ever played with an amazing credit song from Glados, just like in the first game. I heavily recommend this game to everyone, everyone. The 2 player mode is always fun to mess around with because you can really get on somebody's nerves by teleporting them back to the same spot repeatedly. The story is amazing and I could remember the whole story ages after playing. It connects well with Portal 1 so there's not many connections that you need to make, despite the fact that the second game is (if I remember correctly) set hundreds of years after the first Portal game. It's hard to explain why this game is so amazing without giving spoilers, so, why not go play it?

It's like a twisted science experiment where you're the subject, and the game is constantly testing just how much patience you have. review_comment: Gotta say, that was an odd experience. For such a beloved and oft-lauded title, I found this to be a notch below the first game on the whole. The first act was solid, on even footing with Portal 1's puzzles and had an interesting story (+funny new cast member in the form of Wheatley). Then the second act hit, and I was thoroughly disappointed in both the quality of the puzzles and the environmental design. Browns and grays all around made my time spent in the "dungeon" of Aperture Science largely miserable, and some obtuse puzzle gatekeeping made that even worse. The saving grace was Cave Johnson's funny bits, but even that got a little much after a while. Then the third act blew me away with how awesome it was, even a step above the best of the first game. So yeah, a weird ride for sure. I've landed on an 8/10 for this one: 9/10 first act, 5/10 second act, and 10/10 third act comes out to be about that. Very little desire to replay this one, though co-op is pretty enticing.

review_comment: Portal 2 is a great sequel to a great game and I would consider it as good, if not better than the original, as of course should be expected. Portal 2 continues on with same hilarious writing, supported by amazing voice acting. The gameplay also is up to par with original (meaning great), while also adding new mechanics to the puzzles. Visually it is an improvement from the original and depending on the chapter the appropriate atmosphere is there, helped by both visuals and sound design. The only negative, which is probably a nitpick, is that if memory serves me right, the first Portal's loading screens were much more seamless, though that probably is just a result of the upgrade in visuals... plus the loading times weren't long, so as I said, probably just a nitpick. As for co-op, I personally didn't try it out, so I can't speak on it. A last note, I do recommend to anyone curious about Portal 2 to first try out the first Portal. Other than that in my opinion Portal is still a great game, as you can see in this review, I compared Portal 2 a lot to the first Portal, that and Portal 2 is direct sequel, meaning that the writing of Portal 2 will hit harder if you played or at the very least watched or know about the story of the first. In conclusion, I enjoyed my time with Portal 2 and I recommend it!

review_comment: To me, this is the perfect puzzle game. It is challenging enough that I felt a pleasing sense of achievement completing it, but not so difficult that I had to look online for any solutions. The puzzles are all logical (unlike a few other puzzle games I have played where the solutions have only tenuous links to the problems being solved) and you know if you stick to it long enough, you will find the answers. Add to this excellent voice acting, genuinely likeable and funny antagonists, a great environment (especially in the middle part where you are running around the facilities trying to escape), which are not required for the gameplay but really add to the atmosphere and no woke annoyances. Although I love Steam as a service, it is a shame Valve do not make more games, I guess because of the money they make via streaming, as the ones they do make are always excellent.

review_comment: A massive improvement over Portal 1. The sequel addresses many of the criticisms of the original (movement is much better, puzzles are more complex and creative, and the singleplayer campaign is of a proper 8-9 hours in length) and introduces much-needed new mechanics, world-building, and character development. There are a some grievances: the game is still a linear Point A to Point B simulator with very little deviation, the humour is very hit-or-miss, and about 1/3 of the campaign is spent pixel-hunting for a tiny, white surface far into the background that you can shoot a portal onto. Still a good experience over a decade later, although this game is not as peerless as others claim it to be.

review_comment: This is one of the best video games ever created. Portal 1 was an iconic video game, and Portal 2 just adds so much more towards the franchise. It's been impressing me for 13 years, and continues to. If you haven't played it yet, I definitely recommend it. And if you haven't played the first one, I suggest you try it out. The story writing and plot is amazing, the level of humour is top notch. Also, when you complete the main story, you don't have to leave this amazing game. You can play CO-OP mode with a friend, family member, or even a stranger online. You can also create your own levels with an in-game designer, as well as play other people's levels as well, with very popular custom maps and even coded in tools like the gravity-gun from Half-Life. In terms of the game itself, the levels are a bit harder than the last game requiring you to think and puzzle solve, and for a first time run... a refreshing first experience filled with surprise, challenge, and an amazing world and story. Speaking of challenge, you can also play challenge mode. Play through every level again but with a twist... be timed, be forced to use as least portals as possible... and beat people's records online. Play Portal 2, it's great.

Outside of gathering a stronger sense of understanding and overall strategy, your fiftieth run feels pretty similar to your first run. The different decks can offer some interesting twists, but I'm still missing the sense of gradual progression and accumulation of abilities that are present in my favorite rogue-likes. review_comment: I like to call this a deck builder for people who don't normally play deck builders. That's what it is for me at least. It takes the three things that have normally kept me away from deck builders - the need to maximize a build permanently, the learning curve, and competition - and eliminated them. I really enjoy "push your luck" games along with games where you are aiming to beat your personal best, so this really has done the trick for me. Additionally, I appreciate that the learning curve is lessened by being based off of traditional poker hands but it's really not a poker game at all. This game is not only fun to play but an interesting masterclass in game design. If you've ever been curious about deck builders by have been weary of the factors I mentioned above, I'd definitely recommend Balatro.

review_comment: Godlike Rougue-like? Yeah they weren't kidding. Finally got around to playing this with Hades II launching in early access and man was I missing out. The game is amazing, music, combat, a very distinctive and beautiful artsyle. It takes an interesting approach to the genre, instead of a million unique items gotten at random, you pick one of 6 main weapons and will get upgrades to you character and weapon, thus it is more skill based and open to making actual builds without being insanely random. The gameplay is great, that's almost a given, if you like rougue-likes it is a no brainer, but what is most interesting to me is it's dialogue and narrative. I've never seen a rogue-like try this hard to tell a narrative, using the genre to its advantage, it is one of the best things about the game, the sheer amount of voice acted dialouge here is immpressive, all written and acted extremely well. It's one of the only rogue-likes where aside from doing runs for the sake of gameplay, I am invested in these character and how the story will play out. That is what makes the game special, there is so much depth to everything here, this world feels alive and rich and full of character. I could talk about it for a while but needless to say, it is one of the cornerstones of the genre, up there with the best of them, Worth every penny.

review_comment: Hades is a Rougelite in the clothing of greek mythology and my first game of this genre, the characteristic of the game which is to fail and "lose" progress was not so appealing to me. However, the nice music, story telling, charming art style and an entertaining combat system with an avoiding "dash" was astonishing fun to play. If you pair this with some skill and a healthy hunger to collect achievements you´re ready to go. Let´s dive a bit deeper into Hades without too much spoil. The characters were excellently brought to life through voice acting, this was a nice surprise for me, making the game world feel more immersive. When you interact with those characters, in some cases you can choose... yes you can! (your actions have consequences). The arsenal you wield can be enhanced alongside some bonuses which make your runs smoother, oh and not to forget the interesting interior decorations of the underworld. If you do not skip through all dialogues but immerse yourself in the story, you maybe surprised how many emotions will be woken... and even carried into the real life. The weak point of the game in my opinion is that it seems something is missing or could be more elaborated. Maybe there will be a link to Hades 2 where the story connects? For long time motivation it would be nice to have a larger choise then only getting the last overpriced piece of the underworld collection. This is not my cup of tea... is this genre made for long time motivation? perhaps you simply move on to the next Roguelite game or wait for the sequel? All in all I had a lot of fun with Hades. From time to time it can be quite a challenge, in such situations it is important not to lose the joy of playing the game, trying out a new style of play, or taking a break to strategize can be helpful to overcome the struggle. It´s nice to see some developers make solid effort in their work, trying to create a masterpiece. If you appreciate the Roguelite genre and you are willing to give Hades a try you won´t be disappointed. Have fun and enjoy Hades!

review_comment: Hades was probably my first real rogue-like game that I had ever played. I played it on my Nintendo Switch at first only to get the first ending. I decided to get it on PC to try and push for the 10 times completion for the true ending. I definitely enjoyed that process a lot, and trying out combinations, and then building the relationships with the different NPCs of the game. This is especially great when characters remark at your repeated deaths early on, and their reactions especially after beating through it. There's probably so much more that I still haven't really been able to see in the game, but I believe I got a good amount out of it, and I definitely recommend for anyone to try it out. It definitely gave me a good introduction into the rogue-like genre though, and it's a whole lot of fun once you understand how things work in the game. You might want to do a bit of your own research like I did after running through your own builds, or otherwise just in completely blind and I'm sure you'll still be able to enjoy it that way. I also really enjoy Greek mythology, and if that's something you dig, you'll dig this game too.

In the early game you will rarely take damage or be in range of dieing, but you have to go through this area every time you atempt a new run. I get that in roguelikes some early areas have to be easier, and they can give you ways to start your build in the early areas. But so many other Roguelike games that I have played mitigate the boredome of early areas much better. I was dissapointed with Hades because it had received so much aclaim and my expectations for it were high. But it did not deliver. I am not going to pretend that the game is horrible, because many people have dozens of hours in it. But if you are anything like me, then just play Dead Cells.

review_comment: As I reach the end of my natural life cycle with Hades, I only have good things reserved to say about this game. As of writing this I have 100% completed the game, and enjoyed it every step of the way. I don't have dozens of rogue-likes played, but I'm familiar to the genre. Hades' take on rogue-likes has truly paved the way for a multitude of other game formulas. There is never a run through Hades that will be like the last, this is the game's most celebrated mechanic. It keeps things fresh while simultaneously forcing the player to learn the different dynamics of its gameplay, albeit in a fun way. It's a game that isn't afraid to humble the player regularly, and also let them be insanely overpowered. If you're the type of person that loves addictive gameplay loops, crunching numbers, unique character designs, a fun story and seemless-smooth gameplay... then Hades is absolutely worth the purchase.

review_comment: One of the most satisfying and well made games I've played in a while. Gameplay is tigth af, with very few things that genuinely annoy you after the first 30 hours (♥♥♥♥ the shield enemies). The setting is one of the most unique takes on Ancient Greek Mythology in any game with likeable characters with all of which you can connect on a deeper, even romantical level with some of them. The grinding system is rewarding too, with each point of darkness you get you feel like the hours you spent trying to escape from the Underworld were more than well spent. There are many other great aspects to this game but for the best experience possible you absolutely HAVE TO go blind in it. There is nothing quite like experiencing all the niche little details the developers put into the game for the first time in your playthrough. Some can affect the map, others the characters you interact with and much more. It's the little things that make it feel so special and full of charm and you can tell Supergiant games loved every second of making the game

review_comment: The game goes in a very fun and casual direction with the lore of Greek mythology that make it super easy to get into the story. Voice acting I would say is fun, nothing crazy good, but the exchange of dialogue is without a doubt what make you as the player interested in all or some of the characters. The combat and difficulty of trying to beat/escape Hades is without a doubt one of the best elements in the game with a very simple but still layered progression system, let it be with you the main character or in boons(kinda like perks) and weapons. To be shy of 50 hours in the game I couldn't recommend it anymore for a solid price and can even be seen on sale a fair amount of times, and to also know that I've only scratched the surface with most of the collectibles, characters, and side stories, shows me greatly that this game has more than enough content. As of right now though I would say maybe the one negative is that the game is short, but its meant to be for how much you are meant to replay the game, however seeing how short it is, it would have been cool to see more twist and turns, but again this is coming from someone that hasn't fully done everything. Even when just looking around searching for the many easter eggs hidden in this game youre spending time with all these versions of mita and i actually grew to like many of the characters in the storyline because of their fun and unique personalities. And then of course theres the horror aspect. And let me tell you this, you can get jumpscared at times but in general i think this is on the less frightening side of horror games out there. The game strikes a good balance between horror, exploration and relaxing gameplay. It just gets so much right. Would have loved it to be a bit longer because you can speedrun this even with achievments in maybe 4-5 hours or so. Without even in like 2 or 3. Would have loved to see more of that intricate world of miside.

review_comment: I love this game! I decided even after completing the game, to fully complete all the achievements and it was a fun process going back to see small details I didn't see before. Straight down to the animation, art style, and story it's a great game! I think everyone should play through the game at least once and see how they feel about it, as it's a somewhat different approach to a horror game. The small subtle hints in everything as you go throughout the game are also fun to recognize after your first play through. The music is also very good and in certain points you might see yourself bobbing your head to the beat of some of the ambient songs that are playing through the game. The sounds and VO's are great and really immerse you into the game, which I love in story games. Gameplay it's self is really good you might see yourself stuck on certain points since the game tells you what to do, but doesn't always give you a hint even with this though it's still a great game and as always has room for improvement. Overall, for me this game is a 10/10 I can't wait to see how the devs keep improving the game and bringing more content to the game as a whole. I know there's going to be a big update at some point and I can't wait for it to release! To anyone who read through all this thank you, and have a good rest of your day or night!

review_comment: I bought this game only because I saw so many people playing it and also because it was cheap. I was not disappointed. I beat the game in one play through, roughly 4.5 hours. I love the style of this game, I don't think that I've ever played a game in this style but I'm sure there are some out there. The game isn't as scary as I thought it would be but it still had a decent amount of horror and scares to get my heart racing. The story is sort of like DDLC which I also enjoyed playing, but this one is a lot more interactive, and geometric... obviously. The game has a bunch of hidden things around the whole game, collectables, games, , which adds a good amount of replayability, it took me about another 4 hours to 100% but that was with a guide, I'm sure that it would take a bit longer if you tried to find everything yourself. Over all for $15 this game is so worth buying even if you're not into the anime style, I bought it mostly for the story, which I enjoyed a lot. I rate it a solid 10/10

review_comment: The best indie game I've ever played. I do like how this game combining so many genres without being boring yet interesting, and how it can suggest you unique gameplay with cute, adorable and interesting characters and how this game makes you enjoy spending time here and of course my favorite part is breaking the 4th wall, I do like when game designers do this trick and this game is full of these tricks. But let's, don't forget that this is a horror game, and of course this aspect is as not good as previous ones, but even so, game anyway creates scary atmosphere and can make you feel uncomfortable sometimes so I would say game designers managed to make this game scary. Considering all of these facts and taking into account that game was made by 2 guys, this is a masterpiece. Outstanding game indeed. So I would give it 9/10, I don't regret spending my money on this game (I bought it for full price). Let's talk about the drawbacks. Of course game is so short (around 3-4 hours), but come on this game was made by 2 guys so I'm satisfied that this game even released and I'm glad that I even heard about it. Not many endings, but maybe in future developers will add more endings (They've mentioned it in their discord). And of course I'm looking forward to playing peaceful mode (with The Cappie I hope 💙). If last two things are fulfilled, I will give it 10/10. I'm gonna buy soundtrack for this game to support developers more, and I hope that they will make a sequel or just game similar to this. Looking forward to any news about sequel. Praying for you 🕯️🧢 O Great Cappie💙

review_comment: At first I though this would be another Doki Doki Panic copy, but wow, it's so much better and more complete than that. This is a seriously good horror game with compelling story, characters, level design, and gameplay. It keeps getting fresh, with new mini games as well as new ways of getting scary. I personally can't stand horror games that make you constantly hide from something, and this game has one such section that is actually well executed and then it moves on. Sections where you must run away from a chaser through narrow corridors? Yes, it does that well too, but then it moves on to the next. PT references with looping corridors? It does that well too but then moves on to something else. It also has interesting commentary on the nature of games and life and routine, discussing the idea of "being trapped". Certainly a unique experience worth playing. It's fairly priced and has hours of replayability (many endings and choices) with collectibles that help build up the world of the game.

review_comment: Dumbfounded on how this game has received all the praise it has. A word I see being repeated a lot is "polished". Here, I would agree. The game has solid art direction; there's plenty of charm to the 3D anime style, and the soundtrack's quite beautiful, honestly. But, like many other polished things, it's all soft around the edges. The actual substance of this game is nothing but a collection of already done-to-death horror game mechanics... and it's not a stew either, like a lovely dish with all these mechanics served together. No, it's more like... a buffet of raw ingredients? All are given their own sections; there's a P.T section, there's a Weeping Angels section, there's a The Witness section, weirdly enough... not even the non-horror elements can stop themselves from being horribly derivative. Worst of all is how short they are; you don't even get time to have fun with the stuff they stole! There's a shooter section that'll make you laugh your ass off with how ridiculously lackluster it is; at times it almost feels like the devs are in on the joke.

Only true "horror" section is the loop and mannequin section, aside from that the game is not very scary (except for that one Mita jumpscare at the very end lol.) The music is surreal yet comforting and the different versions of Mita have differing and unique personalities which was interesting to see as the story progressed. Although some parts of the story suffer from mild pacing issues, this doesn't affect the story too much overall. Would recommend for anyone looking for a mildly cute/scary game with interesting story elements. 9/10

review_comment: Miside, what a game this was.. I honestly, genuinely can't find the words to describe this game, it was just.. flawless, amazing, fantastic... there's so much i can say about this game, i could rant about it for days. There's so much you can do in this game, looking around and interacting with the environment, choose your own text, and much more. You're a random guy who has a miserable life, eat, work, sleep repeat. One day, you get a message of a game called Miside, you download it and encounter Mita for the first time, she's a friendly, beautiful character you take care of. You help her with necessities and moving things, as time goes on you grow more addicted to the game. Eventually, Mita wants to meet in person, remember, this is a character inside a game. One day, she asks you to look up, there you are, inside of the game. You're in an outdated version of the game unfortunately, so you can't see Mita, yet.. You haft to find items to put on a teleporting device that'll allow you to get to the latest version of the game, once you reach v1.9, you finally meet Mita. The woman you took care of inside the game for over a month, right there infront of you. She's overjoyed to meet you, while you're left confused and scared of what's going on. Mita will follow you around the house as you explore, she'll cook you a meal along with the help of yours. She gives you a sauce called " Love Sauce " which you took it as a joke, after eating your meal everything starts to static and get glitchy, Mita will give you pills to help with the sudden effects. You're having a good time with Mita, however you're still scared about how everything happened so suddenly. Who knows how long you've been inside the game, you finally sit down and play a console game with her and some cards. This is where everything changes.. You start hearing banging inside the wardrobe, you ignore the sounds at first, but eventually they get loud enough you haft to say something about it. Mita says she doesn't hear anything, her face frowns after you mention the wardrobe, you go to check the sound but she stops you before entering, making excuses of why you can't look in there. Eventually she'll give you an option to look inside, if you accept looking in, well, you just made a fatal mistake.. and a big discovery...

review_comment: Most people would say that this game from a first look seems like something of a gooner game but i assure you its not. I went into miside blind and i would recommend you do the same. As of the time im writing this its been about 3 months or so since the game came out but if you have avoided spoilers then your in for a treat. Between the cute sides of the game like playing with cappie and mila and playing games on the tv and the horror sides of the game which i wont say to much about to avoid spoilers but i will say they often catch you off guard. The game was a few bucks cheaper when it game out and its $15 now but its still worth every penny. There are so many cute little mini games scattered around the game to play that really made me immersed in the world of it. The peaceful parts were so wholesome and made me forget all about the horror aspect until it came back again. The game took me about 6 hours to finish and even then i had to go back and replay to find some hidden stuff i missed the first time so it will definitely keep you occupied and youll often feel bad about leaving the game if like me you look to much into it. Bottom line is this game and the story behind it if you really understand it is amazing and ill definitely play it again if it gets more routes added and as always im Praying for you 🕯️ O Great Mita 💝

review_comment: I highly recommend this game. Although not very long, it is beautifully done, with interesting story, several likable characters with different personalities, well done scenes and packed with details and easter eggs. There are few jumpscares, but they aren't just appearing instantly out of nowhere in front of your face (even though it is quite close to that maybe once) and aren't accompanied by a disgusting, eardrum-tearing sound. Some people might be disappointed by low difficulty, and dangerous encounters with antagonists might be longer, but I can mostly overlook it because of how the feel of the game constantly changes as you progress and it doesn't feel monotonous (well, with exception of those parts where it was intentional). It is amazing what the two developers have done. Since they had to cut some content because of not having enough time, I'm really looking forward when more content will be added (hoping also for more endings). I certainly do not regret buying this nice game at full price.

review_comment: Expected this to be a DDLC clone that I would refund in like an hour, ended up thoroughly enjoying it. I finished the whole game and 100%'ed it in one sitting. The story was well made, the gameplay was generally enjoyable and surprisingly varied. Almost every area had some unique mechanic or minigame in it, which is hard to pull off well, but this game does it. Each segment gets its time in the spotlight but does not overstay its welcome. The areas also looked visually great and varied. I personally really liked the areas that appeared more open. The game had a good mix of horror and chill segments, which are spread out in a good way so that the non-horror segments amplify the horror segments and vice-versa. Very polished as well, I encountered no bugs or lag. Overall, would recommend, and absolutely lives up to the hype. 9/10

One of the first narrative driven games of recent that has kept me entertained the entire time, and one i've actually finished in one night! Just then, he reached the fire storage section and fired the anti-matter weapon. By that time, I realized that nothing mattered anymore, so I let him do as he pleased. James had reached my weapon and started firing bullets at me. However, for him, it was already too late. The bomb exploded on a massive scale, destroying all my efforts, all my colonists, and all my work in just a few seconds. That was it. The game was over, both for me and for James. But then, from the ruins, a voice emerged—it was one of the colonists, crawling and trying to heal themselves. Just then, James stumbled into the scene, stabbed my last remaining colonist with his spear, and slowly retreated from the map, leaving nothing but destruction behind. review_comment: Played RimWorld and got through my first colony, which was fun as hell. The only reason I lost enjoyment after that was because I was playing the game completely wrong, and I realize that now after reading these reviews. The thing I struggled with the most was designing my base and making it look decent, which I wanted to do, but I was obviously trying too hard. When things went wrong (which they did a lot), I would quit the save and load a new one instead of sticking it out. That's when RimWorld felt boring and repetitive after 30 hours of basically doing this, which was a huge waste of a game. Now I realize that RimWorld isn't about watching YouTube videos on "what’s the best way to do this and that," but rather about experimenting for yourself and playing the game how you want to play it, not how people tell you to. So, the next colony, no matter what happens, I'll try to commit until the end like I did with my first colony and see if it changes anything, and I'll play how I see fit.

review_comment: This game... is probably my second favorite game that you could spend a ridiculous amount of time on and not regret it. It's got a surplus of things do to and things you will never get to do with one game, so basically, you can repeat it many times and always have a different experience. I at one point had a dude that sucked at everything but research and animals that tamed a fox, and a wolf attempted to kill said fox, but failed. Then it tried again and one-shot the poor fox. I considered killing the wolf, but for some reason decided to tame it, and with a ONE PERCENT CHANCE of success, the guy tamed the wolf and the wolf later became a very valuable asset, even taking a fatal bullet to the head during the last few hours of my colony's time on the planet to protect the one building the ship to escape. So yeah, the game goes VERY deep into the smallest decisions. I don't like how it can sometimes be tricky to stay on top of the colonists mood, because there are some events that you can't control, like an affair. There is nothing you can do there (besides exile the cheater), so in that way it mimics reality, which I do like. A very thought out game with lots of AI usage and it has a sense of survival to it as well, forcing you to sacrifice luxury over more important things. Also, they have a cool saving system where you can save your game before big events, like a battle, to head back if you made a mistake, or to see what would happen if you did something different, and if you don't like this, you could simply turn it off with the push of a button! Which reminds me, the experience you have playing can be completely changed by what settings you have on, so I highly recommend looking at a tutorial before playing, trust me, its worth it. To finalize, I would recommend this game to anyone who likes strategy games and has some extra time on there hands, because this game can take a while, and also, don't get any mods without thoroughly looking at them. And quick warning, this game has some lovey stuff in it, not visually or anything, but it's there. I hope you find this review helpful and have a great day!

review_comment: If you're willing to put a little time into this game, it's one of the greatest experiences the medium has to offer. It sacrifices a bit of Dwarf Fortress's depth for far more accessibility. But it's not just easier DF, it's so much more than that. The scifi setting offers a unique flavor but allows it to touch on many other genres and themes, the combat is far better than DF allowing you to temporarily take a colonist's autonomy and directly control them like in a real time strategy game, and the smaller amount of colonists makes things feel just a touch more personal. This game succeeds as a colony builder, a story generator, strategy game and immersive sim all in one. An emphatic recommendation from me.

review_comment: At first, when I started playing this game I was vastly overwhelmed the first few hours trying to understand how to set zones, how to properly build housing, mine into the mountains, and overall care for my colony. I took a long break thinking this game wasn't for me possibly, before one of my buddies convinced me to try it again. Now I've binged about 70 hours of game-play over the last week, bought the biotech and ideology DLC which made the experience a bit overwhelming again at first, but quickly made the entire experience even better and more exciting. This game offers so many different scenarios and random events that could happen at anytime, at any random scale depending on the difficulty you choose. Want a colony of crazed psychopath cannibals? Go for it. Want your people to be half-cyborg machine purist? Your choice! Once you figure out the basics to this game, the rest is history as you'll get sucked into the rest of the game.

review_comment: While many games find their ultimate fulfillment upon their completion, RimWorld shines brilliantly with purpose throughout the journey itself. In the 1,000 hours I've played, I only ever "beat" the game twice out of hundreds of runs. It's not that it's even that difficult of a game (though you can certainly set it up in such a way), but that each run is its own story, and some of those stories don't find their end in the credits roll; victory is not the condition for enjoyment. From tragedies to comebacks, slice-of-life to epic odyssey, dramatic thriller to slapstick comedy, there's always more to tell, always more to see. RimWorld grants the wish of an avid reader having reached the end of a great book: A new page at every turn.

Rimworld has no designated stories, nor main character. Because stories and characters are shaped by us, the players. And with each expansion, the devs show that they are actually paying attention to people's feedbacks, as we can see that few expansions are clearly inspired by famous mods. If you want a game where it could generate a new story each time you play, this is the game for you. The only downside is their horrible optimization. Seriously, what kind of game is only capable of using single core in this day and age? I know it'll require to change the very foundation of this game's engine to make it more compatible with modern system, but I really hope the devs find a way to do it someday.

review_comment: I like Rimworld, I really do but one big detail that ultimately stopped me from playing for the most part is the raids. Raids themselves are fine but its the implementation that really gets me, I think Rimworld does it horribly. I could have a rich colony in one save-game, the raiding party size is in some way influenced by the value of stuff in your colony (Idk how the raiders are able to tell how valuable our stuff is but whatever, stupid nonetheless.) meaning that if you get rich enough they'll send dozens of people to raid you, the problem is where they get these people and how. If you look on your global map you would most likely be positioned far from other enemy colonies which is normal. But what isn't normal is having 80 ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ people """supposedly""" travel dozens of km just to raid you, the logistics of that are ridiculous and doing that yourself is insane. What makes it even more ridiculous is that if you were to raid one of your enemies, their outpost is a heap of crap and basically unlivable, I don't know how our enemies are not only able to detect how rich we are, but also supply dozens of raider and on top of that do it with crappy outposts. Completely stupid how only we the player have to conform to the caravan system while dozens of raiders can just teleport to raid us ON A NEAR WEEKLY BASIS according to your difficulty. Another side note, I did a sea ice playthrough and I found it funny how raiders can travel dozens of tiles across the freezing ice but the second they appear on my tile they get frostbite within hours lol, this game is dumb but damn is it fun.

review_comment: Rimworld is classified as a "story generator" and man does it give the potential to tell unlimited stories. A good story is the key element missing from a lot of games I've played lately, and I love that I can make whatever weird colony I want in Rimworld. Want cannibalistic drug lords? Rimworld. Want medieval knights? Rimworld. Want to be a raiding badass that destroys your enemies? Rimworld. Even when you start a run with a specific idea in mind, the game could end up going in a totally different direction than you planned, but in the best way possible. I am generally a cozy gamer that plays life sims and farming sims, but this game could easily appeal to survival horror or just survival game fans in general. review_comment: very good game if you want a new addiction. At first it was hard for me to get into, but not too hard. the interface is forgiving and easy enough to learn within a day, at least for me. after a while of playing, I feel like I developed a bond with my colonists; it's fun watching them get better at things, fall in love with or vilify other people, and become happy with their lives. I think watching your colonists grow from surviving in the wilderness to thriving in a lively community is a really rewarding experience, and I spent countless hours building up communities and trying out different play styles and mods. with mods, there really isn't a limit on how you can play the game. they are near infinite possibilities. DLCs are great, a little expensive but the ones I've bought (royalty and biotech) were very satisfying, creating entirely new ways to play and win the game. all in all, amazing game, very chill until your colonists get absolutely wrecked by a thrumbos or don't survive the winter.

review_comment: One of my favorite games. While Dwarf Fortress will always hold the #1 spot in this genre (and top 10 games of all time), RimWorld isn't just a knockoff, it really does add enough to stand on its own (and in my top 20). It also added graphics and UI tools that DF did not have yet, making it easier to play. I do not mean easy as in not difficult, as the difficulty is definitely brutal at times - I mean easy as in less time spent in tedious setup tasks. The replayability is very high as well. The genre is an excellent mix of high-tech sci fi with low-level survivalism, which too few games really get right, but this nails it. The stories that come out of this game are endless and memorable. I must say I actually don't like the additions to the game, I prefer the original content and balance. I don't know why games feel like they need to keep adding things - this already had more than enough richness to play hundreds of hours.

Building is not hard, and you have the option to speed up time, and disable certain disasters. It's really fun if you enjoy both sandbox games like minecraft where you can change the difficulty at any time. The only 2 pieces of advice i have for fellow new players is dont be afraid to go on quests where you form caravans because even if your people are starving they wont die for another 3 days. review_comment: Great game, even without DLC, there is a vast amount of content and opportunities. You can start with a tribe and progress to the stars from scratch with your characters. Each playthrough is a unique and compelling story, often ending on a bittersweet note. For example, I stayed with my colonists from start to finish, and it was heartbreaking to realize I wouldn't see them again. I've never experienced such emotions in a game—fearing for your colonists when they're attacked, grieving when they die, and feeling joy when they succeed. Mods make the game even more distinctive, introducing a variety of new situations and enhancing immersion. The narrator creates funny and tense moments, making each session both engaging and unpredictable. The atmosphere and music are captivating: calm melodies accompany the early days, and a touching song in the credits helps you accept that you won't see your beloved colonists again.

If you want vampires or dog people or you want to raise babies, get the Biotech pack. If you'd like to build an Empire and become a King, Royalty is the pack for you. The new Anomaly pack adds horror elements to the game to increase the thrill factor but I have, admittedly, not been able to that that one (YET!). This game is one of those ones that is almost entirely unique and no playthrough is ever the same. The devs have been working on this game with devotion for over a decade. review_comment: I have just over 700 hours of playtime, and I've never regretted a single one. The beauty of this game is just how customizable devs allow it to be. You can play against a brutal unforgiving "storyteller", what this game calls the game ai, or nerf it completely in your world settings. You can even do this after starting your colony, so if you find your initial settings too difficult you can lower them until they are more suited to your taste. The DLC is completely unnecessary, easily only counting for only the last 100 hours of playtime. You should really only consider purchasing DLC once you've fully explored the meaty base game as most DLC serves to add new mechanics and play styles, none of it is "necessary" in that sense. Check out mods too, the plethora is vast and plenty are exceptional additions to vanilla.

review_comment: This is probably my favorite game of the last decade. Building a colony from scratch on an alien world, trying to face down hardship after hardship is a really good formula. The updates made to the game over time have been mostly welcome. The modding community is large and active. You can mod the game to experience almost any colony fantasy that you can imagine: build a shogunate village in medieval times, form a space marine chapter from 40K, mine into mountainsides with your dwarf fortress ripoff - whatever you want to experience, it's possible. The game has a lot of different systems that work well together, and the modding community has even added more systems that can be integrated into the game like vehicles and combat overhaul mechanics. Would recommend to someone who enjoys dwarf fortress or other colony sim games, but even if you are more of a general strategy fan, you might enjoy this game.

review_comment: I liked this game quite a bit. My opinion of it evolved over my 66 hours of playtime. At first it was interesting, but then I felt like the combat was a bit clunky and not so fun, but once I allowed myself to start to upgrade my character (duh) it unlocked the gameplay dramatically. I wouldn't say it was an amazing unmissable game, but the story was engaging and the voice acting was pretty good (English) and the gameplay became fairly enjoyable for me once I allowed myself to power up. I did have to use a mod to adjust mouse movement controls (NAIOM) because it was apparently not a great console port - although I ended up using a controller eventually for most of the hacking as it was just better for that part. I also used the "Special K" mod from the start which is apparently highly recommended. I also updated the cutsecenes to 1440p (nexus mods) as the native ones are pretty rough looking compared to the gameplay graphics at 1440p at least. For achievement hunters, there are really no technically missable achievements as everything that is not story based can be "bought" with in game money after the 3rd route of the game, though as I played through this game I realized it deserved better than that from me, so I did it all the official way.

review_comment: I originally only knew the character 2B. Played rainbow six siege and got the Iana elite skin which eventually lead me to learn where 2B was from which is this game right here. WOW, I mean... this game is really something else and such a gem. Of course, I got it because of how much of a baddie 2B is and then I realized holy fu- this game is amazing. I first got the game back in December of 2023 for my PS5 and played for it a little bit. I then figured out there was an anime for the show and watched all of the first season of the anime in like 2-3 days. And just wow, I mean the story is so damn good. Sure, there's action to the story but the emotion... the emotion all around is amazing. The meaning of the game and the music omg! I finally picked up the game again in July of 2024 so about 6-7 months when I learned that the anime was having a season 2. I didn't know there was more to the game at all. I thought that was it. The one play through, I was dead wrong... I watched the anime and then played the game and I finally beat the game on my PS5 last week and just wow. Those other endings are basically another game. A short one but I mean damn. It lead me to getting it on my pc to play through it again. I love this game so much. I've listened to the soundtrack just about every day as write this review. The acting, the game play, the story, the music everything about this game is a masterpiece. PLEASE, if you have not played or watch the anime go do it ASAP. You will not regret it, you may not understand anything at first like I did but give it time and you will fall in love with this game!!!!

review_comment: The story, world and characters are fairly interesting, but the gameplay just isn't good enough for it to be worth it in my opinion. The combat gets very repetitive quickly, and they make some weird choices that just ruin it for me. Healing items don't replenish after death, and are extremely cheap, so if you're struggling to fight a boss or something, you can just go fish for 10-20 minutes and buy a billion repair kits to spam during the fight. Also, many of the bosses are just really boring to fight, and one of them had an unskippable cutscene and a like 2-minute run before you could retry. Additionally, death is very punishing, you have these chips that you use to improve damage and health and stuff, which is a pretty cool system, but when you die all equipped chips drop and if you die again before picking them up, you lose them. These will usually be what you've been grinding for all game, and if you lose them, you obviously won't be able to beat whoever killed you anymore. On top of that, when picking back up your body, you first press a button, then the game pauses to ask what you want to do with the body, then a fairly long animation plays while you can take damage, then it asks you if you want to re-equip all the stuff, which you obviously do, and now you're finally back in the action, which is just really annoying. There are some more weird decision like this, but I won't get into all of them. I'm about 60% through the story, and I'll just be watching like a NieR:Automata all cutscenes full movie youtube video or something to see the rest of it because the gameplay is just not worth it.

review_comment: Nier: Automata does a lot and only seems to suffers for it in a handful of very small ways, the most glaring of which are its many invisible walls. Though you can double jump and mantle your way across the obstacle-riddled environments, there’s little distinction between climbable surfaces and unclimbable barriers even in areas that look like they’re absolutely built to be scaled. Its maps are filled with secretive nooks and crannies which makes the inevitable backtracking more tolerable, but actually accessing those spaces can be deeply frustrating, and the cumbersome 3D world map doesn’t offer much help in that regard. After two dozen hours I still struggled to know where I could and couldn’t go, and finding the correct path up or down occasionally involved the equivalent of beating my head against a wall until one of the two finally gave.

The credit scene mini-game was so drawn out that it almost put me to sleep. It really seems egotistical if anything, because clearly it wasn't designed with entertainment in mind. Also, DID ANYONE PLAYTEST THE BOSS FIGHT THAT SWITCHES BETWEEN A2 AND 9S? Not only is it annoying that the character you control switches at random intervals, but every time you switch to the AI controlled character they are right up under the boss, making it a coin flip if you are about to take a lot of unavoidable damage. I can't believe I wasted 80 hours of my life for such an underwhelming ending. A good example of replay-ability with multiple endings is Elden Ring. There it is completely option to try new endings to get the full story, but if you do you are rewarded with plenty of new content like hidden regions and bosses and weapons. review_comment: Nier Automata - Masterpiece my eye. Early in the game, there was a spot on the map I was supposed to get to and fight enemies that drop a quest item, the item didn't drop. I had to go online and find out other people had the same problem. I had to save the game and reload to get the enemies to respawn so I could kill them again to get them to drop the quest item. Being new to the game, I figured I was just doing something wrong, but it was something wrong with the game. Combat is boring and is mostly running away from robots while shooting them with unlimited ammo. The "futuristic" robots looked like their design was inspired by the Jetsons. The soundtrack is overblown and pretentious. In some parts of the game you're in a flight suit shooting at things and I felt like I was being forced to play Galaga in 2024. Twenty hours in, and I have no idea what a "nier" or an "automata" are. The main characters wear blindfolds but can apparently still see? Maybe they're see through? Maybe they act like super cool futuristic sunglasses? No clue. I don't know why this game is on so many best of lists. I've read you have to play through something like four or five times to get the full story though multiple endings, but I wasted my time playing through it once, I'm not doing it again.

review_comment: Game starts with a 6-7 minute top down bullet hell with lots of moments where control is taken away from you for miniature in-game cutscenes, most of which had dialog. There are 4 difficulties for this game, easy, normal, hard and very hard. I chose hard because I was feeling confident and I have played platinum games before. I got past the bullet hell section on my first try, and then I was in the regular 3D combat. I died because I mistook the attack button for a different button on my control. And guess what, I had to do the bullet hell section again. There is absolutely no autosave in this game and the game just tells you that you will be shown how to autosave later on. Okay great, so I do that bullet hell section a bunch of times and continue to die. I die another time because I mistook the attack button again. Keep in mind, you die in around two-three hits on hard mode. And I died 2-3 times on the bullet hell section, because of those mini cutscenes where control is taken away(the camera angle was changing) but if their are bullets still on screen, you can STILL get hit! How stupid is that! I then put the game on normal and start doing the regular 3D fighting with 2B after having passed the bullet hell section once again. Throughout the level, the camera constantly moves obnoxiously to bird's eye view and other awkward angles. It's incredibly annoying and in my opinion breaks the flow of the gameplay, especially for a combat oriented game like this. And a boss then shows that up that is a giant claw with two attacks and it covers the whole arena. You are barely taught the controls; I had no clue how to avoid one of its attacks. And then finally, as I was approaching what seemed to be the end of the level, guess what. A boss appeared! You know what the boss was? Not one but TWO of the dumb claws which I fought earlier! I struggled to dodge their arena covering attacks and died and got sent right back to the bullet hell section. I probably spent about 30 mins on that singular run only to get sent back to the beginning. Funny enough, when you press pause, you see a quick save button but you can't press it! This game has some of the most ludicrous game design I have ever seen. I can't wait to get my money back.

In the first tutorial mission, you have to go nearly 70 minutes without dying to be able to SAVE. I died at the Goliath fight because of poor level design, and just getting so bored during the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fight to actually try. The boss has two moves both of which are just run away the whole time, wait for the boss to very obviously have an opening, and attack for 10 seconds dealing 1/50th of its health. When I eventually died (It took a while because of how tedious and long the fight was) The game sends you back to the very beginning of the game because you didn't make it the 70 minutes. You have to go through all of the boring ass combat again and this time you don't even get to see any new story to keep it mildly interesting. I understand why people like this game, but if you are like me and have fun getting challenged by games without needing to use the "very hard" difficulty, which in this game removes the ability to lock on to opponents and makes you die no matter what on every hit, or you are looking for a game with in depth combat and rewarding gameplay, like souls combat, this game is not for you.

Story, characters, playability, the different routes and endings, little secrets tying the lores and universes for those with a more exploratory disposition, it's all stellar. I have very little to complain about and it's all superficial anyway. Hard difficulty pushes you to make the most out of most game mechanics and is perfectly balanced if you'd like to go beyond casual without undue frustration. The difficulty setting does not preclude anyone from experiencing any of the game content, though, so your mind will also be blown if you go for normal. I am fully onboard the Nier and Drakengard / alternative media lore hype! Thanks Yoko Taro, you beautiful Emil-headed freak!

review_comment: As someone who loves the entire world of the franchise you need to start with Nier Replicant to "fully" appreciate both games. I have 100% both games on xbox and about to do both on steam. NieR Replicant's story is one of the best ever written and has one of the best end games of all time. The last hour and a half to two hours is an emotional payout of everything you've done and people you've met with countless boss fights, betrayal, and two plot twists. I was there day 1 of NieR Automata's release after playing the original NieR. While Automata is in a different weight class with it's story, I still felt it falls short compared to the original; especially with the plot twists having less of an effect on the player; except maybe 1 of them near the end. It's a great game for what it is, but hopping in with Automata is just the lesser of two great stories as well as taking place after NieR giving some major things away. There are 3 characters in Automata that make reappearances and just by seeing them you spoil the fates of those characters and spoil 1 of the plot twists from Nier Replicant. The only thing I'd truly give to Automata doing better would be combat, even with my own personal bias to Replicant's combat, the community agrees that Automata's is better. PLAY BOTH if you're getting into the franchise but please start NieR Replicant first. I would say start with Drakengard but the games are old and haven't gotten a remake yet. (Drakengard 3 leads to Drakengard 1. Drakengard 1 leads to Drakengard 2 or NieR Replicant based on which ending. NieR Replicant leads to NieR Automata.)

review_comment: I didn't expect 90's shmups with narration (never happened in the 90's), Smash TV, Strider PC, and Bayonetta the space opera (if there were a space opera version of Bayonetta) rolled up into one coherent, integrated thing. I wasn't sure what to expect, and kind of pre-imagined a disappointingly slow, bookish RPG with some action. I was prepared for disappointment. I bought it on the pretense that at the very least the online videos didn't have chunky bad 90's Playstation 1 textures or 720P clunker graphics that deserve a car backfiring sound effect in the laugh track. Retro 480P with scanlines is still beautiful pixel art, like Greek mosaics or something. Remembering my experience from the deceptive marketing of Vermillion, I assumed that they showed the best parts, which comprised 1% of the entire jalopy. On the contrary, this is top fuel. The graphics are a quantum leap above the disaster it might have been. It's an excellent choice for those on the fence. For the one who compared it to an MMORPG, ...that is a strange comparison, like calling an orange a hamburger. This is superb stuff so far, just like it was printed in reviews of ancient yore.
