review_comment: The 30 hours I spent with this game had me feeling empty at the end. Ending E was one that had me feel hopeful, in the sense that I could look at this again, and say, that $30 was most definitely worth it. I rarely ever finish games, because story is weak, or gameplay doesn't keep me engaged. And yet, this game did both. The choices I made all had weight to them, and each affected the world in some kind of way. Whether it be allowing Pascal to escape from A2, or leaving him to suffer the unexpected consequences of his teachings. The music is amazing, and there's not a single track I dislike. I can easily recommend this game for anyone who is in a slump in terms of creativity, entertainment or anything, because by the end of the game, you'll be able to push through it some more. In the end, i deleted my save, to save others, like the few who did the same for me. But, I will never play this game ever again, because I don't want to ruin the game for me in future.

review_comment: The game’s standout strength is its narrative, which explores existential questions about consciousness, free will, and the nature of existence, often leaving players with a sense of introspection. The gameplay is exhilarating, featuring fluid, combo-heavy combat with a mix of genres, from action to top-down shooter and even bullet-hell segments. The world design is beautifully bleak, with a haunting atmosphere that perfectly complements the game’s story, while the soundtrack, composed by Keiichi Okabe, elevates every emotional moment. However, the game is not without its drawbacks—its repetitive structure, especially across multiple playthroughs, can feel tiresome for some, as the core gameplay loop doesn’t vary enough between routes. The pacing is sometimes uneven, and while the story is compelling, certain characters lack deeper development. Additionally, technical issues, particularly on PC, can detract from the overall experience. Despite these flaws, Nier: Automata is a unique and thought-provoking title, one that’s likely to stay with you long after you’ve finished it, thanks to its philosophical depth and unforgettable emotional moments.

review_comment: After getting all the 5 main endings and even the Nier outfits, I think I can now properly review this game. It's a MASTERPIECE. There are no bad characters in this game. All of them have deep backstories. I especially like Pascal. He's so like-able, you'll want to protect him and and the whole village. The combat is simple, straightforward, and so fun. The performance is quite smooth, mind you, I'm playing it on a laptop with integrated graphics, and it's very playable. The open-world is not too big, not too small. It's just right for the story and gameplay they are presenting. The waifus, 2B and A2, so bad-ass, so pretty, so smexy, I love them. This game has all of the things I want in a videogame, great story, great gameplay, plays well on a relatively low-end device, great characters, hot waifus. Gonna 100% this game and then play Nier Replicant next.

review_comment: This game is an absolute masterpiece, on the surface it looks like any other JRPG that can be dismissed as Yoko Taro telling all of us the type of women he's into (Which I'll be honest might have some truth to it.). But this game is a rabbit hole, right when you think the game ends, it just gets deeper, each time your jaw drops with what is really going on. This game loves to keep you on your toes, changing over and over again, the last 30 minutes of gameplay is different from the next 30 minutes (In main quest) I really really admire this game for breaking industry norms, not only does the designers break it, but they mold it, and break it again. They test the limits of their given genre, which is what game developers should be doing. Everything in this game is carefully put together, the story, the music, the relationships, everything. This is modern day art piece, and you are the viewer. With the end, this game does not fail to make me stare point blank thinking what the hell I just played as the credits roll. The music in this game is outrageously good for no reason, there's a few points in the game where I just think to myself "Did they make this scene around the music or the music around the game??" I am actually shocked they don't sell the album on steam. There are some cringe JRPG elements in this game at some points, However the good outweighs the bad a thousand fold. I cannot recommend this game enough. What we have here is a gem of a game, and you should play it. TaTa and Fair well.
name: NieRAutomata

review_comment: Really glad I finally got around to completing Nier Automata. This game is incredible from both a gameplay and story direction perspective. The dynamic camera and alternating combat styles kept the game fresh even when fighting and traversal got tedious at times. Although I was apprehensive about having to do 3 playthroughs to unlock the true ending, the payoff was immensely satisfying even as someone who already knew significant story spoilers. Each route should be faster than the last. One caveat that I need to mention is that skipping repeated combat sections or not doing side quests will leave you severely underleveled for the subsequent routes. So unlike me, take your time and help these NPCs out as Himmel the Hero would. That aside, it would be a cardinal sin to not mention the music in this game. As someone who treats most music like beeps and boops, Nier has a truly special OST that is not only memorable but incredibly immersive. If you are on the fence because you have already been spoiled, gave up in the first two routes, or only know of Nier via 2B's butt, all I can say is trust in Yoko Taro to deliver you a masterpiece.

review_comment: Very unique and original game, especially the ingenious way it utilizes the video game medium to tell its story and highlight its themes. That story and those themes are deep and interesting and philosophical but also emotionally sad and tragic. The game's director, Yoko Taro, developed the story and the writing and its quite sharp and poignant, and its emotional points are often driven home through brilliant incorporation of the gameplay. The combat is fairly easy but fun and also has some depth for those that want it. The animations are excellent and elegant and beautiful. All of this pairs perfectly with the soundtrack which is one of the best video game soundtracks out there. This game is truly a work of art and should be experienced by every gamer at some point in their gaming life but beware -- it may lead to unexpected introspection and melancholy!

Most of the side quests are worth doing (a few of them are fetch quests but rest of them really help with the world building). The pacing of the story is also really good. Overall, highly recommend playing this at least for the first 30 hours to fully appreciate the uniqueness.

review_comment: So after 130 hours I can honestly say the only reason I have played this game this much is because of the IP, if this was a stand alone game that had nothing to do with Warhammer 40K it would have been a dead game after the first month, maybe less. The PVE is ok, and has some replayability (thats its only redeeming quality) The absolute lack of content from day one, and the absolute lack of content being added is insane. There is next to no customization unless you like Ultra Marines, or Ultra Marines cosplaying as a different chapter. The customization for Heretics is non-existant, and laughable. The game has a heavy story beat about Death Watch, and you can't even make lore accurate Deathwatch because you cant put chapter symbols on the opposite pauldron (just ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ invert the symbol that is already in the game and let us put it on the opposite shoulder) the PVP is hot garbage, and was a tacked on afterthought with little to no work put into it, it is full of crazy unbalanced stuff. Also the lack of weapons is ridiculous, and then half the cool weapons are locked behind high levels that will take you literal months of non stop playing to get to. I have played the PVP A LOT and have more wins than losses, but am still weeks away from unlocking weapons I've wanted to use since the game was released.IT TAKES WAY TOO LONG TO LEVEL IN PVP! Oh they did just add a new Dark Angel skin though, but you can not customize it in anyway, and is locked to a single class. If thats the way the new content is going to be there should be one new Chapter hero/Skin every month at the absolute least. Or you know put more than 5hrs of content in a game before you release it.

review_comment: I do find it rather strange how unwelcoming the game is of newcomers. It doesn't go out of its way to ever explain any role, word or lore-based concept. And while one could argue that it is a game for fans, thinking that a Triple-A publisher would ever make a game of this size and not want to attract newcomers is downright naive. If you're not already a fan you'll either be real confused about a lot of what they're talking about, or you'll be spending half your playtime on the wiki. Overall it's a decent hack-and-slash-shooter that won't ever impress any non-Warhammer fan or person who enjoys a greater diversity of gameplay; it's all corridors and button-presses and horde-styled defence finales. But on the flip-side, it seems to be a delight for Warhammer fans; a crunchy, blood-soaked romp through a world of stainless steel and great, towering cathedrals, filled with horrid tech bonded with flesh, robot-skulls, and weapons galore, all of it in the Glorious name of the Emperor!

review_comment: If you played this game earlier, it was a ton of fun. You felt like a Space Marine, you did a ton of damage, you'd be able to blast through hordes of enemies in satisfying fashion. With each big update, the developers INSIST on catering to their top 0.01% of hardcore players who whine and complain about difficulty. If you cater to the top % of players, you alienate everyone else. How is nerfing classes and weapons a solution to ANY problem? Let's not forget to busted enemy spawns, often dropping spores on your forehead from almost nowhere or a tight corner. The game started off strong, has a beautiful and testosterone-pumping story, and leaves you on a sour note with each and every horrible update. I've committed to just dropping the game entirely because there's no joy in getting weaker with each update, it only takes away from the feeling of being an all-powerful Space Marine. Great game, horrible devs. Cosmetics are handled in a similarly horrible fashion, but I'll let other commenters rant about that.

review_comment: Is this game perfect? Not by a long shot but I find myself talking about this game in my discord with my friends like it has spiritually shook me. More specifically, I find myself marveling at the enemy AI protocol. Simply put, the enemy AI design is an astonishing accomplishment. This game possesses quite possibly the absolute best demonstration of enemy AI I have ever encountered in my brief existence on this planet. I cannot commend the developer enough about the subtle nuances of the AI and its ability to adapt to you or the player population. Of course it has all the given attributes of modern AI, it is omniscient, it has ESP, it undoubtedly reads inputs, it can compute complex data quick enough to change the move set employed or the targeting priority BUT it is executed in such a refined and subdued manner. It makes for a great teacher, which I would think would be the ideal enemy AI concept. You will fail a good bit HOWEVER it never felt unbeatable. For me, it never once felt insurmountable. NOT ONCE. The only thing I felt was the unyielding motivation to log in day after day in my endeavor to master the combat system and beat that wretched AI. The AI in this game, is beautiful. Something truly remarkable has happened here and I cannot recommend this game enough if you like a challenging game, with an incredibly rewarding and satisfying combat system.

review_comment: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 is a terrific third-person shooter with a compelling story, loads of weapons that are a blast to use, and a healthy variety of enemies to use them on. It once again borrows many of its ideas from the Gears of War series, but they’re good ideas, and Space Marine 2 does a fine job of making them its own. And while the Operations PvE mode that accompanies it doesn’t currently offer enough to keep me coming back, the deep customization options for your Space Marine do look promising if it’s supported in post-launch updates as planned. Besides, when you’re eviscerating aliens on planets as pretty as these, it’s hard not to leave satisfied.

review_comment: Great story and the multiplayer is fun and challenging! Haven't tried PVP but from what i can tell the ttk is in a nice spot and can add some more life to the game. If the Devs can keep a steady stream of content then i can see this game doing really well. If not, for those who seek a more PVE style of game play, they might burn out pretty quick due to the repetitious nature of the multiplayer operations, even though the enemies are procedural (kinda), the mission objectives can get a little stale. However, the progression system and different classes help for those who seek to grind like i do, i can see myself easily putting 100+ hours chasing those levels and gear. Lastly, the campaign took me about 8 hours on normal and that's with exploring every nook for hidden data pads on normal but by the end you'll be shouting "FOR THE EMPEROR!"

review_comment: Space Marine 2 could be a fantastic game, but right now, it's hampered by significant server issues, constant disconnects, frustrating loading times and a multiplayer experience riddled with basic mistakes I'm sure were resolved in the 90s, yet they still persist here. Trying to play with friends is a buggy nightmare and has become such an issue that we are now looking elsewhere for our online enjoyment. This is not the first time I've had disappointing experiences with Focus Entertainment's online offerings (Aliens: Fireteam Elite & Hood: Outlaws & Legends) that also suffered from poor online performance, connectivity and multiplayer issues and it is frustrating to see these same problems cropping up again, and I really hope they take the time to really address these issues for Space Marine 2 - there's a lot of potential here, but it needs to be fixed to provide the kind of experience fans deserve.

review_comment: It's a pretty game but poorly designed. I would go as far as saying incompetently designed. You're a Space Marine with tissue-paper armour who can be killed by a swarm of Hormagaunts. And this will happen frequently due to poor controls and horrible game play systems. You’ll die, but not because of a lack of skill or a failure to ‘git good; you’ll get killed because your marine cannot do anything when surrounded. When he swings, he steps forward, deeper into the swarm. You cannot control your movement leading to frustrating tactical compromises. You can AOE, but it requires at least one swing first, so the melee mechanics are designed to get you killed. There is little to no control over your character. You just get pummelled over and over again, especially if you’re like me and play on the harder difficulties. The whole power fantasy thing is gone. You feel more powerful being a guardsman in Dark Tide than you do playing a Space Marine in this game. It would be okay if there was a game mechanic that could be mastered to get you out of such situations, but there isn’t. All you can do is reload the game and use your new magical foresight to know a horde is coming, and try to thin it out at range. Even that is horribly implemented. You can’t just switch weapons. You have a button for melee, another button for range and another button for aiming. So, you can’t just switch to a Bolter and press Mouse1 to fire and then switch to a chainsword and press Mouse1 to swing because that would make too much sense in this horrible game. No, you have to bind each function to a different key, as though context was a concept far too complicated for the devs. This makes for many awkward combat encounters where you aim your Bolter and then, rather than firing the weapon, you instead accidentally swing your sword. Even the finishers are repetitive and lacklustre, becoming events that, you guessed it, take away your control so you can be surrounded and finished-off by Hormagaunts. It is also a horribly linear game with an absolutely brain-dead story. The linearity is particularly off-putting because your character makes really dumb decisions all the time, as do the other characters. I have absolutely no idea how this game is popular. Seriously, it’s a linear grind with horribly designed combat and a story which makes me feel like I've lost braincells. I’d urinate on this game if I didn’t think that would be an insult to the comparative dignity of uric acid.

review_comment: Really good game. I don't understand certain choices about the design-- I don't think the demographics of the Ultramar system have been represented in quite this way before and they throw dead ultramarines on the maps like confetti-- but I think that it's a solid release and certainly the best aesthetic representation of the setting in a game that we've had, on a par with or somewhat better than darktide. My two big issues are that I think Tzeentch should've been nerfed differently (fewer shield gors and possibly a rubric that prioritizes melee instead of cratering spawn rates) and that I think they added too many buffs to melee at once. People think that every game like this is too difficult at launch, and I remember the VT2 debates over whether it was POSSIBLE to clear the game on legend solo. While some nerfs and buffs were warranted, a few struck me as too hasty. Nevertheless, this is an excellent game and I look forward to seeing where it goes.

review_comment: Normally I'd recommend this game but there's a seriously glaring issue. In the first game, you'd regain healthy by playing aggressively and performing executions. However, now executions only recover armour, which is functionally useless. It can also recover contested health, which depletes far too quickly for you to actually recover any meaningful amount of health. This leads you to rely on the medicae stims scattered around the map, which are rare and inconsistent enough that you are prohibited from aggressive gameplay. Before, aggression was your only way to make it out of a sticky situation, now aggressive and fun gameplay will only get you killed in frustrating ways. It's a shame that they made such poor decisions because I wish I could enjoy the PvE of this game. The only consistently fun aspect of this game is the PvP, which I hightly recommend. I really wish I could recommend this game.

review_comment: The story wants to be good, but the AI leaves a lot to be desired. The main campaign is rather short with only 5 or 6 missions total, with the rest of the story being filled in with about 9 "Ops" missions that take place simultaneously with the main story. The main campaign allows you to try out various weapons and gear as the story directs which in turn allows you to make semi-informed decisions about how you want to equip each class of avatar for the Ops. Problem is, someone didn't seam to understand how to describe the difficulty settings, and as a result "Minimal" (easy mode) feels like Halo 3's "Heroic" difficulty from 2007. Unless you find a Guardian Relic, you can only go down twice before you fail the mission. Playing with friends must be the main way to play, but if friends aren't available you can either go online with randos or play solo and have the AI fill in the other two spots of the party. Even on Minimal difficulty, being swarmed is extremely easy, which leads to excessive stunlocking that will quickly consume your two "lives", and the AI "allies" apparently focus more on their own survival rather than taking out the various enemies, forcing you to do every bit of heavy lifting. I don't have a desired to be carried, but likewise I don't want to feel like all I'm doing are escort missions. If I'm facing down a flying boss called a Neurothrope and I run out of ammo for both my primary and secondary weapons, no grenades either, and no area nearby to restock, it just becomes a waste of time watching the AI allies just standing around the boss as it slowly kills them, they not attacking either. It feels like this game may be the Dark Souls version of a Third-Person Shooter, which if I'd known that before, I wouldn't have bought it.
name: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2

review_comment: Я люблю вселенную Warhammer 40,000, и эта игра — прекрасная возможность для людей, которые не слышали о ней, познакомиться с оной. Из плюсов могу выделить отличную графику, добивание врагов (это всегда круто), неплохую оптимизацию, а также могу отметить кастомизацию, кооперативный режим и PvE, который прекрасно дополняет кампанию. Что касается PvP-режима, то он может нравиться или не нравиться, и ты поймешь это только когда попробуешь его. Из минусов могу отметить довольно односторонний геймплей: не всем может понравиться отбиваться от толп врагов несколько часов подряд. И хоть небольшое разнообразие врагов, боссы разбавляют игровой процесс, я не мог не отметить этого. В целом игру к ознакомлению рекомендую, она подарит вам эмоции, и вы точно найдете в ней то, что скрасит ваше времяпрепровождение.

Fans of the Warhammer 40k series will appreciate the attention to lore and the intense action, while new players will find plenty to love in the accessible gameplay and relentless fun. This is the only game that I have to sit for a minimum of 20 minutes after selecting an operation just so I can have actual players as teammates instead of bots, and even if I managed to have someone on my team, either they have the same role as me or they just leave as soon as they were in the game. The weapons are also ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, especially melee weapons(a purple-tier power sword can't kill a normal tyranid add in 3 heavy slashes on the easiest mode). I'm not sure if Saber's pea-sized brain can realize this but SM2 is mostly PVE content right? Then what is the point of making weapons in this game like a joke? If you want players to be challenged then make the adds harder as the modes become harder, not making the adds harder while also weakening the weapons! Adding onto the fact that the servers and matchmaking system is just in the gutter, classes that need to coordinate with other classes such as Assault and Bulwark are just a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ joke! The core of the game is good, it's just that the devs decided that SM2 players are not allowed to enjoy themselves and that they can ♥♥♥♥ on the players as much as they want because they are the devs. Oh, did I mention the fact that they released future content and then later on say that they won't be out until December? Wanna guess why? Because that stuff actually takes time and effort to put in, but making players' experiences like ♥♥♥♥ by changing weapons and enemy stats don't. review_comment: I am a huge warhammer fan and I have nothing but good things to say about this games combat, story, graphics, cosmetics, lore, attention to detail, etc. However I cannot recommend this game in its current state. I am a full time university student with a job, so unfortunately I dont get to play for too long each day. I would be satisfied since the gameplay loop is addicting but the games servers and constant disconnections and crashes with no way to get back into your game or get any rewards is insanely frustrating. I have been disconnected from the final stage of an operation countless times and have just tried to move on. it happens. This however happens far too often to even call this a finished game. None of the hotfixes have helped anything. this problem also occurs in pvp. I have lost so much time. When you only have time for 3 or 4 operations a day and only recieve rewards half the time, there is a big problem. i have never encountered servers this bad in any game I have played, extremely disappointing. This is the first game I have ever felt the need to leave a review on, since I could no longer put up with this. for context I have a very good and stable internet connection, normally have sub 20ms latency and very low ping on any game. I have a modern pc with a 4070 super and a ryzen 7600x, my drivers are fully updated. This needs to be fixed before anyhting else is even added.

review_comment: The campaign story is a noticeable improvement on SM1, if perhaps still fairly simplistic; it reuses the same exact artifact from the first game as its McGuffin. It pits you against a Tyranid hive fleet and the Thousand Sons traitor legion as well as the arrogance and obstinance of the Adeptus Mechancus across three planets (a jungle world, a hive world and a burial world). The PvE missions are partly woven into the narrative as the adventures of squads Lieutenant Titus dispatches to attack additional objectives his own half-squad can't cover - at one point in the plot, a Campaign mission is simultaneous with Operations; there are only a few missions, however, and the devs are slowly adding more as free updates. The campaign is serviceable, with later missions playing off strongly on pathos and fanservice and macho chest-beating... which is what you sign up for in an Astartes-centered 40k game, wasn't it? A significant addition is a character arc centered around a simple narrative of trust vs caginess in a pressing situation, creating drama within Titus's squad stemming from his own unwillingness to share about his past - it's about as much as you can do with the single-minded superhuman warriors anyway, but it builds off the plot of SM1, it's a lot, lot more than there was in that game... and it's bloody satisfying.
name: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2

review_comment: I have found a fix for my serious crash issues, and can now recommend the game although I do that with a heaped spoon of caution. After the last update they included wide screen support, cool! However it was that support that was hard crashing my computer and by crashing I mean every five to ten minutes. My fix was to go the settings and change the resolution from 3400x1440 to 2560x1400 and then back again. After that the game hasn't crashed since. Hopefully this helps someone else out there. I am still have mixed feeling on recommending the game. I really enjoy this game a lot, but these kinds of technical issues are not really good enough.

review_comment: After more than 100 hours, I can say that this game is amazing.........if you can play it. There are currently a number of game breaking bugs that prevent playing the PvE Operations mode (I'm not really interested in PvP) and the Ultrawide support is an absolute joke. It's only been out for a little while now so bugs are to be expected, however when they're trying to fine tune weapon and enemy balancing, and add additional content without even so much as acknowledging the game breaking technical issues, it's a no from me. Technical issues should always be priority over additional content in the first month or two after launch. Maybe in 6 months. *Update* The game breaking bugs and network issues seem to have been fixed, so I'd recommend this game if you're on a 16:9 or 21:9 monitor only. Any aspect ratio above that isn't really supported unless you want to play Windowed.

review_comment: If you're a fan of action/shooter games from the early 2000's, especially Gears of War, you'll love this game. Combat is gritty and gory. Graphics and art design are top notch with some of the best backdrops I've seen in gaming. There's an epic campaign, operations missions which are weaved into the story, and a PvP multiplayer that is pretty basic but a lot of fun. The campaign is a bit short compared to other modern games and the PvP does not have a lot of variety, but it still feels like a full package. Overall, an awesome time that's made even better if you can drop in with a couple friends.
name: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2

review_comment: This game has amazing graphics and take you back to a simpler time, like back in the early 2010s or late 2000s, when games were simply just better and more focused on combat and story. I think the PvP is a little rough around the edges, but the PvE is amazing. Ignore all comparisons to Helldivers 2(another great game); this game is nothing like it and has its own amazing and unique charm. The combat is so satisfying. Only issue would be replayability, but tbh that is not an issue until you hit like 30-40 hours. Each level is hand crafted which is why it may get repetative playing it over and over again, but there are a lot of levels with different difficulties(meaning different boss fights) and so many different classes to level up. Also, there is a PvP as I mentioned, which I think needs improvement but is on a good track. The devs also released a lot of plans and roadmaps which looks promising. Overall, maybe you won't be playing this game continuously for like months on end, but definitely for weeks on end every now and then. And you know what? That's okay! Some games are not huge time sinks but masterpieces at the same time; this game is a great example. GOTY contender imho. 8.5/10(-1.5 purely for the PvP).
name: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2

review_comment: Campaign is absolute kino, especially if you're a fan of Space Marine 1. Six long missions. Co-op has potential. PvE balance is a bit iffy, largely because it's a nasty war of attrition where hp is easily whittled down with very few ways of getting it back (unlike the hp-restoring executions from SM1), and many enemies require a weirdly large amount of bolter rounds to down vs. what I'd expect. Game DESPERATELY needs better sound mixing and larger field of view since it's very difficult to perceive enemies (or even damage being actively taken) that aren't right in front of you, same as how enemies could silently approach you from behind and backstab you without an audio cue when Vermintide 2 launched. Sometimes inputs feel weirdly dropped. I appreciate how there are many customization options earnable, and how the DLC cosmetics don't feel shoved down my throat like other games. I hope they add a way to sync or copy color schemes between classes though, since right now you would have to manually recreate them across up to 12 different characters (6 PvE + 6 loyalist PvP).

review_comment: Gonna go ahead and get this out of the way, if you prefer modern high speed games with all the sliding and crazy movement this game is not for you. With that out of the way, this game is everything I've sincerely missed from that era of games from roughly 06-2012. No crazy movement no high speed mess, this game is pure old fashioned new game fun. its brutal, gets the blood and adrenaline flowing like crazy. Campaign is fantastic (played on Angel Of Death for best experience) the cinematics are top notch, and the co-op operations tie into the story and are loads of fun to play time and time again with more being added over at least the next two years. there's not an ounce of pay to win, the season pass is purely cosmetics, everything else in updates will be completely free. PVP is a little limited at the moment, also more to be implemented down the road, but also still very fun if you miss those slower paced yet extremely engaging games from the years mentioned above (Gears of War players you know who you are). Even if you don't get it now, i highly recommend when it goes on sale that you do, and if you love it after picking it up on a sale show these devs a little love and grab the season pass to help keep the games lifespan going. I believe the experience is currently well worth the price tag.

review_comment: Space Marine 2 reaches for a lot of things and it's still an incredibly fun and unique experience, but not everyone is going to love the confusing combat at first and I still can't fathom people saying SM1's cover shooting was somehow balanced better. The grind is atrocious for how cool the missions are to go through for your first times and for how fun the classes feel at high level. PvP is similar to the old days where it felt kinda tacked on. Other than that, I can at the very least say its a hell of a game even with so many rough eurojank edges. It's refreshing to have a game that doesn't just tell me to keep coming back daily and if you're sick of the co op, you can just say you're sick of the co op.

review_comment: Dude, beside playing all sorts of other Warhammer 40,000 games, this by far is my favorite. I am excited to see what develops from this game. review_comment: Where do i even start. The gameplay, top tier, the story (with a small amount of lore knowledge and/or playing the first game) top tier, the graphics are top tier as well. This game managed to do what most games today fail at, just making a good game without all the unnecessary ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. currently all currency and cosmetics you can earn in game, with the exception of twitch drops and game editions. this game is everything youd want in a sequel, and almost none of what you dont, truly a modern AAA game. All of the reviews saying that theres no ultrawide support must not have been following the development or even looking at the roadmap of the game, considering they mention directly that, as well as mentioning having to have epic games, who in 2024 does not have it already installed on their computer. The devs have actively made improvements so far to the stability and performance of the game, and are actively working to improve it further. This is by far the best warhammer 40,000 game to date if not currently available. They have laid out a clear roadmap for the future of the game as well as future cosmetics and features. This is the most fun ive had in a coop game since the launch of helldivers before they took the completely wrong direction. Give it a shot, especially if you have a couple buddies, the ai in the campaign is kind of bad, but its not meant to be played that way, and all of the reviews mentioning how bad it is know that. Try it for yourself, and form your own opinion, in my opinion its extremely worth it, and in plus what game in 2024 stays true to the original source material i was very surprised when this one did, all the way to the end. Honestly even if it doesnt win it, this is my game of the year for 2024.

review_comment: This is a game that makes me feel like I'm back in the golden era of Xbox 360. 40K has always been an amazing universe that's wowed me for just being over the top in all the craziest ways. This game has a story that you can play through that isn't complicated, and that's a good thing. You don't know much about Titus, because he's a space marine. They don't really have feelings, so this doesn't feel like a boring AAA game that uses a stupid amount a character development to make up for the fact that it has a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ story. It's just a man, that serves a god emperor, killing chaos, that defy said Emperor. The game play is great too, nothing revolutionary, but that's what makes it great. They took the basics and made it very satisfying. I think this is my first review for a game, and gladly. I haven't felt fun like this in a game for a long time, and I really hope they keep their words, and follow this road map. I'd hate to see it fall like HellDivers did.

review_comment: Space Marine 2 expands on the gameplay of it's predecessor in terms of new weaponry, new coop side missions and a really good story. As an avid Warhammer 40,000 fan, I was quite enthralled by the scope of the battlefield as if I was immerged into it. You participate in the defense of an Imperial system against the Tyranid swarm, which is in-game is as faithful as its horrific interpretation in the Tyranid codex of the tabletop game. I was enthralled by the murmuration of the Tyranid Gargoyles, swarms of gaunts and reapers. The diversity in ennemies reveals new challenges at each mission and the boss fights so far are satisfying. I highly recommend this game to any Warhammer 40,000 fan.

review_comment: So i was really excited for space marine 2, I've played the first and its a classic among warhammer fans however space marine 2 has been nothing but buggy upon release. In a campaign that is designed to be played with friends, there are so many bugs that make it impossible. firstly when we assembled the squad it all seemed fin until we got the infinite loading servers bug. OK we thought that it would be an easy fix, just turn off steam overlay and some other stuff and it will work. and it did... the first time. After that we got to actually play, it was about 20 mins of fun until we got soft locked at the flower wall on the first mission. A quick reload to last checkpoint and we were good.... for all about 10 mins when we got soft locked again at the airlock entrance of the bunker. this time loading the checkpoint didnt work so we decided to start the mission over again. that was until we got the infinite loading bug again... At its current state space marines 2 is an unplayable buggy mess for us, id imagine playing single player might work but the campaign is clearly designed for multiplayer and that just isn't working for us.

review_comment: My specs are better than the minimum requirements, yet I am plagued with severe visual problems. The main issue is Titus, enemies, items, and interactable terrain are invisible, occasionally becoming visible for short periods of time upon changing settings. Most textures and objects are never fully loaded. Before adjusting my settings, cutscenes wouldn't work at all and the game would regularly freeze. After all of my setting adjustments, the game has reached a point where the environments, framerate, and resolution are at a satisfying point, but invisible models still persist. Loading screens, broken cutscenes, freezes, crashes, and setting tinkering have taken up all of my playtime, and I am no longer eligible for refund. I just hope that the invisible models are patched, because I was so excited for this game, and that's really the one essential fix.

review_comment: On the gameplay front, Space Marine 2 strikes a near-perfect balance between fast-paced action and strategic combat. The game flawlessly blends visceral melee combat with satisfying ranged gunplay, allowing players to chain together devastating combos with ease, while still maintaining a sense of weight and power fitting for a Space Marine. The improved enemy AI and variety of Tyranid foes add layers of complexity, requiring thoughtful engagement rather than mere button-mashing. Visually, Space Marine 2 is a tour de force. The environments are gorgeously detailed, from the desolate battlefields to the grotesque alien hives, all rendered with stunning fidelity. The Unreal Engine 5 brings not only the large-scale battles to life but also captures the grim, oppressive atmosphere that defines the Warhammer 40,000 universe. Add to this an intense score and immersive sound design, and you have a game that doesn’t just succeed as a sequel but firmly cements itself as a standout title in both the Warhammer franchise and the wider action game genre.

Unfortunately, this game seems to be particularly taxing on the CPU, resulting in GPU usage below 80 percent being more the norm than the exception. I understand that the density and number of enemies in this game require a good processor, but it shouldn't be the case that even the best AM4 (gaming) processor struggles so much. The typical tech bros with 7800X3D and RTX 4090 probably don't care, but it would be nice if, in the near future, people with less powerful setups could also enjoy the game at high FPS.

review_comment: I was halfway through the opening level of Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2’s campaign, unloading bolt rifle rounds alongside my two squadmates, when I found myself smiling at just how good it feels to be back in this futuristic grimdark fray. It’s been over a decade since the original, but Space Marine 2 reinvigorates the squad-based shooter series with seeming ease. The environments are varied and breathtaking, the running-and-gunning feels great, and the sense of comradeship while fighting with your team, be they bots or friends, can be exhilarating. It may not break much new ground in its genre, but it didn’t need to for me to have a blast playing through its dozen-hour campaign.

review_comment: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2 delivers an exhilarating, action-packed experience that fans of the franchise will love. The game's intense combat, immersive environments, and faithful representation of the Warhammer universe make it a standout sequel. As a Space Marine, you feel the weight and power of the iconic Adeptus Astartes, cutting through hordes of enemies with brutal efficiency. The graphics are stunning, the gameplay is fluid, and the story keeps you engaged from start to finish. Whether you're a long-time fan or new to the series, Space Marine 2 is a must-play for anyone who loves fast-paced, visceral combat in a grimdark setting.

review_comment: The game was a bit rocky to get going, mostly due to crashing, which I think is entirely due to the fact I got advanced access by pre-ordering. Once I got it working (restarting PC, lowering graphics, and putting it on an SSD), the game is fantastic. Gameplay is amazing, from it's stunning gunplay and melee, to the interesting campaign storyline and 3 player PVE mode. The mechanics take a small bit to get used to, but it's such a great experience top to bottom. Customization is a nice thing to see, although it tends to be a bit of a struggle, I can see why the developers have set it up as so. Overall, the game is fantastic and I think it's worth my $90.

review_comment: After hearing a lot of good things about this game, I decided to give it a shot. Now I will be honest and say that I have yet to squad up for the campaign but after playing for a few hours solo... I'm not impressed. The story so far is not something that would draw you in even if you are a franchise fan. It all feels a bit forced and it's mostly repetative in terms of gameplay. The loot the game offers in the missions themselves is honestly underwhelming and basically the same three weapons rotated. I liked that you have to keep an eye on your ammo but even on veteran difficulty there is loads to be found around the map. The game is basically Helldivers 2 but with a sword. I'd "recommend" this to a true fan of the franchise but otherwise it's a game that you can easily skip and save some money.

review_comment: This game is a solid, compact Third Person Shooter and RPG experience. With a reliable multiplayer component that is easy to jump in, play a couple games in under 15 minutes, and wind down after a long day. The campaign has no replay-ability unless you are achievement hunting or helping friends play through it for the first time. The dedicated co-op operation missions are enjoyable, however there are only 7 so it can get repetitive if you want to level up the 6 classes. Speaking of, those classes are all unique in their perks, abilities, weapons and cosmetics, making them the highlight of the dedicated co-op experience. It's a solid package that is only being added too, with the 7th operation mission already added with more on the way, along with new weapons and multiplayer match types. As a 40k fan I am really happy with this, as a gamer I am happy with this. I'd say worth 40 bucks on sale. If you see it any lower, jump at the chance.

review_comment: Great game solid 8/10. I love me some 40k and to see a good 40k game is always a welcome addition. The gameplay was very funny and intuitive although I would say this game is best played on a controller. The story starts really strong and slowly tapers off. I wish there was more mission variety and gimmicks within each mission to make them more interesting. The mission with jump packs was fun. I wish we had more of that. The operations are interesting on paper but I found myself not really interested in replaying them; they have similar issues with the campaign missions. The pvp is incredibly fun. At this point it's pretty simple: three maps, three game modes but so much fun. It weirdly and nostalgically reminds me of Transformers fall of Cybertron pvp. Also the chaos factions desperately need customization.

You get a full left 4 dead style set of mini-campaigns for co-op with cosmetic and skill tree based customisation for classes unique to the mode. Finally, you also get a full PvP mode too! Sure this mode is clearly underbaked and not well balanced, but it's still fun! and it's not trying to be anything else, they just knew that we would all want to pit space marines against space marines to they tossed it in for free! The core gameplay loop is simple, but satisfying and fun, the story is pretty messy, but some of the character moments are great, and the visuals are truly stunning! The art direction is just fantastic, this is the first 40k game I've played to truly capture the grand, epic scale that makes it so appealing, while darktide captured the aesthetic and tone perfecctly, it stuck to smaller scale environments with a more limited scope. Space Marine 2 blows it out of the water, giving you battlefields stretching to the horizon, literal HUNDREDS of enemies at once really selling the super human power fantasy of cleaving through hordes of weaker enemies at once and the insane scale of the world, with buildings and ships covering the entire sky and all of this with enough engine optimisation that I was able to run the entire game on a mid range system at a steady 60fps with all settings on high! The lowest frame dip I ever saw was only 50fps, which is really incredible when you take into account how good this game looks. The only "microtransaction" is a season's pass that is just cosmetics, and which they have said the profits will go back into the development of the free content they are adding later on! I would love to go back to releasing games like this, it launches with a full suite of content, you pay once up front and get everything you want, and it incentives you to keep playing by having a long list of unlocks that you can ONLY unlock by just playing the game, rather than a never ending stream of limited time paid content that tries to tap into your FOMO to get you to keep playing and spending more money. On top of that it is the best representation of the 40k universe in a game yet! Even with some of it's minor flaws like repetitive gameplay by the end of the story mode or a forgettable plot, it does so much right and shows you so much you've never seen before in a game that it cannot get anything but a full recommendation from me!

review_comment: For the combat, the game requires actual thought when it comes to attacking enemies in melee. Mindlessly smashing the attack button without any thought will result in you getting punished by an enemy attack. Unlike other games where close combat is dumbed down to glorified a QTE like the Assassins Creed series. Space Marine 2 requires you to recognize enemy movement and attack patterns similar to games like the souls series. Contrary to what some may think, Space Marines are far from invincible (lower difficulties not withstanding). You will need to gauge when to pull out of a fight, or when to start lining up an execution on a weaker enemy to get your armor back on veteran and higher difficulties.
name: Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2

The game does not look nearly good enough to warrant this performance. Everything is covered in a grimy texture with assets that look like you straight took them out of a PS3 game. If I can run KCD2 and Cyberpunk on maxed out settings comfortably, then there is no reason this game should be running like this. Embarrassing. Wait for a sale and/or optimization updates. I've played games on my Deck that look better than this. When I was kid I couldn't believe how good MHFU looked on my PSP, an entire world in my hands. And now they release a game like this. review_comment: It is very early to judge Monster Hunter Wilds. Given that right now the content is very sparse due to the dependency on a regular content update model and the total lack of G-Rank until the inevitable expansion, I have no doubt in my mind that Monster Hunter Wilds will provide a tremendously great experience when it comes to the very core of Monster Hunter gameplay, primarily by virtue of abandoning overly intrusive combat gimmicks and perfecting the existing weapon kits. However, much like World, I heavily dislike what direction the series is moving into, and I believe with Wilds we have reached a point where these design trends have started to become an active liability—a totally nonsensical main story, the total removal of all vanity gameplay, and the misguided focus on larger and larger MMO-esque player lobbies have sapped my enjoyment of the game every step I have thus far taken into the as-of-yet lackluster postgame.

review_comment: Yes, they made it casualized. Yes, they made it easier. Yes, they made it more accessible. Yes, some parts of the game play itself. Yes, there's too many cutsenes. These changes made in Wilds aren't debatable, especially for returning long-term players; and this matters to some of them and that's completely fair. Regardless, these changes have created the most comfy monster hunter to date. Settling in to grind monsters is good fun, your time efficiency is better than ever, and there's still a very high skill ceiling. Capcom have also once again shown how to do skimpy armours right by giving player choice and variety. The only thing I will speak negatively on is the unforgivable performance. The visuals should NOT demand this much hardware, and developers relying on AI-Slop fake frames to exceed 40 FPS should not be accepted. Wait for a sale, the game is damn fun but absolutely needs more polish.

review_comment: Despite all of my ranting about Monster Hunter Wilds, I think it's a fantastic entry! It is missing a lot of key 'Monster Hunter' aspects, but it makes up for them in a plethora of ways! Combat is as flashy as ever and every weapon now has a super cool and flashy move that makes you feel like an action hero! Once you get past the forced walking sections and the annoying camera issues, Monster Hunter Wilds feels like if Monster Hunter World chugged 3 red bulls and attempted the Fonzie shark jump, except the shark is on fire and Fonzie parries it. It's stupid fun and in many ways I think that the gameplay is mechanically the best the series has ever put out - I'm just looking forward to the game getting more support down the line and I hope that the inevitable expansion goes above and beyond in fixing a number of the issues I have listed here. Highly recommended!

review_comment: My system is more than average. The game not only needs significant work regarding the processing issues but it has some fundamental game mechanics that make the game a struggle session. Regarding the processing, I come into area and it isnt loaded, I watch 1/2 to 2/3 of every cut scene with people as ugly polygon shapes before thy render. Nothing looks good in the environment, as it is isnt loaded AND I actually think so far the environments are ugly. The general style of the game makes me feel like Im a 3D object moving over / on top of the environment instead of being inside of it, this is an art style Ive seen before and I hate it. This is so much less immersive than Worlds, it is jarring to my eyes and I just don't get this style choice as it ruins the open work feel and coupled with the environments and people not even loading right and it is a real mess. I have almost 1000 hours in World so I played it a lot, always with my husband, and we had many issues with the mechanics of that game when it came to playing together. We always had to start a quest then both leave and met up and then go out together so the story never flowed out and was a bit annoying. This game has all those same issues and more of them; devs- since you CLEARLY wanted this to be a single player game you should have just done that instead of teasing everyone that you were doing something open world. If you want this to be something you go and easily hunt and gather with friends- don't hold your breath. I have more issues but the last I will say is that as of right now there is not a hint of testosterone in this game. In worlds I got DJ Atomica (Burnout- IYKYK) to be the main monster slayer and help me around along with some other awesome characters and a cool cat Chef. No bad ass men hunters it's just Werner who literally screws everything up and is braindead, all of the chicks in this game are so touchy feely I want to throw up (Im a girl BTW), no canteen to eat with friends and share resources, no cute cat chef!!!!...what have you all done to this game. I regret not waiting to buy this game, I fell for the reviewers I trusted and got snatched. WAIT to buy this until they do some fundamental changes/updates.

Great progression, an actually interesting story, more tightly paced fights, and even more fluid prep -> hunt flow thanks to the vast open areas make this heavily addictive, even more so than World! The monster variety is stellar and is a nice blend of new and returning monsters. The wound system makes fights so interesting and most weapons feel even better than they did in World and Rise. I am so excited for this games expansion assuming it goes the way of World and Rise, and I will be playing this for years to come.

review_comment: 60 hours into this game. I really much like it but it has serious performance issues! Started playing it on launch day for around 10 hours straight and got no real problems other than dropping FPS. After these 10 hours my PC randomly hard crashed, thought it was a random occurrence and restarted my PC and the game, after an hour ingame my PC once again hard crashed. Searched for reasons and solutions for this problem, recalculated the power consumption of my rig and overwatched it with MSI Afterburner (shouldn't be the problem), temps were never the problem (never above 80 degrees celsius on my GPU and 70 degress celsius on my CPU), looked for data corruptions via Steam, reinstalled it (solved it for a few hours then hard crashed again), updated my GPU, my Bios and even Windows with no result, even looked for damage on my storage devices with admin commands and nothing there. I don't know what to do anymore, i want to play but i can't because it will hard crash right after doing one hunt. Only conclussion is bad game development, because other games (Space Marine 2 on high settings f.a.) work fine, also I'm not the only one with this problem, other players with similar or better specs also get hard crashes. This negative review will stay until April update, if this update even brings better performance. If nothing happens after that my review will stay. This game makes fun and brings new changes into Monster Hunter.

review_comment: I recommend waiting for a sale or when you can get the game bundled with the future expansion. Don't get me wrong, the game is really fun, but It's pretty clear that the days of having content rich Monster Hunter games on release, are over. Low rank goes by super quick, high rank was kinda underwhelming, the hardest hunts take no longer that 10 minutes and there's barely any optional quests. There's currently only one 8 Star quest you can do which are just tempered Arkveld investigations. It was also very disappointing for me to find out that there currently seems to be absolutely nothing that you unlock when reaching HR100. I was thinking maybe you'd get to hunt the Zoh Shia in high rank, but no. I'm sure once they update the game a bunch it'll be worth the price, but as it stands, MHGU still has more value than this game.

review_comment: It's sad, because this game has some qualities. The combat is the best so far, focus mode, perfect block, and parry changed the game for melee weapons and gave them a new way to play that we didn't have before, the AI companions are surprisingly good and don't hinder the player at all, the story adds more to the lore of MH and answers a few questions we had in the past regarding the ancient civilization and their relation to fatalis, the exploration and open world are also the best so far, the world is more alive than any other title, and so are the monsters and their interactions with the environment and with other monsters as well. The game is more accessible than ever and everyone can play. But until capcom fixes all the broken things in MHWilds, i can't give it a positive review. review_comment: If this game had a fraction of the problems it has then I would still probably recommend it. Notice how none of my cons have to do with the core gameplay, the real bread and butter of Monster Hunter. Tokuda could cook up a half-baked dud and it would still be a fun game at the end of the day, and that’s exactly why scores from journalists are as high as they are. I have higher standards for the devs though because I know what they’re capable of giving us, and because of the multitude of issues present in this game I cannot recommend it in good faith. I’ll definitely continue playing it alone and with friends but if somebody tells me they don’t want to buy it, I really can’t blame them especially if they’re on midrange hardware that should realistically run this game at 1080p/60fps natively. Wilds probably should have been cancelled and then developed on the REX engine instead with Ichinose’s next game to fill the gap. It’s just too ambitious for what the RE engine is capable of unfortunately. At the very least it should have been delayed for half a year, but Capcom rushed it out the door to appease shareholders. So now it is what it is and I’m not sure if the team will be able to fix all of the huge problems this game has. I really hope they can and they prove me wrong, but that’s not what happened with Dragon’s Dogma 2. If Wilds does reach a state where the good outweighs the bad then I’ll update my review but until then I can’t recommend a $70 game with such high hardware demands that pushes the envelope so little.
name: Monster_Hunter_Wilds

review_comment: This game is so disappointing. If you are going into this to play with friends (as you do with monster hunter) I wouldn't touch this game. As it currently stands it essentially forces you into playing singleplayer first, roadblocking the fun you could be having with your friends behind the singleplayer story content. I dont play these games for the story, narrative, voice acting, or characters because these games are in fact are not great at those things. Being forced to play through mediocre singleplayer content that's poorly voiced and written just isnt fun. When I played through worlds with friends for the first time we would be forced to watch the new monster cutscenes before we actually got to hunt together, everytime we would roll our eyes as we signed up for a solo quest just to leave it to fight it for the first time with one another after all seeing the cutscene, this game has SOMEHOW made that even worse by gating things even further. I buy monster hunter to hunt monsters with my friends and this game is very much ANTI that, it's antithetical to what monster hunter is. I want to sit down and fight stuff with my friends, I do not care about Erik cringely talking about how "this forest is AMAZING". I wish the game would be more focused on what really made monster hunter special, since the older titles, hunting monsters with friends.

Have upgraded only 2 pieces of armor and am still wearing the rest as starting gear and past the "black flame" The lack of a really customization camp or house kinda sucks, but that will more than likely be coming in a DLC of some sort. Though painting your tent is kinda neat. I'd give it a decent 8/10, but the crashes make it like a 3. After all, good visual, sound, and gameplay are neat and all, if only it could be played for more than 10 mins without a crash. Not recommended now, but once the crashes are done happening, will change it.

review_comment: i am 10 hours in and nowhere near free of the absolutely claustrophobic story. i honestly think a newborn baby could have made better decisions about the narrative design in this video game, because although lacking the power of speech it would not be able to make any of the good decisions that have undoubtedly been made besides this one, it also wouldn't be able to say "don't let them do anything without being introduced to it via cutscene first, in our open world game". i hear high rank is way less miserable about this and that's the only reason i'm continuing to play it. the actual gameplay, which i believe represents a small fraction of the 10 hours i've spent on monster hunter wilds, is competent, solid, and fun, and the game is set up to grab you by the arm and usher you away from it like a wayward child as much as it possibly can without outright stopping you. you can technically leave camp and go fight a monster yourself if you need materials but despite most other things being tutorialized this never once gets mentioned and if you happen to organically discover something new while doing that you get told you don't have permission to play that part of the game yet. i have never played a game that has less confidence in the things that organically happen in it being cool enough to keep your attention, that is more desperate to hide any real part of itself behind careful staging, and it drives me insane that they do this because, like i said, the gameplay is good! it's as good as it's ever been. dumbed down, i guess (i wouldn't know - the oldest monster hunter game i've played is mhgu and i liked both world and rise better) but it's undeniably a monster hunter game, so like... why are we doing this? why hide the video game part of your video game under a bunch of tedious smoke and mirrors? why?

review_comment: Please note that the performance issues I experienced were minor or infrequent so performance of the game didn’t affect my impression of the game. Made it to HR 100 recently and I can say that Wilds isn’t quite as big or grand as World but it has some polish and convenience that I wish World had. All cutscenes are skippable which is a big plus for me (I downloaded a mod to skip them in World for my second playthrough). Difficulty feels generally easier than World but it’s pretty easy to seek out high difficulty monsters if you prefer and even some of the harder non tempered monsters are still able to kill me in endgame if I’m not careful. The story doesn’t feel as long as World but you also don’t have to do super long Zorah Magdaros missions or scour the map for footprints over and over again so I don’t think it’s necessarily a bad thing. I’ve been enjoying endgame and the new weapon crafting system. It’s nice to be able to craft a T8 weapon of any type at the end of the game without going through the entire weapon upgrade tree. Part of the difficulty being a bit easier is that monsters are more exploitable with the wound system and other environmental factors but I think it’s fun to feel like you’re using your knowledge to exploit the monster. It reminds me of the posture system in souls games a lot which is a very exploitable system and feels good without making the game feel easy. Wilds is a win because if you do a firework emote the support hunters will do it too and the fishing wudwud will cheer if you catch a big fish near him and that’s all you need really.

If you can manage load in and play the game with your friends and slay monsters, more power to you! But to everyone else unable to play, I urge you to down vote and leave negative responses until these issues are fixed. Everyone else will be distracted by the blacksmith chick so its up to us to attempt any sort of disruption in sales to be heard. My review will be subject to change when the crashes are fixed.

review_comment: I put in about 75 hours and I suspect this is what the average player will put in before the current base game (as of this review, before TU1) grows tiring, plus or minus 10-12 hours depending on experience. Just 1 or 2 truly endgame hunts would have completely changed the game, but the endgame weapon system for min maxing has almost no function currently since tier 8 weapons handle everything just fine and tier 3 gems drop like candy. I do trust that the current sandbox will provide its intended experience, which is to introduce newer players to the world and give them difficult bosses before TU's start to be rolled out. Combat difficulty is more player oriented then game system enforced. Meaning difficulty is mainly on the player to accept. For series veterans I would strongly recommend waiting for a sale while newer players are good to go so long as they can functionally run the game. A small note about optimization: This games optimization is very poor and while I purchased the game I wont purchase any of the cosmetic dlc to really support the devs.

review_comment: So, should you buy Monster Hunter Wilds? If you really want to play the newest iteration then yes absolutely, its a very fun game. That being said, only about 30-40% of the game is out now. MH games tend to have the vast majority of their content released as title updates and the master rank dlc that release 1-2 years after the game. This was the case with with MH World and its dlc Iceborne and it was also the case with MH Rise and its dlc Sunbreak. The best time to get into any MH game is 2-3 years after release when all the content is out and you can get the game and its dlc on sale. World and Rise are both often on sale so they may be better investments for the time being but if you're patient then Wilds is definitely worth getting into

review_comment: Steam allows refunds within two hours of in game time, within two weeks of purchasing the game, no questions asked. Within two hours of booting up the game, I had not even finished precompiling the shaders to be able to run the game, much less played the game I purchased. I must now question if these shader compilation processes are artificially inflated in their processing time to stop refunds on Steam. By the time I got to start the game, I couldn't tell what was happening in the opening sequence due to textures not loading and things popping in and out of existence around me, but by this point is was far too late for a refund. With the way the pause menu works in this, I couldn't even try and pause and adjust the graphics settings, because the game keeps running while the settings menu is open. The only reason I have 12 hours as of writing this, is that I left it on overnight to run the shader compilation, I have less than 20 minutes in the actual game. With a 3060, definitely higher than the recommended 2060 in the given recommended specs, I am getting frame drops and occasionally go from frames per second, to seconds per frame, on medium graphics settings, with frame generation off and upscaling on performance mode, not that upscaling should be needed to run a game at 1920x1080p. The developers of this game should honestly be disgusted with themselves, and their management should do the world a favor and quit their jobs, because this is entirely unacceptable performance for a $70 video game from as big a studio as Capcom.

review_comment: While I feel for the people that have not been able to play and can't ignore the many performance and optimization issues that came with the release of this game, based on my time spent, I think it should be given a fair chance. I was skeptical because of these issues and a lot of the beta footage we recieved, that I would not be able to run this game well on my 4060ti, but the game looks great, runs well and has had no framerate drops that I can recall (so far). My experience with Wilds has been amazing so far, from the hunters I've met to the new weapon and gameplay changes, and the new monsters are awesome as well. The story is great and hunter voice lines made for such an immersive experience, I actually payed attention the whole way through and didn't skip anything, which I do in most games. I do feel the keybinds need to be further optimized for PC, as there do seem to be a lot of useless actions that conflict with others if you try to change them... but once you get used to it, the game really opens up (if controller isn't your thing). review_comment: This is my first monster hunter game. I didn't really know what to expect going into it. I was pleasantly surprised. The game play is rock solid, crafting and upgrade system addicting, and the animations are very high quality. The story was fine but I honestly did not care and ended up skipping a lot of the cut scenes toward the second half of the story because I just wanted to fight cool monsters. I've heard performance being a major issue for some people. I have a 4080 ti. I havent really had any performance issues as far as fps goes, but i have had several crashes over 40 hrs and a handful of visual bugs. Both were infrequent enough to say they didnt impact MY overall enjoyment of the game but I feel like I have a pretty high tolerance for these types of issues. I have no reference for how hard or complicated some of the previous games are, but the difficulty is fine for me. I enjoy challenging games a lot, which this game is definitely not, but once you get to the end game you have to pay attention and have the right gear to efficiently kill stuff. That being said ive only failed one quest in my entire play time, and i think i would enjoy the game a bit more if it was more challenging. The amount of systems working is a bit overwhelming for a first time player of monster hunter, but if youve been playing video games for awhile or youre a vet of the series youll be fine. Just read stuff and pay attention to what the game is telling you to do. Overall, love this game. Very hooked on the end game loop right now trying to craft high level stuff. 8.5 /10. Excellent game.
name: Monster_Hunter_Wilds

review_comment: Absolutely loving the game so far. While the story might be as interesting as Worlds story, it still has been decent. People have been complaining about the difficulty but it hasn't felt any easier than World, but it does feel a little harder than Rise at least. It seems the complaints are coming from players that have played an insane amount in the past games, where I have around 300+ hours in World and 200 in Rise, so I do not find the game to be easy at all and it seems to have a much more leveled difficulty which I think is the best direction the game could go. The game has been running quite well on my 4070, on high and highest settings (This is with DLSS at Quality and Frame Gen on) Getting around 80-120 fps, depending on the area. Frames have been smooth enough that I haven't seen any massive slowdown while fighting anything, which for me is a good thing. My only real complaint so far is a lack of an area where a team could hang out/eat in, and I loved the housing in the previous games, especially Iceborne. Hoping thats something that could come at a later date.
name: Monster_Hunter_Wilds

review_comment: This is easily the best Monster Hunter to date. Most people complaining about performance issues are running this on old hardware. This game is not meant to be played on a potato. Sure, it has lots of room for optimization which which will improve performance for some but for those of us with newer rigs it runs totally fine. Quick load times. Beautiful graphics. Very tight and rewarding combat. The multiplayer match finding can be quite janky at times but as with previous titles this will also improve in time. My biggest complaint is with a couple annoying characters in the Main Story but lets be honest, this isn't a game you play for the story. The game truly opens up after the Main Story is complete and there are even more hunts and monsters coming in future updates!

review_comment: I have a PC capable of running this game at max settings, but only with DLSS and Frame Gen. The problem with that is that the game looks blurry and sloshy AF. If you don't enable DLSS, it looks horrendous. Everything has jagged lines and looks pixelated. The only way to have crisp graphics is by enabling resolution upscale (or w/e it's called) and putting it at 1.75x-2x. The problem with that is that it tanks my FPS hard to an unplayable 25 FPS. Capcom please fix! Stop using DLSS and frame gen to save some development time and make the game look good without them in the first place. Not to even mention the poor performance compared to what graphics the game has. Don't get me wrong, the game can look really good. It's not at cyberpunk levels though and Cyberpunk runs way better with PATH TRACING on my PC. That's just unacceptable. I don't buy this "Verify hardware requirements" shtick. It doesn't hold.

review_comment: I will begin this review by stating that I have put close to 6000hrs into the MH series (4000ish of which is in MH4U) in the last decade or so. I adore Monster Hunter and the series has long since earned my loyalty, but it has lost any loyalty I have now. This game is simply awful at being a Monster Hunter game. It feels like it attempts to iterate on World, the weakest entry in the series in the last decade, moreso than anything, the base game moreso than Iceborne (which was by far the best part of that game). Anything interesting or compelling gameplay-wise is gone. World's awful heavy-handed story? Back and 10x worse than before. The whole game is plays itself as you listen to asinine dialogue that drags on and on as the game forces you to go places and do things you have no interest in. When you aren't lucky enough to be in a cutscene, every line of dialogue is followed by a 5 second pause that makes it feel unnerving and awkward. All the interesting and unique changes from Rise/Sunbreak (no hot/cold drinks, palamutes, weapon skills, &c.)? Gone completely. The game literally won't even let you upgrade your own armor until you're quite deep into it. All hunts are short and barely interesting and you can craft all a monster's equipment after just one or two hunts. Capcom even had the brilliant idea to remove the ITEM BOX. All of which is to say nothing of the horrible performance and constant stutter that makes even attempting to play this game a migraine-inducing hell. This easily takes the cake as my least favorite entry into the series (even acknowledging the abysmal MHST2). I pray for a decent Sunbreak save transfer tool to crop up, because all this game has managed to do is make me wish I was playing an actual good game. A beautiful game and a testament to the fidelity with which Capcom can produce a title, but utterly horrid AAA drivel to play. I will not be playing the next main-series entry. 4/10

review_comment: Would not recommend for $70, especially if you're a fan of the franchise and enjoyed World and Rise, and I won't delve into the optimization and performance issues as everyone already talked about it. CONS: 1) The lobby system mechanics is bad, people cant be in the same "world" and start quests from the handler, therefore, must kick people off. 2) The mount movement control is far worse than Rise's. 3) Cutscenes take longer than the actual fights (especially In the earlier part of the game), and parts of the quests where it makes you "walk and talk" w/ NPCs is really annoying when there're a ton of them. 4) The open world aspect of the game is essentially restricted until you progress the story enough, and it only feels forever due to the length of the cutscenes. 5) No monster hunter language... PROS: 1) Every weapon and armor look way cooler and sets each other apart based on the monster. 2) New monster designs are cool and fights are fun. 3) The new focus strike mechanics are pretty cool. 3) Being able to bring 2 weapons with you can make the fight more interesting.

review_comment: 10/10 game, for the first monster hunter to be released on PC day 1, i have very few complaints. Having high end PC, i do experience some frame drops when entering cutscenes and frame generation instantly crashes my pc, Other than that the game is a true experience and hands down the best Monster Hunter and the best RPG. The story is amazing, the amount of post game content and sub plot is almost overwhelming, the visuals are stunning, and the music? oh my god the music. They know when to make you feel like youre stranded in a desert lost and lone with the music alone, boss fights have a dark souls level of sound, even just walking around passively the music makes you feel free and limitless. The weapons feel amazing after the changes from the beta. The monster roster is the best Monster Hunter has ever had (and i havent even seen all the late game stuff yet, and title updates and dlc are still to come) and THE WOUND SYSTEM is the best gimmick they have added. Please, for your self, play the game. How often do we get what we pay for? i bought the $80 pre-order version cause im a simp for cosmetics and my only regret is i didnt get the most expensive version cause i just want to support this game. The game is easier than other monster hunters but i dont think thats a bad thing and alot of game back from iceborn which is master rank and a whole different beast in its own so i dont think the "its too easy" complaint is valid although i wouldnt mind it being more difficult in the high ranks. But i digress, Have fun, grab some friends, and go hunt!

Some textures seem to be improperly loaded which makes for some funny immersion breaks but the game is 100% solid and worth the money. Its beautiful aside from very few seldom issues, the combat is smooth, catered well around different weapons, and the monsters and their gear are SICK. Story is also good enough to have me sucked in but NOT so confusing that i need a textbook lol. If you like MH series buy it. review_comment: The reviews posted citing severe performance issues are accurate. To be fair, I have a relatively low-spec PC (5700x3D, 2060 Super) but sub-45 FPS for a modern title on all low settings at 1080p with DLSS is unacceptable, especially when it looks this bad. For comparison, I can play monster hunter: World WITH high-res textures at MUCH higher settings while getting AT LEAST 60fps. I was gifted this game, but $70 is far to steep a price for a game with such bad performance issues. Wait for updates that address optimization before buying or avoid if you have a mid-tier or lower system. Do NOT trust the minimum and recommended specs on the steam page or that Capcom have posted. When and if Capcom addresses these issues, I'll update my review.
