Religion part of the game still seems in development; will have to play more to figure that out. I can't readily see where opposing army strength is at; difficult to fight wars that way. Can't find how many trade routes I should have or a listing of who is receiving them. Espionage is underwhelming with only able to hit a "counterspy" button. All the above said, the imagery is fantastic, the new concepts are intriguing and I appreciate the great generals and fleet commanders during combat. There is room to grow but that's okay. Civ VI started out very, very slowly but came on strong. I'm hoping for the same here.

I already know that I will be dumping at least another 1000 hours into it. The review remains negative because while I respect the hard work it takes to produce a game like Civ 7, the removal of basic QoL features, and launching with DLC already announced that probably should have been in the game from launch, rubs me the wrong way. This is acceptable for indie studios but not AAA games. Once the game is more polished and fleshed out, looks better and performs better, and has most of the easy stuff that should've been in from day 1, I will change the review to positive. You cannot rename a city, you cannot set a scout or ship to auto explore. There's just simply no reason why a game this expensive shipped at this price. They should have spent another 6 months finishing it. This is not even mentioning the 129 euro price to play a week early with a few civs/leaders locked unless you pay double? Now there's a focus on 30 euro DLC to essentially sell you parts of the game it should have shipped with originally. I would say wait a year and buy it on sale. review_comment: In general, the game looks great, and a lot of the basic game play is fine, but certain areas of game play still seem half-baked and unbalanced. In particular, NPC leaders seems insufficiently differentiated in their strategies. It is as if the AI has been trained to make them all hyper-aggressive, and their approaches are weirdly synchronized. It feels more like playing against one AI that wields multiple leaders, rather than seeing different personalities, tendencies, and approaches, the way Civ VI tends to play. Diplomacy is a constant whack-a-mole to try to reduce hostility from other leaders, even when they have no principled reason to be hostile. Unlike Civ VI, past transgressions and favors don't seem to age out, so the other leaders stay angry about things that happened a 1000 years before. Other intermediate goals also seem to trigger the AI leaders to all behave the same: during the Age of Exploration, once religions get established, there is suddenly a bum's rush by all the leaders to send out missionaries, like your worst nightmare of a theocratic Catholic Spain in Civ VI, but it is everybody all at once. Or in the Modern Age, all the leaders suddenly create explorers, and the AI is running them all to the exact same excavation sites at the same time, so you can arrive and find a stack of a dozen explorers from 4 leaders on the same hex for one dig, and that same stack trundles around as a group to every other dig site. It is a mad rush to stay ahead of the AI playing the same strategy for every leader at the same time. The game also seems to lack some basic report screens that would make it easier to keep an overview of what your cities and towns are doing. P.S. The problem of the explore rush seems to have been addressed in the latest patch.

review_comment: I've tried playing this game a few times now, and generally speaking, I'm lost. It's very confusing - there are way too many things going on, and it's not what I'd grown to love about the game. I love exploring, and early empire building. In my third game, I built a few towns, and was told that was my limit. Okay, how do I build more? I guess there's always Google. And sending someone to trade. It shows me 2 different towns to trade with. Okay, I'll click on one of them and they'll go. No, that doesn't do anything. Okay, let me check the options of the unit. No, not there. I think I finally figured it out, but it took way too long. I'm also told that I have a crisis, and it's getting worse. I'm not entirely sure what the crisis is. It's not the UI that bothers me - I can figure most of that out, but there are way too many things going on. I feel like I'm playing Diplomacy.

review_comment: I'm sorry, but I've been playing the Civ series ever since Civ II, and this is the first one that simply isn't fun. Instead of enjoying myself, I find that I'm tugging at my hair and speaking out at the game in a loud, angry, frustrated voice. Where is the active unit? Really? That's how you designate it? And when I click on it, nothing happens? How do I cycle through the units? And when I click on a city to examine it, the city's name literally disappears off the map, also obscuring the population count and the number of turns until population increases? But wait... if I click another button, then another window opens that shows me the population count. Okay, so why are my citizens unhappy in that city? Oh, because there's a -5 happiness penalty? Okay, and what causes that? Oh, it "just is?" Okay, and how can I fix that? Oh... buildings? Okay... which ones? No answer? You want me to figure it out for myself. And why is my population 7, but it sure looks like I'm only working the fields on 4 tiles? Oh, and I just gained a leader experience point (or something like that). Great! Why? What did I do to earn it? No explanation? Okay. And okay, I thought I could only have one regular (non-commander) unit in a given tile, yet it sure looks like I've got two warriors stacked on top of each other. And it looks like I'm "befriending" an independent city, even though they're hostile towards me... how did I do that? But why is that not happening for a different independent city? And I just proposed a scientific research agreement with another civ... the help text said it would increase my favorability with them by 12 if they supported it (which they did), but my rating remained the same. This is just too irritating. I know the developers say they're fixing the interface, but despite my being a 29-year veteran in this franchise, I honestly don't care to wait for it. I seriously think the Civ franschise came to a crashing halt with this mess.

review_comment: Honestly as someone with nearly a thousand hours into Civ5 and 150 hours into Civ6 I like the bones of this game a lot more than civ6. Wasn't a fan of the map art style in Civ6, well they fixed that, landscapes are very pleasant to look at. The army system is genuinely interesting and a good pick up from Humankind. The mixing of Civ's is something I could take or leave, kinda liked persistent aesthetics, but also like changing things up from age to age, so that's cool I guess. For me the game's issue (and why i can't leave a positive review) is purely based off game stability and UI choices. I haven't experienced any lag issues or frame rate dips, nor any crazy sudden spikes in memory usage that i noticed happened a bit on Civ6 release date so that's nice. However the save file glitch alone makes the game quite literally unplayable as it was intended to be played, as such I wonder if it even complies with consumer laws as it's technically a broken product being sold. In addition, the endless please wait turn timer has returned, which is something I vaguely recall in Civ5 almost ten years ago when I was running it off what was essentially a dumpster lid with wires, and should not really be an issue with my current hardware which more than surpasses the recommended requirements for the game. DLC policy is neither here nor there, that's purely based on individuals opinions so I won't really comment one way or another. I did not participate in the Civ6 passes and other stuff, and i feel no obligation to here, i will however, probably pick up the expansions when they come out. I know Civ releases can be a little rough (I was a kid when civ5 came out and I remember what it was like before G&K and Brave New World came out) but this is kinda basic stuff like being able to hit the turn button, which you know, I feel should probably work on release. The UI is probably the game's biggest issue in terms of style and actual gameplay, its lifeless, sterile, and feels rushed. Having opponents diplo tabs taking up half the top right of the screen was certainly a choice, as that was an issue I had with civ6 and their little face bubbles to be honest. I will say I appreciate the idea of moving the diplo stuff from a separate tab like in civ5, but honestly I think that's probably the way to go, a simple small drop-down menu. Also using influence is a neat idea, but the whole screen needs a complete overhaul, its kinda stinky right now. the menu is confusing, not intuitive and just a little clunky.I look forward to this game being playable over the next two years, that said it was still a better launch then humankind, so I guess in the current state of the turn based civ builder market, Faraxis is still kinda limping ahead of everyone else. I don't blame anyone for holding out on the game until much later, as that is the financially wise calculation to make, I being a longtime civ fan was just curious to see what this game would look like before I pour several hundred hours into it when its actually good. Save your money for now. Also one more turn button and more map sliders would be greatly appreciated.

I usually turn off all game music but this one has really cool civ specific music that I was kind of digging (Missisipians) so I left it on. Army concept is nice so you don't have units carpeted all over. Fantastic visuals. I agree with some others that the UI could use some tweaking to give players quicker access to things they want to see easily. I'm still learning but enjoying. I mostly ended up buying this because I own every other one and I bought the Founder's Edition so I would get all the DLC's later. I've always bought all of them and I get FOMO. Should you buy this game? I don't know. I think I'll get many hours of enjoyment out of it but It has to compete for my time with KCD2 now. review_comment: If you like cities skylines then you’d probably enjoy this more than any other civ game. The game looks amazing but is unbelievably slow and boring. It’s dull and lifeless. There’s some good mechanics like getting rid of builders and letting commanders pack units but this has removed all strategy around troop movement and capturing builders. Replacing spies with a drop down menu where you purchase actions with little to no consequence has removed all strategy and immersion. This feels more like a paradox game with all the menus, sub menus, and barely findable progress bars. Combat looks and feels bland. You can’t explore ocean until halfway through the game. You cant capture settlers and you get nothing from winning a war besides temporary control of a town/towns. Religion has been watered down and "culture" is essentially just leader abilities from civ 6. There's no strategy, no planning, and no rewarding pay off. It feels like they just want you to build sprawling cities and nothing else for the entire game. You cant rename a city and the city building, while looking amazing, is abysmal gameplay with no strategy required. Hopefully the expansions will bring strategy and planning back to the game.

review_comment: Are you after that "One More Turn" feeling? Well, Civ 7 delivers it. It has a lot of different ways to mix and match your leader and civ choice in each Age, creating a lot of replayability, and it's absolutely gorgeous to look at. Other innovations such as the growth system for cities and towns eliminating the worker/builder micromanaging and drawing a distinction between cities and towns themselves make for an experience that's quintessentially Civ without all the stuff that gets old fast. No more queuing up something to build in all the far flung cities you captured but don't really care about, etc. Yes, the UI needs work, as does the map generation, and there are obvious places to put even more content into the game. But it's fun, and that's what matters.

Trouble is, you have to first choose to repair it in the city menu, then click on the building type you want to repair on the map, even if you only have one of this building type. Gone are citizen management, tile improvements, unit promotions, loyalty, opportunity costs, the list goes on. The game has tons of issues but the biggest is that it's just not rewarding, there's hardly a challenge to speak of. That's not to say that it's easy, it's just pointless and tedious. Age transitions were meant to "fix" the snowball-y nature of its predecessors but the whole POINT of a game of Civ is that your choices build upon each other. Not so in this one. The first 90% of the time you spend in a game simply does not matter, it genuinely has almost zero impact, and that's a fundamental problem that I don't think they'll be able to fix anytime soon, if ever. The UI does not feel great, and I suspect this is because the game was launched with consoles in mind. I hope improvements going forward bring some more intuitive PC interaction while maintaining support for console players. I also miss the ability to select a city and see the outline of the tiles inside the boundary. This can only be done during an expansion event. There are a number of little details like that in the UI that are missing (or I have not found). Outside of UI, I did have other criticisms. I did feel slightly underwhelmed by the end victory screen. I liked seeing all the numbers and charts they had tracking progress from turn 1. This may be tricky with the ages, but I would love to see this come back. There were some bugs, as expected early in launch. On the whole I still feel the good outweighs the bad, and would recommend.

review_comment: This is my third Civ game, I started with Civ V and loved that game and fell in love with Civ VI as well. I feel a very similar way about this game as I did going from Civ V to VI. Going from something you love and are used to to something different is always a step but in the case of VI to VII I have had a great time. I have seen alot of comparisons between this game and humankind but I don't see it. Aside from the civ switching after eras thats about it. This game has three eras which is honestly not that many comparatively and the switch is done really well. Each age feels like a mini game of civ which makes the game really palatable and easy to jump in and out of, having there own goals and challenges to achieve a golden age going into the next era. The switch between eras also acts a little bit like a catch up mechanic which is really nice, playing with friends in a casual setting isn't all that fun when all of a sudden you are no longer competitive and won't be for the rest of the game. Amongst my friends and I we have not had that problem and it makes the game better for it in my opinion. There is also the ability to select which age to start in so if you prefer early, mid or end game you can jump in at that point. I have seen alot of comments relating to the lack of a one more turn feature and bad UI which I get but I don't think it takes away from the game, to me if those complaints keep you from playing you aren't giving the game a fair shot to begin with. There are some tweaks and changes to be made but the inovations that have been made to the game feel awesome and really fresh. Another thing to note is this feels like the most complete Civ on launch of the three I have played and aside from some small fixes, it feels like a complete game with all the bases covered. Either way, thanks to Firaxis for making this awesome game and I can't wait to keep playing.

review_comment: Was really excited about Civ 7 and then I played it. From the units to environmental detail the graphics look great. The first disappointment was the lack of options for the advance options to setup game play. During the game the units no longer have the auto explore option which is a mild annoyance. It seems like trying to advance technology and culture isn't as important since you may not even finish researching them all before the jump to the next age. I didn't like how the jump into the next age is basically a reset of what you had done so far. It was like an episode of Quantum Leap. You left your civilization to jump into a completely new one. It's not a short jump, but a large one time wise. The game feels rushed. I don't know about others, but I enjoy playing the game on marathon speed. In this game it feels like the standard speed compared to the previous ones. I do like the options given for dispersing barbarian outposts instead of just gold. Same with what replaced the tribal villages. The different options make it feel like you have more control over how you want to move forward. I ended up returning the game because of the whole ages skip/reset and game ending instead of allowing you to continue to play. If I wanted to play speed civ I would have chosen the quick speed or played online

review_comment: About halfway through my first game, I'm really enjoying this iteration. Diplomacy is significantly more interesting and useful than in any previous version. Resource management is also much more diverse and interesting. Since I haven't finished a game yet, it's too early to say, but so far the gameplay changes solve or at least improve on major problems that have plagued all prior Civ games: there's less incentive to save-scum, and the age transitions and city vs town distinctions significantly cut down both the micromanagement that becomes increasingly tedious as more and more productive cities result in more and more (often pointless) build orders every turn. In every previous version, end games are typically boring, because the game is almost always decided 100 turns away from reaching the victory condition. I haven't finished a game of Civ 6 in years because it's so tiresome to just click through turn after turn waiting to rack up enough tourism or capture the last city or whatever. I don't know yet if Civ 7 fully solves that issue, but it looks very promising.

For example, I would like to know at a glance if a tech/civic unlocks a building that gives Happiness at a glance. It should be clearly visible in the tree with the Happiness icon or at least some color code. Reading the trees feels like reading a contract and so I'm having trouble planning and finding out the info I need to strategize. Some mods are already working on this. It's not a deal breaker for me, but they've dropped the ball there.

review_comment: Game is a slow starter in the antiquity age, but when you reach the second age it turns up. You need to be strategic with influence management or you'll fall behind so make sure before you click on the next turn to check all the progress of leaders. How much gold culture science their producing etc for leaders with a lot of science or culture make sure you steal their civics preferably they should be far from you as you dont want enemies with your close neighbours. Combat is decent barbarians is gone thankfully and now its independent factions that you have multiple ways to interact with. First is befriending them formally using influence, incorporating them into your civ which will make them count as a town in your overall civ. or you can use them to trigger raids against others or you can conquer them if they're hostile and take over. Resources are pretty simple aside from treasure fleets so do your research before choosing an economic focus. Aside the antiquity age naval exploration is pretty decent you will lose ships early on until you unlock certain techs but yh, enemy players are very aggressive in the first age so make sure you keep track of all your surrounding neighbours make allies disband allies if you don't want to be dragged to wars keep track of independent factions and you should be fine. The game is pretty fun so 9.1./10 only thing to improve would be there should be more info for certain game mechanics like treasure fleets and trade but its good.

The way the rules change as you progress seem overly contrived and convoluted. Why reset half the game with every age? Only your capital remains a city, independent city states disappear, you'll lose some units, but not all of them, you'll lose some buildings, but not all of them, some buildings won't yield as much, your alliances disappear. Like, why make all of these absurd changes? It makes it hard for me to feel like I'm developing any sort of coherent strategy. I also feel like you're pushed into playing a very narrow set of strategies. Changing civs and not matching civs to leaders removes any sense of immersion. Resetting so many stats about your civ from age to age makes the world seem disjointed.

review_comment: I have played every version of Civilization including Call to Power and Alpha Centauri. Civ VI took a step back from Civ V when it first came out but Civ VI eventually carved out its own space in the Civ universe. Unfortunately, I can't see how Civ VII can replicate that. Civ VII's greatest sin is it's boring. These types of games may all be spreadsheets underneath but Civ VII feels like a spreadsheet on the surface. You don't feel like you have just built the Parthenon, you feel like you just added a statistical adjustment. The Ages kill any sense of ownership and progress. They also destroy the illusion you are creating a civilization (why do I have to be the Egyptians to become the Prussians?) A true start earth map would never work with this version. The further elimination of historical leaders in favor of virtue signalling feels like the designers forcing their values on the players (Harriet Tubman but no George Washington? Really?) Here's a tip: Sometimes a barbarian is just a barbarian. By far the greatest sin is they didn't fix the AI. The AI is terrible. AI capabilities have definitely advanced to the level where Civ VII COULD have a great AI. Unfortunately function has definitely taken a backseat to form and virtual signaling. I hope there is way for Firaxis to salvage the bones of Civ VII and rebuild it.

The previous few Civ games felt like an experience -- Civ 7 feels like just a game. Ultimately, it forces you to play smaller game modes and an even more narrow play style to achieve a victory path. This takes away from organic, sandbox and random playthroughs in previous Civ games that made it so fun. I have logged 2000 hours in Civ 6 and never once experienced any sort of playthrough burnout. I have logged 112 hours on Civ 7, can win a science victory by 1850 every game on Diety and then the game just ends -- no continue play option, no future era .. nothing. Then you justify the nonsense civ switch (Rome > Ming...) with "history evolution through eras" and then you have an immortal Benjamin Franklin leader of Songhai... You blinked to casual gamers to enlarge your market (those who are not going to buy the tons of DLCs you are planning to sell) forgetting your faithful players. review_comment: Civ 6, killer game. So if Civ 6 was so good, Civ 7 should be even better, right? Wrong! I was super jacked, so jacked I bought the Cadillac version. Terrible decision. I start a new game playing as Ben Franklin, but my armies buildings, troops are (for example) are French or Roman, which leaves me scratching my head, but I continue the game. Trying to figure out the new mechanics, etc. And then it's time to progress to a new era. Guess what? The troops/army I built, gone. Nothing but the Army General(s) or Fleet Commander(s) are left. Why in the f**k did I go thru all of that s**t just to lose my troops? So now I have to build them back up again. The maps are smaller. There are no more barbarians, city-states, some are friendly but most are hostile and constantly harass/attack you. Which sucks because I want to build my troops for defense/conquest, but I can't because I'm fighting these damn hostile city-states non-stop. Unlike Civ 6, you can only have one counter spy, which means the other players will steal you blind regardless. And if you do catch one of their spies, all they suffer is a penalty, meanwhile you're losing culture/science at a ridiculous rate. There is no "Hey hey! You got caught. No more spying" dialogue. When progressing to a new era, I 'MUST' switch to another civilization. So Now I'm playing as Ben Franklin with an Asian culture (for example). I feel incredibly frustrated by this game and regret buying it. I wonder what the devs were smoking to come up with this steaming pile of horse apples? The worst part, I seriously doubt I can get a refund because I bought the game thru CD Keys and my statute of limitations has run out. I have a serious case of buyers remorse over this game. My advice, give this one a hard pass and stick with Civ 6.

I trust their response to feedback and welcome the changes to gameplay mechanics that are flawed, but unlike some reviews I've seen, the flaws are not unplayable. This game's mechanics with the ages and changing empires as time moves on is a great mechanic, but I feel like it needs some tweaking in terms of allowing the leader to change with the empire because it doesn't make historical sense to have Benjamin Franklin lead Rome. As more civs and leaders are introduced, I'd love for this feature to be added. review_comment: Civ 6 (Yes, SIX) is the pinnacle of Civ games. You have continuity, the freedom to choose your own path to victory, clear and direct objectives and goals and clear and direct methods and strategies for accomplishing those goals. Civilization 6 gave you a sense of purpose as you played, and a rewarding sense of accomplishment when you achieved any victory, big or small. Civilization 7 does a terrible job at best in these regards. Playing through a game of Civ 7 feels like mindlessly trudging through a bog of unnecessary complication. The game developers took everything good from Civ 6 and transformed it into a complex web of handcuffing flow charts and accomplishment trees. I despise how Civilization 7 pigeon holes your game play into a predetermined narrative. Just as I feel that I've established my civilization in this world, the age ends and FORCES me to abandon my civilization (nationality) and start again with a new one. And heaven forbid I should want to expedite my exploration of the world early in the game or expand my empire to a different hemisphere before the game narrative deems it is okay to do so. Civilization 7 is the first Civ game that I have played in this series in which the hours that I've played during a session feel wasted rather than enjoyed. My Civilization Saturdays will be better spent going back and enjoying Civ 6 from this point forward.

They have taken a game that was highly polished and detailed in Civ VI, diluted it, removed vast amount of features and civilisations as well as removed most of the customisation options when starting a new game, and instead added a handful of new features that change the core essence of what Civ is about. The map design is also a joke. Seriously, it’s already led to countless memes because of how badly designed they are! I’m sure it’s going to be patched, I’m sure it’s going to have tonnes of DLC in the coming years, but as far as a release copy of a new Civ game goes, it should come with a warning. review_comment: At the end of the age you get a score screen like you just finished the game, completely disrupting the flow of the game. The maps are small, the AI is dumb, and the civs all feel the same regardless of whether you're playing Charlemagne or Harriet Tubman. The since there's no progressing past the age, you just all end up at the end of the tech tree with the same units clashing armies. Diplomacy is improved but trade now feels weak and lame, so there doesnt seem to be much incentive to really engage with other civs except to keep them from conquering you or getting a small tech boost (which is again, useless because no matter how far down the tech tree you are, you are never an age ahead of your opponents). Independent factions aka city states, are rarely useful imo, they give you the same lame bonuses for befriending them no matter which one you befriend. And dont get me started on multiplayer, which desyncs constantly so playing with friends isnt very fun. It's worse than Civ 6 ever was in that regard. Idk that there's any fixing this game either. because of the way the ages are programmed, i dont think there is anyway to bring continuity back into the game, which is my biggest complaint. You never feel strong or advanced compared to your opponents. you're limited to a few cities and cant expand the way you would like to. all of my cities ended up feeling the same regardless where and how i built them. I dont think there is any fixing it, the game is just garbage because they destroyed the entire appeal of the civ franchise, which is to grow from a stone age civ to a space faring one. unless they can somehow remove the age system which seems built into the cake, i dont see myself ever playing this game again. maybe if it was on sale and a few more updates come out, but even then, i have better games i can go play, like Civ 2, Civ 5, Civ 6, or Endless Legend.

review_comment: I have been very impressed by the style of this new game. It is very obviously part of the franchise, however has refreshing changes that make elements of the game new and exciting. Obviously it does not play exactly like the old games, but the soul is still present. I have noticed a few small surface level bugs like formatting errors in menus and the tech tree has bugged out once as well. I am confident that they will be fixed. I have not personally run into anything that has broken the game yet. Love the soundtrack! The graphics refresh is also fun; makes the obstacles in the world more believable. One thing I do miss from the older games is the extensive amount of customization you can do for building game parameters. Now the advanced menu doesn't really have any customizations beyond difficulty, length, and world type. You used to be able to completely build a world entirely around your style of play, but it is much more limited now. That is my only major gripe.

I have never wrote a review for any game, ever. I ordered the founders package, not to play earlier but since i love civilization franchise , I didn't want to wait for the extra DLC. I realize that games now, always have bugs or issues upon release that are eventually, patched or updated. Right now this game is complete hot garbage. I will ignore (not event mad) of the whole woke/DEI and supposedly Harriett Tubman controversy. Granted she is a relatively important American historical figure but there are more important ones, I would have preferred Fredrick Douglas if they were trying to find new historical people (good idea on trying to introduce new leaders) but some are historical figures that everyone knows for a reason. Tubman addition not a complete surprise since civ 6 went a little woke with Abraham Lincoln in Civ 6. I could be wrong but Lincoln was the only leader in civ 6 that had a negative attribute for something (plantations). I do give credit to them for trying new things by introducing new leaders. Overall, my problem is that they tried to do to much and over complicated the game with over abundant of decision making, mechanics, and systems. I played 215 turns with Roman Empire and Augustus. My specific issues and problems are listed below. First, I agree with other reviews, the UI is awful. I find it very cumbersome and not very informative on new things. Some of the new things, don't need 50 page manual to understand but maybe a little instructions of the pro and cons of the narrative events that seemingly happen for no reason. Half the fun more me was figuring it out myself. I never got passed researching the wheel in science tree, and the special Roman Civic attributes in civic tree. I was about 60 percent through the antiquity age, then age counter shot up to 99%, after AI player conquered another AI player. Then the antiquity age had one more turn before exploration age. Once in exploration age, it was a complete new science and civic tree that represented the middle ages (basically time jump and automatically researched all the science and civics, I did not research). Unless I'm wrong, to my understanding all the other AI civs also advanced in technology to catch up exploration age. Which if the case true is extremely dumb because your basically getting reward for bad strategy and penalized for good strategy. Once I choose the Normans, I couldn't finish building special Roman buildings or Roman specific techs/civics, plus half my military units disappeared (the game noted that half my units would disappear in the new age). I specifically trained more military units and sacrificed certain building for later, since Rome is militaristic. Additionally, once i reached exploration, I couldn't build any wonders from antiquity era. Also when changing to a new age you are not free to choose any new civilization, only certain ones that somewhat similar or historically accurate to one before (my choices after Rome, were Norman or Spain). I think it is an interesting idea to choose another civilization but I prefer to change leaders upon reaching a new age or the option to mix and match any leader for any civilization when the time comes. I think you should be able to choose whatever path you want. Play as Rome or America and stay that civilization then transition to a new Roman or American leader with different unique characteristic as you progress to new age or start as Rome then transition to England or France, then transition to America with either Roman leaders or new leader specific that new civilization. I also don't like the crisis and happiness aspect. I tried hard to to make good balanced decision between happiness, production, and food (as needed) but even if you make good decisions even if not the most efficient or proficient decisions, you have to choose various crisis problem to deal with as progress to the next age. My crisis was a happiness problem, despite going slow in expanding cities ( if you expand to quickly and go over your settlement limit you lose happiness). A settlement limit is dumb, if i want to produce an settle a bunch of towns and cities that should be my choice. I was making sure the happiness system was good but as I got closer to the new age, my happiness plummeted drastically, despite trying account for potential happiness problem. If your planning your cities well and progressing, why should I have a crisis, or have to choose one before moving to new age. Maybe the crisis event happen when you are not progressing and making bad decisions, like in civ 6 and you go to the dark ages or similar. In closing, a lot of good ideas but poor execution in game play because it is very restrictive. In my opinion they made to many changes, in trying to make the game bigger and over complicated it with to many decisions/systems/mechanics and DEI (not because of Harriet Tubman). The DEI concerns are specifically in the feeling that they tried to make the game to historically accurate. It is a game and a fantasy game at that. Why can't I start as America in ancient or antiquity era and go forward or bring Rome, Mayans, and etc into the modern age. The game feels like they just incorporated all the stuff I did not like about humankind. Humankind was ok, had some merits for different mechanics and ideas but in the end I stopped playing Humankind after a few months. Civ 6 had great ideas but very simple and not overly complicated, like apostle and influence by settling to close to another civilization. If they had just tweaked some of systems and mechanics instead implementing the concept of making it bigger and more complex will make it better (bigger and more complex doesn't always make things better). I highly recommend not buying this game if your a fan of civilization games from the past.

review_comment: If you love CIV, and have always loved CIV, then get ready for a crazy surprise..... YOU WILL LOVE CIV VII. If you want to get lost in all the whiny, negative reviews, and let them sway your decision making, then don't buy it. Buy it in 3 years for 90% off. You'll feel cool because you "beat" the system, and didn't have to experience the "horrible UI". Yet, throughout those years of holding off to stick it to Firaxis, you'll still be watching others stream it online, BRILLIANT. I on the other hand, like many of the actual fans of the series who aren't dragging their feet through life with a pessimistic attitude, have waited 7-8 years for this game. We wanted different, and it's different. We wanted change, and there are too many changes to even list. People b*tched about the cartoonish style of CIV VI, so they went back to a more stylish, sleek, realistic art style. Now the UI is too dark and foreboding and you miss the art style of CIV VI? Hmmm.... I bet the devs wake up saying, "man am I glad our fans ARE SO EASY TO PLEASE". To finish on a positive note. Yes, I recommend. 10/10, actually 100/10. No I'm not joking. In a day and age where studios feel the need to rush the newest iteration every year, or every other year, and continue to not listen to fans, there is a lot to be said about a tiny studio who actually listens to their fans. My actual, one complaint about this game, is that there are so many ding dongs that want to complain about nonsense. Give Firaxis some constructive criticism, hints, feedback, ideas, etc. and then give them some time. Most people respond better to a respectful, modest tone and feedback, than they will to some knobhead on youtube just trashing their product. LOVE the game, and looking forward to spending thousands of hours on it.

review_comment: Here's the truth of this whole thing and why I'm so ticked off about it... This game had so much potential, but it just feels like a Chinese knockoff of Civ 6. The killer is that most people would say that Civ 6 is the weakest in the series.... While I disagree, if that were the case, comparing the two games, Civ 6 is a masterpiece, (Even at it's catestophic launch.) Look, I get it, it's a new game, but this isn't Civ anymore, they took all of the good parts of the Civ franchise away, and doubled down on the irritating parts of past installments, while adding even more stupid garbage to supplement as if you weren't going to hate the game enough, they had to make it worse. I love Firaxis, I don't want to see them fail, however, they seem to want to see themselves fail by releasing such a disappointment with so much hype around it. This developer has had such a loyal following for over 30 years.... People keep buying the games because they want an updated version of the games they love, not something so drastically different that it's unrecognizable from the games they love. Firaxis basically spit in every one of our faces with this trash heap.. There are a lot of devs that need to learn this, but I digress. The truth is, The game feels unfinished, and I'd love to tell you that they'll fix it over time, and I'm sure they'll try, but unless they do away with the garbage era system, then this game will always be trash. I will not sing it's praises, I will not recommend it, and no, I'm not hopeful that it'll be good in the future because it's rotten down to it's foundation. In order to fix it they'd need to build a new game.

review_comment: Been a long time fan of the series with roughly 1k hours between civ 5 and 6. This game, at its core, is probably my favorite implementation of the game. The new mechanics and design choices made by the devs in this game are innovative, fresh, and FUN! The game is absolutely half baked and its clear they sacrificed the UI in order to get the core game ready for launch. The pacing is off, fair number of bugs, AIs pretty brain dead, map generation lacks variability and some mechanics just need some more work. IMHO these are symptoms of an early released game, NOT A BAD GAME. All these things will certainly be fixed and polished; quickly resolving many of the complaints raised by other reviewers. I'm giving this game a thumbs up not for what it is today, but for what I have confidence it will be. Every civ game gets ♥♥♥♥ on at launch, this is no different. But like every civ game, they age like fine wine and this game as the potential to be the finest bottle yet. I'm not excusing the bad launch or the fact that DLC is already coming out in a few months. If you want to make a statement, don't buy the game or hold off until the devs have fully patched out everything wrong with the game. I dont blame you, its lame what they did. that being said I got the game because I already know I'm going to love it and I'm enjoying my purchase as I ignore it's lackluster.

You forgot you were forging your own legacy for this game you could have made this better than any other civilization game out there including humankind. for each civilization you started out with could have given us leaders from those eras that were from that country you only did that with a couple of the countries not everyone like in XIV 6. As for the continents very upsetting to see things such the actual continents of earth featured in the game and options such as Real world start location huge the hole earth, something that no other civilization game ever had very sad about seeing that be thrown out the window. Another thing I will add to this is the Governments we get to choose in XIV six you had the options of Monarchy republic Theocratic parliament Democracy Scientific Unitarianism and granted there are still some of these options in XIV seven too but some of them were taken from as well and once you pick a type of Government the timeline which they are affiliated with somewhat forces us to move on to another type of government such as Democracy or Communism we cant stay Monarchy forever we are forced to an extent to move on from that form of Government wasn't too happy to be pressured on that topic too. All and all in the very end I hope that insight such as this will make you realize that you somewhat lost sight of your own legacy for the game and left it in XIV 6 and that you adopted too many ideas from other games the Civilization Franchise had its own look too it put more detail into it went above and beyond to put itself in its own category of Perfection from other Civilization games. There are currently bugs and some features that need refining, however, as well as some in-game descriptions that do not inform players correctly of how to manage their civ. Also, I appreciate the reset between ages, but I wish there were more things to connect you from age to age. Sure there are some buildings, but that's really it. Overall, for me this is a great game for scratching a certain meticulous itch, and I would recommend it for anyone that might feel the same, but I would say wait until they've ironed out the annoying parts, which I guess is a tradition for each entry into this game.

Why on earth would you take out the one more turn mechanic? I personally like playing domination victories and I have not been able to do that since usually one Civ breaks either the culture or science mechanics and wins. Again this is not how I usually play my Civ games. This game needs a major overhaul on the mechanics and AI before I can recommend this to anyone. Oh yeah why can't I have the quick unit move mechanic? I have to wait for the slow moving animations to move massive armies around the map! Come on man! Another gripe I have is why do I lose all my units when an age ends? I spend a lot of turns and money raising an army only to have it erased at the end of an age. I have yet to be able to have nukes or any real modern age army units. This game needs a lot of updates before I can fully enjoy it. PLEASE FIX THE GAME FOR THOSE OF US THAT HAVE SUPPORTED THIS FRANCHISE FOR MANY YEARS!

review_comment: This game could be great, but it's rushed. There are few leader or civilization options, though they'll try to tell you that there are many civilizations. Not really, not when you need three of them throughout the game. The true number is a third of what they advertise, because of the age system. The age system could be OK, but it just makes the game boring and repetitive. Every unit type has a tier 1, 2, and 3 version per age. Woo. There's so much variety! It feels like the skeleton of what could be a good game, it really does. But it feels rushed and only halfway done. And honestly, I wouldn't be so upset normally. The devs have proven they listen to feedback and improve in Civ 6. But, they are selling DLC? For this game that isn't even yet worth the regular asking price? I gave it a good try, I did. You can see my hours played. But I wish I could go back in time and tell myself to hold off. It'll be a long time and a lot of updates before I feel like playing this one again.

review_comment: I have played this game for almost 70 hours. I has been challenging and interesting. It has certainly been engaging whipping me through hours and hours, entire days even without me hardly noticing. There were some bugs when I first started, I read about them and I experienced only one personally, it was not game ending. And there are other strange things having to do with exactly how you build your cities - these I would call puzzles. Understanding the game better means you can build a better city. I'm not trying to find the perfect META layout for the game just now, but my mind does wander that direction sometimes. I've won games several times at this point. I'm starting a new game today and decided to write this review. Replay value is important to me - starting a fifth game is good. I've been going "random" for my starting leader and civilization - and that's lead me to enjoy learning the leaders in a different way. There's many leaders left to try out - many of them don't align with my personal play style from previous CIVs (diplomatic/science) but that's okay. Its having me stretch a little bit and I appreciate that as well. I wish more of my friends played CIV and also that those that do had time for multiplayer - I'd really like to try that, but not really with random people from around the world.

The devs borrowed an idea from a game that failed, Humankind. Why did you had to take everything that made the Civ series special, enjoyable to play and overall a great game and destroyed it? review_comment: Apex Legends is a game I have played for 4 years, and I have definitely seen its ups and downs as time passed. I would personally recommend this game not just because it is fun, but because it has its own unique characteristics in comparison to other Battle Royale games like COD Warzone and Fortnite. You can certainly look up many things about this game, but I believe that it is most likely guaranteed you will find a legend in the roster that suits you best. There is also a great amount of customization in this game (Which can be very expensive if you choose to spend money on this game), comparable to the likes of the games I mentioned prior, with extra possessions like your tailored banner. The last thing I will say before I review this game critically is that it may be tough for new players, though if you research ways to get better online you will get through it. Now, since we have sung its praises with many more that I did not mention, we must now look at what apex does not get right or what it could fix to do better. Hacking is currently rampant in apex, especially in the competitive mode as you move up the ranks. This has been a problem for a very long time, possibly dating back to season 2 (when I started playing), when I was on console so at that time hacking was barely a concern or even not a concern at all, while when I switched to PC in season 3, I personally started seeing cheaters in game as soon as season 5. It also relates to the large incident that happened in ALGS recently, where 2 players (Genburten and ImperialHal) had their game hijacked, giving them esp with full hitboxes, health, and player names, along with bullet (not aim-locking) aimbot. Hacking is the only concern I will describe in this review because it has been recent, and is a genuine concern and has been for a long time. In conclusion, while apex has many great qualities I mentioned, there are some concerns that do not have to do with how the game is intended to be played. I would personally give the game an 8.9/10, because despite its shortcomings, it is unique, it can be tailored, and most of all, it is great, but its shortcomings hinder me from giving it a 9/10 (Amazing). Opinions can differ widely on how good or bad this game is depending on who you ask, so I am not expecting you to 100% believe in my opinion, and all I ask of you is that you at the very least consider it.
name: Apex Legends

Zacząłem grę na nowo między sezonem 10, a sezonem 11. Cały sezon 11 świetnie mi się grało w grę, pomimo, że tak to ujmę, wysokiego progu wejścia. Poznałem Ś W I E T N E osobowości podczas mojej przygody z tą grą, więc tutaj ode mnie plusik. Jednakże, czemu tak niska ocena? Developerzy nie widzą w tej grze nic innego jak zarobku. I TYLKO zarobku. Developerzy wolą wypuścić recolor skina z karnetu z sezonu 3 o wartości ponad 160$ (Zacznijmy od tego, że nagrody z karnetu premium, są z założenia w grach nagrodami, które są poniekąd przedmiotami, których nie można dostać NIGDY więcej za sprawą tego, że płacimy za przedmiot P R E M I U M, mam nadzieję że wiecie co mam na myśli, po prostu są to przedmioty dostępne na jakiś okres czasu.). Po jakimś czasie, developerzy zdecydowali się na pójście krok dalej i zrezygnowanie z dodania nowej postaci w sezonie 18, i zdecydowali się na rework postaci Revenanta (Dlaczego? nie wiem xd) Z ogłoszeniem uniwersalnego heirlooma, o nazwie Katar, i rezygnacji z oryginalnych heirloomów dla postaci, zacząłem mniej grać w Apexa. Heirloom to przedmiot, który nadaje "reference" i w pewnym rodzaju przedstawia historię danej postaci, bo było w nich piękne. Sam jestem w posiadaniu Kunai'a do Wraith, jako że to według mnie jeden z najbardziej clean heirloomów EVER (moja opinia). Po pewnym czasie zrezygnowałem z grania w Apexa, chociażby ze względów na brak gry z kimkolwiek na moim poziomie (ego top xd) i przeniosłem się na gry single player typu Resident Evil 8 Village oraz Resident Evil 2 Remake, które są świetnymi grami swoją drogą. Kompletnie zapomniałem o grze jaką jest Apex Legends, ale przypomniałem sobie o niej wraz z zobaczeniem posta na X'ie, dotyczącego OKROPNYCH zmian w karnecie, przez które on miał podrożeć, jednakże kątem oka zauważyłem, iż zrezygnowano z tej idei (ciekawe dlaczego xd, podpowiedź? opinie o grze w ciągu ostatnich 2 tygodni) Uważam, że gra straciła swój klimat, a developerzy są po prostu łasi na kasę, i to może być jednym z głównych czynników, gdzie niektórzy OG gracze nie są już tak chętni do gry w Apex Legends (z mojego punktu widzenia) Gra już nie jest tą samą grą, którą była między 2020, a 2022 rokiem, i trzeba przyznać, że "zeszła na psy".

They further monetized it with more battle passes and a direct payment system for them leading it to get review bombed and then rolling back parts of the changes, where they still make more money off individual players, just not as much. They also secretly implemented a kernel level anti cheat system and banned a lot of accounts, "accounts" not "cheaters". Similar to Valorant's vanguard the system will ban you on a Virtual Machine. I got banned for downloading the game opening the practice range then closing and uninstalling (Playing on a VM is how a bunch of nerds play video games including SomeOrdinaryGamers and others but it can also their is a chance that cheaters use them to copying a disk image and repeatably cheating, getting banned then making a new vm) I don't completely disagree with a kernal level anti cheat (it has worked well for Valorant) but more they way they handled the implementation, if I knew that EA didn't allow virtual machines I wouldn't play on one, but instead they hid that they implemented a new anti cheat software and made a blog post bragging about how many players banned without noticing that their player base is also shrinking with the ban waves ( cheaters make another account, everyday players will quit when we lose all of progress and characters on our accounts). So in all, EA is reverting to former ways of over-monetization and using an invasive method of anti cheat to pretend like they are handling cheater. Looking at steam charts its seems like EA is responding to a sharp decline in player base (lost half of their player base on steam in the past 6 months) and looking to make the number go up, trying to get the player base to pay twice as much. Then they ban players for using an uncommon system configuration have poor ban appeals and wonder why the game's numbers are still on the decline. (Also if they are supposedly banning 100,000 accounts per month, as their write up says, they are directly responsible for the player decline and trying to extract more cash out of their dwindling player base) TDLR; EA's is trying to account for half the player base leaving (or EA banning them) by 2x the price for battle passes and they are contributing to the player shrinking with a poor anti cheat implementation.

review_comment: I've been playing apex since release, I'm a day 1 player. I started on console with well over a few thousand hours and I have 330 hrs on PC. I've played every game mode, LTM, event and I play ranked every other season. I have thousands of kills, millions of damage dealt, just as many deaths Lol. Apex is a game I've always played, at one point I loved this game and it's all I played. But as time went on it got more and more infested with hackers, people making smurf accounts to grind and sell. The player count has been so up and down, especially lately with the player count dropping from 600K to 90K just this season. It's mainly because of EA. Every cosmetic these days are dull and rushed, 90% of the time it's a recolor. They'll drop one skin and charge $40 for it because it comes in a bundle with a sticker and weapon charm. I mean for God's sake the entirety of their 6th year anniversary was just skins they already released. They didn't even attempt to reward the players who have stuck by them for 6 years through some of their worst times. Which every season seems to be worse than the former so that's saying a lot. They don't listen to the players, ever. In game audio has been a problem since release and they either make it worse or don't fix it. I can hear teammates foot steps louder than gunfire but a full team of metal characters can sneak up on me full sprinting and using abilities. Ridiculous. But the reason I can't recommend Apex the most is because it isn't new player friendly. The people who are playing have done so for 6yrs. You can't possibly catch up to us, you just can't. The learning curve is difficult and the skill based matchmaking (SBMM) is bad. You have one decent game and you'll be fighting the top 500 best on PC, Pros, Streamers, Content creators, Kill grinders, Leader board holders. I've introduced countless people to Apex and have watched them drop the game one after another because they simply can't keep up. This game doesn't make it easy. I mean half the time our new players are fighting hackers or smurfs making new accounts to farm them for badges and stats. Unless you're like me and have spent a ridiculous amount of time and money on this game you don't want to lose by simply quitting then I wouldn't recommend playing. If I didn't have so much to lose I would've quit playing so long ago. This is entirely my own experiences and opinion, just know it's a very seasoned opinion. I have played all but one singular season. This game gets worse with time.

review_comment: I have about 5,000 hours in this game (3000 on PS4 and 2000 on PC), and I have watched a game that I love degraded by corporate greed. Slowly over the seasons we saw unique game modes and interesting storylines replaced with collection events aimed at sucking every dollar from the user. Things got worse after their longstanding creative director left and proceeded to decline as Respawn had massive layoffs, despite increasing profits. The new battlepass has solidified the fact that Respawn and EA only care about shareholders and profits rather than creating an enjoyable experience. $40 for 2 premium battlepasses in a single season without the ability to use in-game currency is the epitome of a cash grab, and Respawn has the nerve to say that they're doing this because THE COMMUNITY wants it. This could not be farther from the truth. This has been my favorite shooter since Halo 2 with amazing movement and challenging gameplay. However, I cannot use this to justify playing the game anymore. It is truly a shame.

With the all the hacking, bugs, and the like it's appalling to see them up charge what the average consumer can afford. They still haven't upgraded the tick-rate of servers for smoother performances for players (Apex - 20 hz vs Average Multiplayer - 60 hz) even though the game has been printing money for them with its fun gunplay and movement mechanics inspired by Titanfall, a series anyone had played has adored. I have put nearly 3,900 hrs into this game (2,200 on Origin, ~1700 on Steam) and I enjoy it dearly even with all its blatant faults, but this is one of the scummiest things they've tried to pull since the Battlefront 2 controversy. EA needs to stop being greedy and focus on improving their systems (in-game and in-office with their executives making financial decisions).

This game is no where near as good as it once was and I pray every night that someone at EA and Respawn sees all these horrible reviews for the game as of recently and decide to revive this game because it genuinely can compete with other battle royale games if the right people get their hands on it.

review_comment: Battle royale as a genre just plain sucks. It feels like the skill floor is very high with this game, and no matter what my squad and I do, we cant survive our first firefight of the match. That only leaves us with ratting till the end zone, but the issue there is that everyone has red armour by then, and we may as well jump off the edge than try and fight a full team of red armour. The game was still fun though, since my squad and I could play arenas, which removed the downtime and looting and only had the good gunplay and cool character abilities. Speaking of cool characters and abilities, you wont ever get to use any of them. It takes TWENTY THREE levels to unlock A SINGLE CHARACTER. With nearly 150 hours on the game ive only unlocked THREE characters aside from the defaults. When the abilities and characters are such a core part of your game it is awful to make it take so long to unlock one. With the removal of the only fun gamemode (arenas) this game is just boring and sad.

review_comment: I have no idea why the suits that run these companies are so tied up with this client side anti-cheat stuff. When it comes to anything security related you're not supposed to trust the client AT ALL, that's what server side checks are for. That's what we've been doing for decades with the internet - don't trust the browser/client, server side check everything. The Finals has proven how effective this is, which has stopped cheaters from using hardware level scripts completely or any other form of local cheats/scripts unless they literally hack into their servers. Other publishers need to take notes, because you're wasting your money whilst you're trying to save your money by making the client as trustworthy as possible; that's just not going to happen.

review_comment: 2000+ Hours on console, 500+ Hours on Origin, 2300+ Hours on Steam. Day 1 Player. I'm glad I only ever spent 10 dollars on this game. Don't really care too much about the battlepass issues, skins and such are cool but never been of much interest to me. It does suck what they are doing but considering its EA, is anyone surprised? The real issue with this game is the cheating. The list of the types of cheats being used in this game is astonishing, and by accounts that are 500+ levels. Every single match, no matter what lobby you go to, has cheating, and not even like 1 person, entire teams fighting each other with cheats. Soft cheats, hard cheats, you name it. They don't even try to hide it. It reminds me of Lance Armstrong's story of how he said he used drugs because everyone was using them and the only way to have fair combat was to doing them yourselves. Apex is literally in that state where people are using cheats just to be on par, can you imagine. The game has never been this bad in terms of cheating, balance, moral, player count or monetisation. Such a shame because the gameplay loop of Apex is still the best there is, it can definitely be better, but none of the other shooters feel as good, however if you can't even enjoy that anymore, there is nothing left. I doubt anyone from Respawn actually plays their own game or even cares anymore. I think the time has come for this game to be given to a different studio, one that is fresh with joy and wants to do well with Apex. A new studio should build the game from the ground up on Unreal Engine, and build internal anti cheat mechanics, and not replay on easy Anti Cheat and the like. It's the only way to combat the current state of the game. However the good news is, the core game itself is so bad now, for the first time in years, I genuinely don't feel like playing it. I actually want to thank the cheaters and devs for not caring, it's what I needed to leave for good. This game isn't good for anyone's health, even if you have a good life, this game will do everything it can to ruin it, and that's when its working well. It's been fun, had some great moments, got some mad clips, will definitely remember the good times but will also remember the lack of respect and care from both the players you encounter and the devs, and their tactics. It's time to choose health over Apex. Thank you.

review_comment: I'm just done. I've had enough. I have over 1k hours (99,99% solo queue), 500+ wins, 10k kills and I really enjoy the core game mechanics and gameplay. I have played the game for a couple of years, and I didn't plan to quit because I enjoyed improving at the game and I love watching ALGS. But I've just had enough. I'm just tired of EA and Respawn not dealing with the big problems in the game. The same problems that have been there for years now and just gets worse and worse. The final drop in the bucket for me was the changes to the battle pass. It made me lose the last enthusiasm I had for this game. It just made me not want to play anymore. I will never pay 10$ twice a season and not even once. I don't really care about skins and would never just buy one in the store, but stuff like battle pass with unlocks and stuff just makes it so that you have something extra to grind for. The 4k coins I have feel kinda worthless to me now that I can't use it for battle pass. You must be stupid to give EA 10$ or 20$ every split for what they provide. This is what they choose to do when cheaters are rampant in every mode, the matchmaking is trash, solo queue is hell and ranked system is just not it. There are so many cheaters now at every level and in every mode. The full-on cheats and so so many "soft" cheats and especially the "soft" cheats is ruining the game. There are so many with wall hacks and/or soft aimbot now it makes you doubt so many of the fights you have. And when there is so many cheaters it just ruins the game. You stop wanting to improve because you are not playing against other players, you are playing against cheats. So this is it for me. I will continue to watch and enjoy, ALGS but I will not be playing this game anymore at this time. If things have changed in a month or two I might check back in, but I've lost hope. At the core this is a great game, but it's just so misshandled and neglected, and so has also the communty and playerbase been. This game has become too EA. I'm sad to go, but enough is enough. Peace out

review_comment: With Apex Legends being one of the prime free battle royals of the last decade, they didn't get this position by mere chance. With Titanfall being the IP this game is set in, the weapons and set pieces make it a very familiar title to those that have played the previous games. The gun-play and movement are fun, fast-paced and clean for those who enjoy longer TTK shooters. With any multiplayer game it does have some issues with balancing characters but for the most part the devs keep it mostly under control (This is only my personal experience). While playing with friends is the best way to go, I have enjoyed plenty of solo sessions as well. At the end of the day this is a battle royal through and through, so from its core there is nothing super unique about the game from that aspect. However the Legends and game play keep it above the seemingly endless sea for free-2-play BR's out there on the market. Whether you enjoy shooters from a casual perspective or you enjoy a test of skill. Whether you are seeking a trio to win or go after self-glory, this game has plenty to offer.

review_comment: I can say for sure that this is definitely one of my favorite battle royale games by far, in the top 3 for sure. This game was just perfect in every possible way, honestly speaking I don't even know what they could've made better. The guns, the movement, the map, the new stuff they add, just everything about Apex Legends was so good. The first time I played it was on the exact release date (Feb 4, 2019) on my PS4, and I played it with my cousin. We decided to play in groups of three so we could get some help to win since we were new to the game. Surprisingly, our first game matched us with someone who was already pretty good at the game, even though it was the first day it was ever launched. He totally carried us to victory, no joke. Me and my cousin only got like 1 kill each, and we ended up winning our first game on the first release day, which is still crazy to me. I'm grateful I got to play most of the seasons, especially the OG ones. I loved it a lot, including the Hemlock, which is one of my favorite guns in the whole game. Honestly, I can't complain except for the fact that your account isn't the same on PS4 or PS5 or any other platform you play on. I played on PS4 for a long time and had so many cool skins, battle pass stuff, and gun wraps. My account was fully maxed out until I switched to PC. Even though I used the same EA account, it took me to a new account on PC. It basically had nothing on it, like starting over again. It got me really annoyed and frustrated, but I managed to grind a bit more and almost maxed it out again. I really wish I could play this game more. Also, I don't like that there isn't a solo mode. I kinda get why, but sometimes playing with random people can be really annoying. But again, I can't complain because most games aren't as good as Apex Legends. I honestly recommend anyone to play this game, though I suggest playing it with a friend or family member, just anyone you can talk to. Overall, it's a great game and definitely beats most shooter games like Fortnite, Warzone, PUBG, and the rest. This is just my opinion and if you disagree, that's okay. I hope you find this review useful!
name: Apex Legends

review_comment: With over 600 hours on different platforms and accounts and still playing, I won't ever recommend Apex Legends to a new player unless they are a Titanfall fan and a former fella Pilot trying to find redemption in the Apex games. The game has various problems such as : Terrible Servers which are 20 tic! even roblox has 60 tic servers- A cheater problem for years, Aim hacking and wall hacking has been around for as much as i remember and the third problem is the terrible matchmaking not allowing new players to play with other new players, instead they get in a lobby with 3 stack preds and masters and die immediately. Apex shines when it comes to movement, character design and universe (After all anything titanfall related is fun) and the feel of guns and abilities. My relationship with this game is a toxic, LoveHate one. when the servers are good, the matchmaking is good and there are no cheaters to be seen, the game gives peak enjoyment but unfortunately that is a rare sight to behold. in the end, Apex is a terrible place for a new player specially solo ones but if you can fight through all the problems, there might be fragments of a good game within this hot mess to see and enjoy.
name: Apex Legends

review_comment: Used to be a great game, still is to an extent but the playerbase has all but left this game in the dust. Great mechanics and the character variety is excellent but the developers have been focused on monetizing everything and making money instead of improving the game. The shield system rework wasn't the greatest and a lot of the new character abilities aren't as fun and unique as the new characters up until Seer really felt. After that they became almost reskins to the older characters with slightly different mechanics and damn near copies of other games. Lots of reworks have been recently done as attempts to save the game but they are clearly rushed and more often than not aren't what the playerbase wanted. Ironically, Titanfall 2 servers have been packed as opposed to Apex Legends servers which really shows what the community wants from EA but I doubt anything will be done of it. If you haven't played the game yet, I wouldn't recommend it as it's not what this game used to be and it's now just a money pit until the servers are shut down and something else is made.

review_comment: I have uninstalled - and subsequently reinstalled - this game 3 times in the last 48 hours. I have added the game to my "ignore" list, removed it from my library, all in an attempt to save my sanity. Yet, here I am, typing a review as I await the re-installation of 70+GB of pure pain and suffering. This game is fantastic but it remains the most humbling experience I have ever had. The level of skill required to be consistently good at this game can only be attributed to some kind of demonic deal, a soul exchange, a dance with the devil. I thought I was decent at games, yet, now as I approach 30 years of age, I find myself screaming at the PC, depressed, questioning the very meaning of my existence. The graphics and art style are not my cup of tea, the community is poisonous, the micro-transactions are borderline predatory (see what I did there?) When it's good it makes you feel like a King amongst men, but when it's bad, it's worse than chewing broken glass whilst having red hot iron forced through your eyelids. The game is free, but I have spent over £1000 on it and I plan to spend more. 10/10

review_comment: Iv'e been playing Apex since season 0 and have well over 5k hours in the game. (Ex PS4 player, hours wont show on steam obviously). This game is truly at its core one of the best FPS on the market. Despite a lot of negativity, so much has changed and been introduced to the game to keep it fresh and moving over the last 5 years. There are issues, audio/networking/cheaters etc. But overall, this is still the only FPS that makes me want to boot up after work. I dont want to go into a lengthier review or start a fight over the state of Apex. Just wanted to lend some positivity from someone who loves the game. iv'e made so many new friendships through this game. The E-Sports side of Apex is fun as hell. And if you follow some of the individual devs on twitter, they really do care about the game. So do we. I hope only the best for the game moving forwards.

review_comment: Alright, I like this game, it's fun, but only because it's new and I play with friends. This game has a few serious issues which makes me want to not recommend this game. It's a headache to run, from constant crashes every 1-2 games to facing infinite loading screens fro hours on end, the amount of bugs I've tried to fix are endless, and pretty much none of them are on my end. I've checked, trust me. The issues are Apex specific, they never happen with another game, and if not for friends, I would not have touched this game. This game feels less playable than cyberpunk at launch, that's how bad it can be. Of course I've managed to fix some issues, but there's always some other issue which I end up facing. Plus EA literally collects data on you in game. I am not kidding I have spent at least 10 hours trying to get in and be able to play the game rather than playing. I will probably continue to play this game for a bit before I fully quit it but I can't really recommend it to anyone, as of now, it's been a net negative experience. There is also the matter of fact that cheaters are ridiculously rampant to the point that I'm most likely getting cheaters in silver lobbies, and if they're not cheaters, if I'm wrong, then they are not silver players, which makes playing competitive not fun. These same cheaters can have remote control access to your computer and download potential viruses on your computer while playing the game. Do you want to know one of the fixes to make this game work? Turn off your antivirus and firewall as they may be interfering with Apex Legends.

My BRAND NEW FRIEND shared his scree while playing and got killed 8 times in a row to people over level 300 in a lobby that only should have been for new players. Not only is this game becoming a money suckling degenerate camp but it is also no longer player friendly. To speak on my own behalf, no matter how much I train, how long I play, or how hard I try, I almost always find myself dying to someone that has no business playing against a level 100. Not to mention the cheating problem in this game. There is little to no consequence to downloading a cheat client and booting it up for the ranked grind then selling the account. All EA cares about is making the next $300 heirloom slightly acceptable enough to not lose the remaining half of their fan-base. If EA doesn't do something that is beneficial to the average player and makes the game genuinely more fun or adds something that the people actually want, I can confidently say that this game will die alongside greedy Call of Duty and Fortnite; two games that became too focused on the money and cosmetics, not on game content or play-ability.

I have pretty decent mid-range laptop (GTX1660ti, 16Gb ram, SSD, Core I5-10300H) and it's not working with current version of game. Year ago, no problem, normal loading speeds, normal game play (crashes did happen, but it was negligible compared to now). Now, menu takes veeery long time to load, sometimes it doesn't load correctly even after hour, when you get in the game it crashes very often, especially in ranked mode (lucky if you can play 2-3 games in row, it just crashed a lot, beggining, mid, or at the end of game, it seems to work ok, no lag, and suddenly boom, it's down, it is impossible to rank up, you win 2 games and lose it all when it crashes) other game modes seems to be a bit better. Then there is imput lag, sometimes it's fine, but those time are less and less often, aiming works but movement, it moves nearly 1second after you stopped holding movement controlls. Shame, because new updates bring lot of content that seems to be fun, if it worked, new content is great, but developers forgot the most important thing- to make the game actually work! Shame that it worked better when it first came out, after 3 years it came from great game with bit of lacking content to unplayable not working game with lot of content (which is then useless if you cannot play). Had a lot of fun playing it but I think, the time has come to move on.

review_comment: Imagine owning a franchise longer than the original owners and still not understanding what the actual soul of the franchise is. Started off with a bunch of potential but still fumbling it time and time again. Always one step forward, two steps back with each update. This game was a huge step in the right direction when it first released, returning to the art style and gameplay of the older games with a modern take. The weapon sandbox though is abysmal. Why do Halo 2 and 3 have a more diverse sandbox than this game while being almost two decades old? Weapons were fun and interchangeable, what happened? Now, everything is so stiff. The few weapons from the old games that have been brought in feel good but what the hell were 343 thinking with some of the Banished weapons? Fighting mainly Brutes. No Brute Shot. No Brute Plasma Rifle. No Mauler (a BRUTE weapon). but it's okay because we got the "MaNgLer" and the "SkEwEr." So many missing guns that help fill the gaps and make the game actually fun. But no. Instead adding in some BS Fuel Rod Cannon that's just a reskin of the default rocket launcher. The vehicles are just.... why...? Ghost is clunky like the Halo: CE one, and not in a fun nostalgic way. Chopper handles like trying to stand on an oiled up beach ball in the middle of the ocean. Might as well not even use the Banshee. And not only that but having the worst standalone story of the entire franchise that goes absolutely nowhere. By the time you watched the first cutscene, you find out everything interesting has already happened off screen. You get to be Chief, meandering about a Halo ring with no stakes or sense of what the hell is going on. No real prior links or characters to reel you in. Just get to listen to a whiny pilot cry and give him a pat on the shoulder when he's sad. I really wanted this game to succeed. Had hope it'd take off at some point but the only thing it actually has going for it are nice graphics and a good Forge mode, that it took years to release. I can't find any reason to play this game over the old Bungie games. It's just soulless and wants your money. Especially moreso now since they have to have FOMO for the Battle Passes. That was never supposed to be a thing. Hell. No one asked for a Free-to-Play Halo. Don't even bother with this. For a LIVE service game, expect to get one weapon added a year and maybe one singular vehicle during the game's lifespan. But don't worry. In the meantime, you can throw $20 for a singular armor set.... Get real.
name: Halo_Infinite
