review_comment: I've been playing Halo Infinite since launch and the only reason I've stuck with it this long is bc I love the Halo franchise and have been playing all Halo titles extensively since Combat Evolved. This is the worst Halo ever made. It launched with a laughable amount of content and manipulative cosmetic system and 3 years later nothing has changed. 343 should be ashamed of themselves. I just played a tactical slayer match on some unmemorable map of theirs and spawned right in front of enemy players 3 times in a row.... 3 years into this game. I wanted to love it, so badly that I still put hundreds of hours into this title (704 at this posting). Every update I came back just hoping that it would feel less broken. Nope. The matchmaking makes no sense and sucks the fun out of the game, the micro-transactions are ridiculous, the new progression system is unimaginative and repetitive, the social features are near nonexistent, and even the menus are quite plainly the worst of any Halo. Oh and let's not forget that they took every last shred of grit and masculinity out of Master Chief and the UNSC (even if you don't play the campaign just listen to the narration over your mp games) and FOR WHAT?! Was 343 TRYING to ruin the legacy? I even loved Halo 4 and 5, so it really says something when I finally have to face reality and admit that Infinite falls so short. I pray that if another Halo title is in our future that true fans are at the helm.

review_comment: I really enjoyed the campaign, especially the parts of the story that took more of Halo 4 Chief and humanized his character. The first act of the game is one of the best parts of this game's gameplay and the soundtrack is S-tier levels, other than that there are no big set pieces, no feeling of the stakes being raised like the looming threat of the halos being fired like in the older games. You can feel that this game was meant to have so much more but wasn't able to deliver on it. The Multiplayer is an honest joke at this point, There is so (still is) much content missing on day one, to the bad UI design and one of the worst sandboxs this franchise has had. The fact that most of the effect is being put into selling us overprice cosmetics is a massive joke, this game needed to be delayed but yet for some reason, shipped out when it wasn't clearly in a polished state. The future of the franchise doesn't look too promising, if the current development team could pull MCC, I'll happily give this game a 2nd chance but it doesn't seem like such a realistic dream to have. In summary, play the campaign (When it is on sale or on gamepass, because why are you charging for a full-price game if multiplayer is free!!!) it the only 'worth' thing playing.

review_comment: I can't speak for the campaign because I haven't played it, but the competitive (specifically Ranked) multiplayer is smooth and polished; I keep coming back for it because of Halo's uniquely heavy team oriented game-play. The social playlists have also gained a lot of attention by the developers and are currently in a very good state, with rolling updates for the year, customization of game-types and a diverse selection. The forge community and the addition of the custom browser (playing community made maps and modes on an in game browser both for console and PC) are enough creativity and crazy fun to keep you busy indefinitely. This is a completely different game than what was delivered on the initial release date. I believe if the current state of the game was what 343/Halo studios had initially delivered on the release date, Halo Infinite would be one of the top games today. But, it's still here to play and so am I.

review_comment: I really, really wanted to like this game. Truth is, the campaign is conceptually cool but the stability is embarrasingly bad. Barely stuttering through, on a 2070S running at 1080, punctuated by seizure-inducing graphical glitches where the terrain will randomly flicker between black and white. Fiddling with the graphics is about 50/50 - it may help, or it may entirely crash the game. Graphics aren't the only problem. Sometimes you'll exit at a checkpoint, but after relaunching, the game will resume at a completely different location than where you started. Missions seem to restart at the beginning, despite checkpoints, but some mission flags aren't getting cleared. Building shaders can be hit or miss - sometimes it'll work, sometimes it'll crash at 60%, sometimes it'll crash at 98%. Regardless of the current setting, toggling the Steam shader cache (either once, or twice) may occasionally help, for a time. Only Microsoft managers could take a cash cow and run it into the ground this spectacularly.

I was expecting great things since I loved the competitive in Halo 5 with its easy to learn hard to master system. The skill ceiling in that game was pretty impressive. This game, while the player with the better accuracy does win so it is a bit of a skill ceiling, also fails way too hard with server latency making these match-ups way too luck dependent. Did I get put on a west coast server? No? Then I lose 7/10 times. The monetization system was perfect because it was all cosmetic and you could earn everything through just playing the game, or pay for faster unlocks if you wanted. This is the perfect system. Let people pay if they want, don't force them to. TL DR, if you want to play a good Halo game, go back to 5 (skip 4), Reach, 3, or 2. To whomever forced this unbaked product out on to the market 3 years before it was ready, I am severely disappointed in you. review_comment: 90% of these negative reviews should be ignored (the same can be said with many review bombed games, not all). If you have never tried Infinite's multiplayer, or if you haven't tried since launch, PLEASE give it a shot. Feels good, looks good, variety of game modes, good customization, and as far as f2p games go, pretty nice monetization. There's a free pass with some popular armor customization that you can earn from the start, and when a battle-pass comes out you can earn all the rewards for free for a certain amount of time. All previous battle-passes can be bought and played through for $5 - $10 USD depending on the pass, which in my opinion, is incredibly fair, the passes have A LOT of sweet rewards. The $10 Fall of Reach pass really has all the customization most players like me will ever want anyway. If you're looking for a fresh Halo MP experience with a modern feel, this is it.

I will rather be talking about the campaign, gameplay-wise, I think this is the best Halo. The addition of a grapple hook adds such a crazy amount of possibility when it comes to the physics, making most scenarios feel unique. The vehicles also feel fantastic in this entry. Although the gameplay is at its best the story is at its worst, The bulk of the game is clearing bases in an empty open world and then running through endless metal corridors pressing buttons, and finding power cells. The few boss fights in the game were extremely easy including the final one. I played through it since I've played all Halo's and didn't want to leave one out, but I can only recommend the campaign on a deep sale, I think I paid like $20 or something.

review_comment: cons: the story has its ups and downs but ultimately falls flat, why the closure on cortana is good, the endless are just sorta glossed over and not explained at all. The weapons selection is the worst out of all the halo games, most are just slight modifcations of other weapons. Only 3 forrunner weapons this time around, which to be fair are good but not great. The banished stalker rifle over all is a downgrade from the beam rifle when you use it, but jackel snipers will make mince meat out of you. The entire campaign is like the famine skull is always turned on, your weapon ammo is garbage, the shot gun only has 3 mags when it takes on average 3 shots to kill most enemys on heroic, meaning you are starving for ammo constantly. A constant theme in this halo versus others is the enemy weapons do more damage to you than yours ever do to them. Next issue is level design, on paper the High value targets would be fun, but due to poor cover options, most are a slog and not fun. You are supposed to take marines with you, but due to map geography and the fact marines cant teleport to you when you go far away, you will just be soloing most things which is a slog. Lastly off the top of my head the only new vehical is the wasp which is terrible, has low health, its rockets do almost no damage. Couldn't have even brought the mantis back, a grizzly, a cobra, even the gauss hog is absent something that has been in the game since halo 2. This is just a few things, maybe buy it on sale like i did but over all the campaign was the most boring halo by far. Im genuiely confused by 343's decision making for this game.

I like the fact that the Halo team has been giving some of what the community wants, which isn’t common in modern large-scale FPS games. It just seems to be about profit. I’m particularly excited about the direction Forge is taking. review_comment: cons: the story has its ups and downs but ultimately falls flat, why the closure on cortana is good, the endless are just sorta glossed over and not explained at all. The weapons selection is the worst out of all the halo games, most are just slight modifcations of other weapons. Only 3 forrunner weapons this time around, which to be fair are good but not great. The banished stalker rifle over all is a downgrade from the beam rifle when you use it, but jackel snipers will make mince meat out of you. The entire campaign is like the famine skull is always turned on, your weapon ammo is garbage, the shot gun only has 3 mags when it takes on average 3 shots to kill most enemys on heroic, meaning you are starving for ammo constantly. A constant theme in this halo versus others is the enemy weapons do more damage to you than yours ever do to them. Next issue is level design, on paper the High value targets would be fun, but due to poor cover options, most are a slog and not fun. You are supposed to take marines with you, but due to map geography and the fact marines cant teleport to you when you go far away, you will just be soloing most things which is a slog. Lastly off the top of my head the only new vehical is the wasp which is terrible, has low health, its rockets do almost no damage. Couldn't have even brought the mantis back, a grizzly, a cobra, even the gauss hog is absent something that has been in the game since halo 2. This is just a few things, maybe buy it on sale like i did but over all the campaign was the most boring halo by far. Im genuiely confused by 343's decision making for this game.

The game itself isn't extremely difficult or anything (even LASO is the easiest in the game), but the game is entirely unfinished. I had to convince my friend to play with me for the co-op achievements, and they were so bugged it was excruciating. There's a point (at least in LASO) on the last level that will glitch out after one of the hardest altercations in the game and the only way to get through that part is by restarting the whole mission (but again, it's bugged so good luck, it took me three different runs just to be let through without the game breaking and halting my progress). This game is such a buggy mess and it's sad how awful of a development team 343 is, truly. Side note for devs everywhere: STOP MAKING HUNT/GATHER ACHIEVEMENTS (Datapads), NO ONE WANTS OR ENJOYS THOSE. Side note pt2: If all you plan on doing is playing multiplayer, disregard this review because I actually enjoyed the multiplayer (except for the God-awful microtransactions). review_comment: This game continues to disappoint. After years of hoping and praying that 343 could fix their networking issues with a seemingly mechanically good game, they again mess up their networking to a state where it's worse than it was before! I can't say I'm surprised, every single release of new content has broken the game in one way or another. 343, I have completely and totally lost faith in your company and the halo series. I've played halo competitively for years, and this game is by far the biggest disappointment in the series. Every game is either an Iowa server with varying ping from 67ms all the way up to 100ms, the same goes for the texas server which the game seems to pull the other 50% of the time. I've never in my life seen games with servers fluctuating ping so widely and rapidly. 343's latest "networking fix" seems to only making issues worse, and continue to cause a ping disparity. This game seems to only be playable if you live in the correct regions now, which is absurd. It's impossible to be competitive in this game when every game is on an 80+ ping server. I live in the bay area, and ping 10ms to SF server, but I pull that server maybe 1 every 25 games?2 thumbs down 343, your development has been a continuous letdown. Shame on you for ruining such a good series with your lackluster talent acquisition, and choice in Azure servers. Good god this game stinks.

review_comment: I'm not the multiplayer PVP type, so I can only rate the single player. I LOVE the gunplay. Awesome weapons, feel and sound powerful. The world and mission areas are a little one-sided, both in terms of colors and light, so variety would be even better. All in all, I really like the game. The open world gimmicks and things you can collect are fun, but not necessary if you want to play a pure mission run. Story-wise, it's typical Halo, epicness here, a little trash and cliché there, just fine. In view of the last parts, however, the story has been dropped and replaced by virtually no content, even if the connection to the Banished and Atriox from Halo Wars 2 is super cool. The Master Chief has been given a bit more humanity again by, among other things, sympathizing with the enemy, which I really like. ♥♥♥♥ I love Halo, Halo is always good

Very next turn, they forced me to surrender. Yep, I capture their city and they forced me to surrender. This is because of the stupid war support mechanic. Also, while I'm fighting, I learn that one of my cities is under siege by a random army of independent people. I have outposts on all the territories around my city and its on the coast. There is no unoccupied territories on the whole continent. Yet somehow a random army of independent people spawn in with the strongest units available and there is nothing I can do to stop them. Just randomly spawned out of nowhere, awesome. How am I even supposed to deal with that? These two aspects just ruined this game for me and I doubt I'll pick this up again.

review_comment: Half-baked game. There is a lot that is good about this game, but there are a lot of issues that should be easily fixed. There is no grace period after a war, I won a war and the next turn the AI demanded the same territory that we just fought over and I held. I refused (obviously, I won and still had troops available) and they declared war on me (what?, I just crushed him). When they war started I had more war support than him (4 to 2) and I lost the following turn and had to relinquish territories that he didn't demand despite no battles or anything happening. This is an issue apparently that has been around for a long time and the developer has no inclination to fix, this kind of issue that is a core mechanic (war and the aftermath) and continues to persist tells me that the developer has no real inclination to finish or fix the game, they got their money.

review_comment: Long time Civilization game player here. Since Civ I, Age of Empire, as well as Space 4x genre which I have always though of as Civ in Space. Humankind is EXCELLENT. Every bit as good as Civ VI, and better in many ways. The transition between cultures is very fun, and truly allow you to shore up your strategy as the game unfolds. Victory Points are forever, and the in this game they are achievement stars - you always know what you could be doing to get closer to winning. This is very well done, and a feature that ever player of the genre will admire. Combat is tactical, or automated. I find I can usually do a little better than the automation, so when it really matters I will control combat. The only cons: unfortunately, like Civ... it can get a bit boring near the end of the game, when you are clearly crushing everyone - but the conditions must be met.

review_comment: Instead, the rotating cast of cultures means everyone feels much the same, everyone changes quickly, and you don't have the same investment in the game. Do I care that Red and Blue are at war? I probably should, but only if it means one has more "Fame", whatever the heck that is. There's nothing quite like the feeling of teching up only to run into a roadblock where you can't get enough Fame stars for the next era, and instead watch Green run away with the game because they took three cities instead of two. It could have been really fun to see Zhou go into Ming or Han, then Edo or Viet, then China or Japan, but no; everyone can go anywhere, and often it feels like the game was decided a hundred meaningless moves ago. At least in Civ I have an actual character to yell at when they take my city location instead of some knock-off Mii.
name: HUMANKIND

review_comment: In conclusion, while Civilization 6 has long been a staple in the strategy gaming community, Humankind emerges as a worthy contender, if not a superior successor. With its innovative mechanics, diverse civilizations, stunning visuals, and refined AI, Humankind sets a new standard for the genre. Whether you're a seasoned strategist or a newcomer to the genre, Humankind offers an unparalleled experience that's sure to keep you coming back for more. Amplitude Studios has truly outdone themselves with this masterpiece, and I eagerly anticipate what the future holds for this incredible game.

review_comment: I was slow to warm up to this game. As someone who has more hours in Civ V than any other game and also loved Endless Space 2 - this is in many ways a natural fit: the beautiful art design and resource system of ES2 fused onto a Civ V superstructure. Add some advancements in diffuse city building / regional map control and it makes an interesting mix. However it took a couple of tries for me to really engage with the game - but once it did, oh boy. I only really play a full Humankind every couple months, because I find it so acutely time consuming that it feels more like an irresponsible drug bender than reasonable engagement with a benign pastime. For that reason I kind of resent Humankind - but in other ways I love it. I honestly think I will just stick with Humankind for the foreseeable future instead of jumping to Civ VII. If my perspective sounds like yours, you may want to do the same!

review_comment: For fans of 4x nation builder games, this turn-based strategy game is a refreshing take. The mechanics of victory and progress are distinct enough to allow for genuinely different approaches to achieve your victory - first, while still building on a lot of the standard resource and opportunity cost principles. The expansions all add distinct and engaging optional additions to a well-developed game, adding possible complexities and variables, that force new strategies and approaches as the game progresses. While some mechanics will require you to grow familiar, and they still haven't bothered to make the AI actually engaging to play against, the game is quite fun and a great addition to the 4x genre.

review_comment: The approach to empire development is much better in this game in my opinion, it feels less gamey and rather takes a more immersive approach where your decisions create a foundation for your future decisions. Specialization and spearheading wide or tall strategies are satisfying once you've got a hang of the basic mechanics. I've had games where i funnel resource to a capital city using outposts and smaller cities, building a tall super city. Then I've had other games where I've focused grabbing as much territory as possible with no one city being particularly strong. All in all the game is much more immersive and compelling to me than Civ has been to me in the past. I'm now addicted to the game flow of Humankind.

review_comment: Really enjoyable game. I've played all of the Civs, starting with good old Civ I, and Humankind deserves a good spot within that lineage. The culture thing (that you change culture at every age) seems to be the big thing that most Civvers don't like, but I don't mind it. What I truly enjoy though is that the game is more focused on gameplay than having to read pages and pages of information to make a decision every few turn (Civ VI anyone?). Some Civvers complain about the city cap - but I find that really refreshing, I hate having to pick the same construction in 25 cities in Civ when I make a new discovery. Overall this is a really nice entry and a refreshing take into the genre. Highly recommended if you want a bit of variety from Civ.

review_comment: A somewhat fresh take on the 4X strategy genre. You build a civilization that evolves by blending different cultures across eras. So, in the Stone Age you're Egyptians, in the Bronze Age you switch to Hettites, and in the Dark Age you roll with Teutons, and so on. This mix-and-match approach keeps gameplay quite exciting and your strategy adaptable as each nation comes with certain bonuses and spceial troops. City-building is also deep, with cities that can grow by absorbing adjacent territories. Battles are round-based tactical. Diplomacy allows to respond to your actions with a grievance system. Overall, a great game if you enjoy city and empire builder games.

UI is customizable. I prefer this to the other 4x games that seem to have that outdated looking hard shading detail and I wish the newer ones like Millenia looked like this. The music is great. Combat is aweome, you can have full control, or simulate it if you want. You can even import and make your own maps with the map creator if you like, it's like a sandbox, it is very fun to build maps sometimes and it's easy to do. You can create an in-game persona and I found that to be very immersive and it encourages role-play. it was easy to learn, I learned the controls quickly. Art style, combat, music are huge positives.

Next gen is still behind PC capability so please fix these issues, i bought this game without reading reviews because i have been buying since the beginning, lets address these issues. review_comment: I don’t usually write reviews, but I had to warn everyone about NBA 2K25. After waiting hours for the game to install, I was excited to dive into MyCareer... big mistake. It was an absolute disaster from start to finish. First off, the gameplay was terrible. The controls felt clunky, the animations were stiff, and the game just didn't feel polished at all. MyPlayer progression felt like a grind, with no real fun factor. You spend hours just trying to build your character, only to hit roadblocks that feel more like money grabs than actual gameplay challenges. It's clear that the game is more focused on pushing microtransactions than providing a satisfying experience. And don’t get me started on the crashes. As a PC player, I had constant crashes. No matter what settings I tried or updates I installed, the game would just randomly crash. It got to the point where I couldn’t even finish a game without it freezing or closing out entirely. AVOID if you're on PC — it's borderline unplayable. I gave it 2 hours and 46 minutes of gameplay before I had enough and requested a refund. It was that bad. After spending so long installing the game, I couldn’t believe how quickly I just wanted it gone. I’ve been a fan of the series for years, but NBA 2K25 was a total letdown. Save your time and money. Don’t buy this mess.

review_comment: 2K25... What can I say that people don't already know about it. I mean it is just a disappointment. I get off of work everyday at 6PM. As a plumber by the way. Then I get to come home and have my wife yell at me to change my kid's diapers. Finally I call my two old friends from high school and tell them, "You know what guys let's try 2K25" Because I remember as kids we enjoyed the 2k3 and 4 versions. Anyway I put down 60 dollars to buy the game and my friends do too. After getting our builds together and thinking we are ready we head to PARK mode. We make our way to the pads to start our first park match and size up our opponents. Then, my friend, Terrance points out the other guys are all 90 Overall + and we are just 60s. But, no problem, that shouldn't make too much of an issue... right? Well we get into the game and the other team gets the ball immediately. They pass the guy my other friend, Bobby is guarding and the guy is about 7 Foot 2 but he easily out-maneuvers Bobby's point guard he built, breaking his ankles. Then knowing the fundamentals I am in help and try to contest the big-man. Of course as a 6'7 forward this was a bad choice and being a 60 overall my character can get a grand total of 2 inches off the ground meanwhile the 7'2 GIANT flies in like Michael Jordan and annihilates my character. The rest of the game went like this. And the next ones after that. So, we decide to try to upgrade our characters because it shouldn't be that hard. We quickly figure out that VC upgrades characters and set our goals to getting it, we also noticed you can buy it with real life money. But, why would we need that? We already spent 60$ dollars on the game right? Then for about a week my friends and I get off work grind VC, repeat. Finally at the end of our grinding we discover we are all around 85 overall. So we make our way to the park believing that our skill can make up for the little overall we are missing. But we quickly realize we don't really like our characters anymore after trying them out. But we continue playing, We grinded for a reason. We get into a couple of matches where we quickly realize everybody makes their shot. EVERYTIME. Green everytime. I mean come on 2K when we played it was not like that. And with that we left the game. So if I could give this game a star review it would be 1 and if I could give 0-5 it'd be 0. The end. Never again. I download 2K just to get away the bunch of crap I have to deal with in real life and I have to deal a mountain of ♥♥♥♥ in the game... Just great.

review_comment: I play offline. I like to play Sandbox style in MyNBA. Playing against the computer has always been horrific.. and somehow its gotten worse. You have NO control over your own players. Like literally none. Your players are SLUGGISH and unresponsive. Open man under the basket, press pass, the animation is so slow and sluggish, the computer easily steps in front and steals it. Maneuvering your player has never felt worse. Just dribbling around the court, your player is going in directions you don't want them to, you get stuck in simple dribbling animations, that you can be pulling back on your left stick for literal seconds before your player even steps in the direction you are pulling. Off-ball ball screens suck your players into them. It could be a point guard setting an Floppy screen, you'll get sucked in the animation and they get open every time without fail. The reverse is not true, your shooters seldom get open when running plays. The difficulty is just lazy and has always been lazy. There is this invisible, never spoken about difficulty slider that just kicks in out of no where. Randomly your players feel like they're running i sand, pass animations are slower, player stamina gets worse, speed gets worse, etc. in an attempt to simulate difficulty. Instead of making the players perform better, opponents play better, they run plays, they attack more, they have more aggressive tendencies, they just make your team 10 attribute points worse across the board. The hardest difficulty should be the most fun. It should be the most realistic. But instead its just tunes how ridiculous the game is going to be. If you're up by 6 in the fourth, winning that game is next to impossible. The computer will end up cheesing you. Not because they earn it, by being smart dynamic AI with real logic, no, your players will randomly jump at passes putting them out of position so they can get an easy layup. Next time down the court you'll come off a ball screen with your 92 overall pg and go for a pull up and he will lose the ball in a contact animation. They will then come down the court and hit a three, and then another three, and then another three. Until your lead has vanished and you are now down by 6. WITHOUT fail. I like basketball, I like building teams and playing a game every now and then, so I buy 2K. But it has not improved other than graphically. It has never been worse. I cannot believe I sent $90 on this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. I have dreams of playing a game next to the people who built this garbage just to point out the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and see them try to justify it. This game is clearly the result of late stage capitalism. This should be criminal.

review_comment: Constant freezing, computer blue-screens, forced easy anticheat (Which I believe is causing many crashes etc) for "online" features such as mycareer, even if you have no intention to play anything online. Menus taking way too long to load for such simple features (even with strong computer hardware). Poor simulation accuracy in many instances, rigged ai (to compensate for poor ai), many features working only about 15% of the time on a good day (such as NBA start today MyLeague, downloading custom team designs etc...), still terrible support for key board key-binds (where things like editing player tendencies are such necessary changes to mimic realistic simulation, you'd think having a keyboard would mean you could easily type the values, or use pg up and pg down keys etc to quickly alter values, same thing goes for negotiating player/coach contracts). Coaching system still is terrible and has no consistent tangible value. Alterations to offensive/defensive formations on the time out screen are dependent on which team calls timeout for some reason still, ie offensive changes can only be made you take a timeout on offense, defensive changes can only be made on the whim of CPU taking a timeout at a time you wish to make adjustments (this issue has been present for at least 2 games now). AI gets every foul call where you get seemingly none, defenders on the players team's speed gets throttled as soon as the game decides its time a cpu player to get a bucket. CPU will get perfect shot and dribble animations to completely cancel out player defense, where player animations get the opposite. Shot meter and timing changes are awful and I've switched to playing purely real player %. Player AI has no concept of off-ball movement or spacing on offense, which makes it really easy for CPU to defend your whole team even when conceptually at disadvantage, meanwhile player AI on defense has no concept of proper help defense strategy and will entirely ignore manual coaching changes made to try and fix the issue. Modern offensive strategies such as guards screening for other guards is almost impossible to configure to happen in real life (as the only possible screeners are C/PFs when manually calling for screen). When creating a new MyLeague, they forgot to include the option to import settings, so you have to import your custom settings AFTER the season has already started which is really annoying. Real life strategies often are almost entirely impossible to replicate in game because the extreme balancing changes that have been done to prevent PvP cheesing (such as deep 3's, DHO's, cutting). Switching AI is INCREDIBLY slow and they somehow made it worse than previous gen ai. Historical rosters are a joke. Essentially no creativity available for offensive or defensive schemes. Every game and team composition feels the exact same without wildly altering player sliders(which are very difficult to understand in many cases). Player progression and Training has been entirely gutted. Allstar festivities still suck and are boring. Post season things are still flat and meaningless. Player farewell-tours are unnoticeable. Every aspect, from game stability, in-game gameplay, season simulation, player customization of team strategy, and every other facet of this game, are somehow worse than ever. Absolute pathetic excuse of a leadership team - the programmers, animators, and everyone else deserves better than these rushed corporate BS releases. Please will another company step in to compete with the fools in charge of 2k.

review_comment: Generally a pretty solid 2k game, and they actually updated PC to use the next-gen (current at this point?) version of the game which is greatly appreciated. There were/are a few bugs that could be pretty frustrating such as hearing the opponents in rec which led to griefing (patched), and the ever prevalent issue of the shot meter randomly resetting between games. However, as long as you have just a slight degree of vigilance, that's fairly manageable. My biggest issues are with some parts of the structure of the game itself, that is, the rep system and the cost of builds. For me to even hit Vet II for my reputation, I was well over 1000 hours into the game, and that really just isn't attainable for a vast number of player. I understand gatekeeping some of the higher ranks and associated rewards to players who are committed to the game, but it also makes it that much harder to play literally anything else when you need to have such a crazy high time commitment to reach what appears to be just past the middle of the rep rank system. As for the builds in this game, there is a lot of freedom in terms of what you can do, and cap breakers make that even more true. To some extent, you have a much greater ability to make a true superstar than you have had for probably the past decade of 2k games. However, the prevalence of things like cap breakers and more diverse builds also make it a lot easier to fall into the trap of wanting many MyCareer builds. Having many options to choose from may seem nice, but upgrading each of them costs about 100$ to max out, and getting the VC to upgrade players without purchasing it is unsustainable. Regardless, the biggest concern I had when I switched from console to PC 2K was whether or not there would be a large enough playerbase to consistently find games and also the prevalence of hacking in the community. I can happily say that hackers have been few and far between in this rendition, and while they of course do exist, I only run into them online in probably 1/20-1/25 games. At the beginning of the year, this was probably closer to 1/100-1/150, but I have been okay with this ratio anyways. As for the concerns with the playerbase, I have also been happily surprised. I am usually able to get into a game in just a few minutes, with notable exceptions being when it's extremely late at night/earlier morning (2 AM - 8:30 am ish). The park usually has one lobby still active and running during this time (It's always Rise), but as a Rec player, I know that I can't find games in that window. As a whole, the game is a fairly solid 2k and definitely the one that I have put the most hours into, but it has a few flaws in terms of 2k being fairly money hungry (which is nothing new) and some minor flaws related to it being the PC version of a primarily console game community.

review_comment: I have been an NBA 2K consumer since Allen Iverson was on the cover without missing a year but as of the last 5-8 years I have continually been disappointed and a saddened by the state of the franchise I have spent my time, money, and energy on for decades. The unfortunate reality is that the game continues to be a micro transaction plagued mess in most game modes. Modes like MyPlayer and MyTeam are quite literally unplayable without spending money and every year VC grows in inflation. The seasons system is predatory and further forces you to have to either spend money or invest an unreasonable amount of time in order to keep up with the folks that pay. The gameplay has always been solid so I have no complaints in that department. MyNBA/Eras is the mode I have been playing the most for the past few years but since that mode doesn't make 2K any money they invest little energy to improve and refine the mode as much as they could. Overall I have only been buying the game when it is substantially discounted for the reasons stated above. I hope for the future sake of the franchise that they find a compromise between making their stockholders money and delivering a solid product to their consumers. So far they have only delivered on the former.

review_comment: Nigh unplayable. Offline at least. Your "Teammates" (all star calibre players even) will keep losing assignments and will constantly have poor positioning on both offence and defence. Offensively, your open 3 pt shooter will constantly either stand 5 feet away from the 3 pt line, or will run up to another teammate so that one opposite player is guarding 2 of your own. AI knows how to "rubberband" past a decent defensive effort, while offensively, you'll "yoyo" in the most unrealistic way until you get a sliver of day light, but your teammates will again squander that through poor positioning and movement. There is nothing realistic about this game. Kudos on making a ton of animations, this isn't Dota, I don't have another puberty to give away to learn how each and every animation works, and without that, and the constantly switching players on Defence to "correct" a mistake every 2 seconds, this game is unplayable. At which point you aren't playing. You're juggling a falling pile of trash. I play games to make moves, not to be dictated what the ai wants to me to do. The gameplay is so so reactionary. And the ability to make a move is so so restricted. You start dribbling in this game, and your teammates will legit come and stand next to you. I'm like "how do I explain to you good sir, that I'm trying to create separation?" Even during iso, 4 seconds of daylight. Then again the same thing. Why do I have to watch videos by other youtube creators, download sliders and settings, fix the contracts, and the progression, the spacing, the defensive and offensive settings, and then learn player animations, to play a basketball game? What's your job then? We added animations! Swell, you got real life players to wear sensors and move for you. I can't in good conscience give you credit for a bang up job with just that. And why does the coaching staff keep clipping into each other? Did you run out of development budget? Didn't use to clip in previous games, whats so special in 2k25? In case you (developers) guys legitimately wanted a list of things to fix. In case you guys were actually sitting around thinking "I can't figure out why people don't like our game more?" Well I've given you plenty of things that you can improve free of charge. Paid for a product, and helped improved, as if it were my job. I see why you guys close game servers every 3 years and stop with the updates. Because the demand would be a lot a lot less. I'd rather stick with a basketball game that works as close to as intended, than go through this cycle every year. And since I won't get a game like that, because it's far far away from your own interests, I can confidently tell you guys that I'm done playing. I feel used, playing this game has been such a bad experience. I hope the team behind 2k gets their just desserts. I hope other games, by better developers show up so that fans of basketball can enjoy themselves. Somebody who isn't all obsessed with their bottomline so much more than they are with the quality of their products.

review_comment: For the most part, NBA 2K25 was the right time for PC players to get back into NBA 2K. The game runs on Next Gen already, meaning if I got it right, a PC player can now play online with a console player. However, I have one huge bit of negative feedback about the game. I've been playing for quite some time now and I've noticed that every so often, the game falls into these periods where a glitch comes out. I call them boomerang passing. The pass doesn't get completed from the passer to the intended receiver. Instead, the ball boomerangs back to the passer. Because of this, the game becomes mostly unplayable. Inbound passes become out of bounds violations, the shot clock runs out because the NPC can't pass it back to the PC. And some shots go wild because they boomerang back to the shooter. Lately I've noticed this glitch come up whenever the game gets an update - the end of a Season, holiday updates (Halloween and, now, Christmas). I've asked a friend who has the game on a console and he hasn't experienced anything like what I described. I hope 2K is able to address this, or at least provide a solution for us non-console gamers. I mean, 2K has already banned my surname from use as a MyPlayer surname for some reason, and now the game isn't playable at times.

A lot of the technical issues that have riddled recent releases (2K23, 2K24) are much less frequent, after 35 hours of play, the game has only crashed twice, that is a win in my book. The game just feels right again to me when I play, shades of 2K20 right. IDK, I am not going to write a novel about how I feel about a game, I just wanted to give some credit where it is due to a game that takes more beatings then just about every other one, even though most of it is warranted.

Anytime I try to traverse from the tunnel to the court to play the next game in MyCareer, the game seems to be loading and then the audio starts stuttering and then makes my steam deck crash. The text is also blurry but that is fixable. The city on the steam deck also stutters as well but doesnt cause a crash. I am hoping in a couple of weeks this will be fixed but we shall see I guess. As for right now if you have a desktop and love NBA/WNBA or basketball in general I recommend the game. If you have a steam deck, I would hold off until it gets the verified status.

review_comment: With well over 5,000 hours in MapleStory, it has never been more clear that the developers are willingly disconnected from the players. The most recent event is the epitome of this behavior. While game development will always have its challenges, the game studio should have clear communication in regards to serious issues that affects 99% of the players who choose to participate in timed content (MapleStory relies hard on daily log in rewards and timed content). Changes are not reasonable to happen overnight or even within the same patch, but to leave the community in the dark without acknowledging, addressing, or simply expressing the steps they are taking behind the scenes is a slap in the face. If you look at the actions this company takes in similar situations, you will notice no communication until after players have lost out or invested time into content that they simply can not succeed in. At best they will post some statement about how sorry they are and offer some compensation that usually is so disconnected from what the players want or value equivalent to the frustration caused. review_comment: Quite an interesting game. Counter Strike 2 is a, if not, THE original shooter game that kickstarted many other popular video games. It consists of two teams, Terrorists and Counter Terrorists, going against each other and trying to complete an objective (whether it's killing each other or planting the bomb). The mechanics are simple-- Look, aim, and shoot. But the skill ceiling is quite high, which makes this game unique and is a huge factor why it's still kicking even after all these years, If you're looking to play for fun... Don't. Only 53 hours in myself and I slam my desk in frustration because an AWPer hits a noscope. But if you're looking for a challenge where you're willing to put in the months at getting better at this shooter game, I'd recommend it! Go and by Counter Strike 2, lad.

review_comment: I am a 15 yo teen, probably one of the youngest people playing this game. I am a single offspring to my father, who is 45 now. My dad got this game for Christmas in 2021 from his mom, so he installed it on his computer and he started playing. By the end of the week he had 24 hours on this game. This was horrible for me, as it was already hard for me to find ways to spend time with my dad, as he is always out with his friends or just watching YouTube. So i decided to make a Steam account and get this game to see if I could maybe play alongside him. I loaded into the game, picked my character and world and started playing but I was stuck on what you where supposed to do. I asked my dad for help and he hosted a game for me to join. I loved it as it was the best time I had spent with my dad since my cat had died. This game has ever since brought me and my dad closer again and now we actually spend time together outside the house together as well. This game reminded me that there's fun to be had in everything, and it has brought both me and my father many happy memories.

Blizzard, unfortunately, gave up on the "producing good products" portion, and just want to psychologically manipulate their consumers to maximize profit without providing content worthy of such profit. Then, when the dead horse stops spitting out money, they may finally offer things that they deliberately held onto for years in spite of high demand, solely to get one final surge of revenue before scrapping the game for the next project. review_comment: I don't leave negative reviews because I only use the review system to praise games that I like, but man this game deserves the hate it gets. The first Overwatch was an amazing game that me and my friends used to play constantly. Then the company thought it would be a good idea to delete that game and replace it with this much worse version of it and label it a sequel, advertising a cool looking PVE mode that they would later down grade into being lame, and now it's being said that it may be dropped entirely. Overwatch 1 was Game Of The Year in 2016 and they still thought it would be a good idea to get rid of it. I only play Overwatch 2 when my friends want to play it, everything I enjoy is all just stuff from the first game, the new stuff is either bad or I just don't care enough to use. There are cosmetics in this game that cost more than some Triple A games out there, meanwhile we used to be able to get all of this stuff for free in OW1, either with loot boxes or in game currency that you didn't spend real money for. Yes, you could buy loot boxes, but they were easy to get and actually rewarded you for playing the game and winning. Now loot boxes are gone entirely and they've been replaced with a shop that requires real money and a Battle Pass where you have to pay to get the good stuff.

review_comment: I love Overwatch, this is my favorite FPS of all time. I have been playing this game since 2017 consistently, even through the worst metas, and the no updates for months. I have been here through the ups and the downs. I played the last day of OW1 and the first day of OW2. I state all this to show that my review does not come from a place of hate, but a place of love for this game. They have been updating this game and bringing new life into it once again, but all that glitters it not gold. Arguably the best season of OW2 was the first, as they removed stuns, but they choose to give the new characters hinders and knock backs abilities. This has made the game so incredibly un-fun for the tank role which kills half the player base. Also, you have to find a group of OW lovers to play with as this game is miserable for solo q'ers. For these reasons I do not recommend this game, when these things get fixed I will change my review. Overall, we are taking a big step in the right direction every update, which gives me hope for OW2.

review_comment: As a longtime Overwatch player, I've watched the game evolve (or devolve, depending on your perspective) over the years. Overwatch 2 was supposed to be the fresh start we all needed, a chance to revitalize a beloved franchise. Unfortunately, while it brought some exciting new features and heroes, it also introduced changes that alienated many long-time fans. The shift to a 5v5 format, while strategic, felt rushed and unbalanced. The monetization model, while understandable in today's gaming landscape, has created a sense of entitlement among some players. Despite these drawbacks, Overwatch 2 still offers a fun and fast-paced multiplayer experience. However, it's hard to shake the feeling that the game has lost some of its magic.

review_comment: As much as I sometimes get addicted to the game I cant recommend it in the state its in. The developers dont seem to have love for it anymore and it feels half finished. So many overpowered characters while other characters who were fine get reworked. Some characters need intense skill to do anything with them and some you need none at all and a simple button press will win the game. I also dislike to sectioning into roles although this is my opinion but I feel like making Tanks overpowered on purpose makes other players have to rely on them more than others, Most of the time a good tank is more valuable than a good damage role. Theres another case of this with Supports being the opposite, Supports are so weak sometimes they can hardly live or do damage without another role defending them. Some supports are so weak in fact that they rarely get a kill (mainly mercy whos only damage is a little pistol). In my opinion Healers should be able to pick you up when youve fallen not just be there for you to step over. Which you will have to step over them cause Healers never get the play of the game. The Play of the game shows who did the "best" but most the time its just broken and goes for who got the most popups on thier screen which is usually not that special. If you look it up Blizzard has talked about how they score this and a ranked games and they have a very clunky scoring system. For Ranked its even wierder cause it doesnt matter at all what you do in your game, Helping people, Assists, Deaths, nothing. It only matters how many kills you get and if you win. With kills not doing much at all. If you lose you will go down a lot even if you did better than the enemy and your teammates will not be good early on in ranked. Another thing about this game is the Community, with the roles differences it makes people play very aggressively, as in aggressive to thier teammates as well with Tanks and Damage often yelling at support to do thier job when they can hardly stay alive as it is. Healers sometimes yell at the tanks too and its because the tank is the driving force of the team and you probably wont win if they die too much. Sometimes youll be winning and then suddenly the enemy team drops playing for fun to change to the most broken characters(usually a Bastion or Dva) and then will start winning. It makes it hard to have fun when that happens cause it happens so often. Also about the whole Overwatch 2 thing, Blizzard promised things, made people wait on it, then canceled things but still used them in marketting and put out a cheaper version of promised things. Its still fun if you can look past all of that but if you want a serious balanced and fair game dont look here.

review_comment: You still can’t see the leaderboard in replays. You still can’t see private profiles. The scoreboard doesn’t show healing received so you can’t really adapt your playstyle to what you can expect from your supports. No cool shiny tank borders. There isn't a way to preview any skin from the hero gallery. There still aren’t any after-match cards. They still haven’t brought back LFG(Looking For Group). Ever since they introduced the new player progression on profiles, they haven’t merged the old stats with the new stats. I also heard they’re wiping OW1 stats but I could be wrong. If you say anything that could be perceived as offensive in chat, you will get a point on your account towards silence, suspension, or ban. Reporting for anything but cheating and abusive chat will do literally nothing. People who’ve spent countless hours and money on this game can be spam reported by literally any group of malicious actors and get their account banned for anything(pfp, name, hero pick, play style, you name it). It’s not the report that matters, it’s the number of reports that matter. So long as someone paints a target on your back, you can lose access to the game even if you had your chat turned off! It’s so wild to me. Anyways, I feel like spending money on the game just to get your account banned from playing into the same petty 5-stack multiple games in a row(because there aren’t many players on at the time/they’re bleeding players) isn’t cool. Also having no one to review your report appeals and getting an automated response afterwards is *very comforting* to those who are totally blind-sided and actually enjoy the game but suddenly can’t play it anymore. The point is you shouldn’t get access to the game/your account revoked just for “communication” as if we’re playing VR chat where all you do is sit in a lobby and talk to people. This is a first person hero shooter game and I’d like to have access to the things I’ve purchased regardless of what people report me for(unless it’s cheating which actively compromises the game’s integrity). At most it should be revoked access to the voice channel and chat because no one ever uses those constructively anyways. Oh yeah, and chat… They will censor “GG EZ” with something silly but won’t censor slurs. Nice. Cool. Awesome. They will also ban you for saying profanity even though their characters in-game say profanity and the only way you can see profanity in chat is by turning off the filter. So if someone turns off the filter and actually sees you type profanity in chat, they can report you for it. Cool. It would be nice if they could reinstate all accounts that got banned for chat and simply silence them/give them endorsement level 0. If they’re really good/nice I’m sure they’ll climb back to endorsement level 1-2 in no time.

review_comment: I'm not a big gamer. I may play one or two titles, IF their easy to install/play on my niche hardware/software choices, and then abandon them when something else grabs my attention, and in this fashion I came into playing this game accidentally, never played OVW1, didn't, and still don't. give a sh!t about the integration of aspects from the first game or promises by the devs, or have any expectations based on preconceived notions or games from Christmas past. I randomly played this game on a friends Switch, the two joystick game play was crap but saw potential with a keyboard and mouse, and so when I got back to my machine I installed it (points for being able to play it on Linux, even though I'm pretty sure that wasn't planned by the devs) through steam and started my 180 hour journey into high blood pressure, rage-quitting a million times, and the search for a game that scratches all the itches and runs similarly on my hardware and OS combo. I don't know if its the mechanics, a lopsided matching system, flagrant cheating, or what but at least one game in every session I'm confronted with players that make it so I can't even leave spawn and make playing a horrible experience. And one game out of every session is what I would expect from a game as this, its hard enough to challenge, but I can be competitive, and is the reason I keep coming back. With every other game falling within the spectrum of those two vastly different experiences. I play anywhere between 10 and 20 games per session so I spend a good portion of my play time losing my sh!t because the game is impossible to play due to the aforementioned issues. Needing to know what I am getting myself into, I have researched and found a robust cheating community so I know that it exists, and could be quite pervasive. but I still am not a gamer Yoda and cannot pretend to know the difference between an elite player and a hacker, it all looks like magic to me and makes the game play just as frustrating either way. review_comment: Alright look, despite what everyone is going to review about this game, at its core, and as a whole, I still believe this game has value. It will never be what it once was 10 years ago. Fresh, revolutionary, and unique. The game space has changed and the transition from Overwatch 1 to Overwatch 2 may have been unnecessary all together, but in a way it, was a necessary evil for the future of the game. How Blizzard went about it was horrible including the lies and deceit in regard to the PvE content. The balance team has absolutely no idea what they are doing or have been doing for the past 7 years (both new AND old teams). However, after all is said and done, this game gets frequent updates (100x more than Overwatch 1 ever did) at it's whole, and at its core, will still be just a fun casual game to get on and play for a bit either by yourself or with friends. Anybody looking for a hard-hitting competitive game to grind and climb in should definitely look elsewhere. If you are looking for a fun casual experience, then Overwatch 2 will not disappoint you. To reiterate, this game is for casual gamers looking for a fun time getting to play with unique hero characters and learn the ins and outs of team play with some moments of of solo carry potential to spice things up. For those looking for die hard competitive game to grind hours and hours on, the horrible balance (especially as you climb the ranks) preventing you from potentially playing your newly discovered favorite heroes will, and at times horrible 50/50 matchmaking will drive you away.

review_comment: The game is great in my opinion but has too many flaws within the game that too many people have commented on already. The biggest fumble this game contains is one of the poorest matchmaking I've ever suffered through but is not what I'm discussing in particular. What I'm presenting is that the players who host custom matches are some of the most shallow and empty minded individuals that have ever graced this earth. To those who don't know, customs work where you host a match, edit the MS roster that people choose from, and then anyone can join and play. Sounds simple and should remedy bad matchmaking, right? Wrong! About 90% of the custom lobbies (among about 5-6 lobbies on a good day during peak hours) listed will be whats known as a "A WIN Rotate" game where MS costs are unrestricted, its a 1 round elimination match, and both teams are socially expected to take turns not playing the round (Whole Match) to allow the other team a guaranteed win (for the purpose of grinding the monthly missions, currency, and leveling up Mobile Suits) while match 'rotations' are normally a 5-6 minute process, meaning you have to wait every 10 minutes before its your turn to play. You might be thinking you can just AFK it and do something else while getting free progression right? Wrong! The game has this wonderful feature where you have to confirm you're MS after teams are formed but before the match actually starts, and if you don' confirm you'll get booted by the game, not the host, and have to wait until that last player slot is filled (I forgot to mention that all games, both official and custom can't actually be started unless you have a max lobby, normally 10-12 players). and after the match is said and done with, you have to manually confirm, again, the exp you gained and the rewards you may or may not have acquired (not guaranteed even with a win). My biggest quarrel with these lobbies is that they take players out of the pool, waste their time without them knowing or even caring because of 'EZ LOOT', and now you and everyone else who wants to play the game the way it was intended via custom or official matches have to wait for sometimes hours at a time just to get an actual shooter experience. In conclusion, customs could have been the cure for the worst matchmaking to exist and sometimes are, but the players in the community ruined that prospect.

review_comment: I've played this game for 40 hours on PC. and i have more hours on ps4. This game is fun, this game is frustrating, this game is literally the only modern Gundam game i enjoy playing. But if i play too long i get pissed. the gameplay revolves around stun mechanics. which would be fine, but its the only way to play this game. You have to equip weapons with good stun or you'll get nowhere in a match. The progression is a joke. you can only get really cool MS from a gacha game. good news though you can earn all the currency ingame... but than again, you can only get 3 per day by doing daily missions or doing maybe doing an AI mission. they suck. the level up system takes literally forever. im no where close to where i was on PS4 even after 40 hours.Finding a game most days is pointless. As of 5/14/2024 the game has less than 2000 players daily. Quickplay is unplayable because everyone goes into Ranked. Which is where all the try hards use all the Stun MS and weapons to win a game.For some reason even though the MS you can play are limited by a cost system, it being 100-700. they force you to play cost matches in rotations. so if you wanna play a 250 game but all there are are 400s and up, your outta luck. Why they did it like this i have no idea but its probably their biggest mistake sinse alot of the lower cost MS are really fun to play cause their so simple. like Basic GM and Zaku simple. i honestly just want a Gundam game that has a Singleplayer campaign, that lets you use a wide variety of gundams and MS. Or at the very least i want a modern take of Journey to Jaburo or Zeonic Front. This game can be fun but ultimatly i play it because i don't like the other Gundam games out right now and its the only descent one out right now that i kind enjoyed. But with no one playing it, and the game being less and less fun the more i revisit it. i dont think i'll be playing this anytime soon again.

Friendly fire is on so your teammates often stun you, sometimes to get an advantage, and Bandai does nothing to stop them despite having a reporting system built into the game. Bandai should either get a server or focus on using this system in a single player game. Oh wait they have one, Code Fairy, but they won't release that on PC. review_comment: This is a great game for any MS Gundam fan. It looks fantastic, you can control your MS relatively well, and you have lots of cool animations in battle. It may seem a bit clunky at first, but I liked it after a while. It makes you feel like your really piloting a massive, four story war machine that walks. The control scheme is a bit wonky from the start but you have the option to change the key bindings if you so choose. Honestly the stock control scheme isn't so bad once you get the hang of it. Despite the clunky nature of the controls, your MS are quite fast and agile ( depending on which one you choose). The MP is quite fun, when you're able to find a game. I haven't experienced bad servers per say, more like not many people playing at certain times it seems. It can take a while to find a game at times, but it's worth the wait IMO. Even single player battles are worth checking out. There isn't much in terms of single player content but it's at least replayable. You have a HUGE variety of MS's to choose from from the Guntank to the all the newer MS's ( I haven't watched the newer anime's, I'm watching them in order). You can upgrade them / customize your MS's to your hearts content. They have space battles and ground battles in which you can exit your mobile suit as your custom pilot and play boots on the ground. Over all its a great game with a bit of a tough learning curve, but not too bad. If you're willing to learn the game, it's a super fun and rewarding experience. Despite all the hate this game gets, I'd say it's worth playing and really worth giving a fair shake. If you have a decent PC and a decent graphics card this game runs consistently at 60 FPS easy on max settings ( while in battle / matches. The hub world drops FPS but not unplayable by any means with the right equipment). It isn't the most graphically intense game so it wont require much to run it smooth and crisp. I have my PC hooked up via ether net and I have experienced ZERO latency issues and no lag at all while in a match. I seriously cannot recommend checking it out enough if your a MS Gundam fan. You'll geek out in minutes of playing ( I sure did lol).

review_comment: Incredible...... amazing.......... graphics are great small details throughout the game BUT its 2024 and I now see why the franchise itself is going under. review_comment: Well, after a sloppy release, I waited a week before purchasing the game. I seriously had my doubts about how it was going to run. I set my Nvidia GForce RTX 3080 to "Ultra rendering" with "ray tracing" and "DLSS" set to ON. I also clicked on the "Super Rendering" for RTX NVIDIA cards. Hours of perfect play, not even one crash with my monitor set at 144 refresh rate. After a couple of hours of adjustments to mouse directions, keyboard keys, and my Thrustmaster hardware, the game has been smooth as silk and looks absolutely incredible. The detail is extraordinary. I can't believe how "real" it appears. Better than I imagined! I never thought I'd say this but...Nice job Microsoft and Asobo. Your efforts are noted. The cloud system is working perfectly. With over 4500 hours on MSFS 2020, I don't foresee having to go back now, ever. Three "must haves" I recommend for excellent game play: 1. Relatively new computer (I have a 2023 i9) 2. Powerful Broadband (I have unlimited) 3. Newer accelerator card (I have G-Force RTX 3080). If they continue with the fixes as they show up like we did with 2020, and get the marketplace up and running correctly with all my purchased planes, they will have knock this one "out of the park". Thanks MS!! No disappointments here!!

review_comment: I've been playing MSFS 2024 since it's rather difficult release. I wanted to rack up over 50 hours before giving a review. Was the release rough....absolutely. I'm running a 4090, i9 10th Gen intel, 80GB ram, at 1440p 1GB Fiber, I know I had better luck then some of the initial day one people. Microsoft and Asobo could have done better to start but looking at where my experience is now, I must say they've done fantastic. It's stunning and even more magnificent when you think about the gravity of this undertaking. There's bugs here and there, VR needs a little work, however, if you put in the effort and have some patients, I find it worth every penny. There's so much to do and learn. Career mode is getting my attention right now. Love it! Overall, I'm really pleased with it's current state. The turnaround over the last couple weeks is nothing short of EPIC. It didn't take long. There will always be more work and improvements. Looking forward to many years in this sim and if they come out with a new one......I'll get that too. Asobo deserves more credit and awards then they'll get for MSFS 2024. If day 1 ran the way it does today...Game of the Year! Respect what this can do and understand the limits of your current systems and go for it.

review_comment: I am not recommending this product but may revise this rating when the publishers get it remotely acceptable. This is not a Beta test, people are paying more for this game than 99.9% of what it out there. This was today's experience, with 77 hours flying time in this version, level ~30, and had FS2020 since it was launched. Instead of enjoying a Sunday morning mission or two, I have shut down my plane and decided to finally share my frustrations. Started up my well-tuned RTX4090 based system, and Quest3 VR setup. Started a light freight mission in a Draco X; never flown before. Checklist OK and as soon as I move the fuel conditioner forward my right eye (only) has a horrendous shimmering which makes playing impossible (Googled and I am not alone). Never mind, annoying but hey. So back out to Missions, let’s do a parachute mission in a Cessna 208B. Into the mission, outside prep done and now in the pilot seat. Fuel on, battery on, avionics on, fuel boost o... hang on, where's my passengers? Oh another mission where the mission doesn't actually start, let's check my toolbar. Oh look the squashed barely readable toolbar bug is back. This isn't fun. It really isn't. Last night I had a 3-hour mission. 2 hours in after returning from maybe 20 mins of autopilot I'm back in VR and Oh look the Mouse and Keyboard are not responding at all in the game (fine in any other of course) so I can't respond to ATC, I can't cheat in extra fuel because there's nowhere near enough provided at the start for this flight (yes I have leaned back the fuel a lot) so before long I am spiralling to my death and reputation back from B to D. Microsoft you honestly do deserve everything you are getting over this half-baked joke and all you butt kissing sycophants that are preening around saying "it's all part of the journey baby chill out man" well f--k you, this is supposed to be a AAA game. You think Half Life Alyx would get the ratings it has if half your experience ended in a tantrum. Comments welcome but please note I honestly don't care what you think (unless you're agreeing with me).

review_comment: I have now played for 52 hours and these are my thoughts. The release was disappointing at best and unacceptable at worst. For reference I am a commercial pilot and these are my thoughts for the game in its current state. The first comment is about the streaming service I have 1 GIG internet and I am hooked to ethernet with a great PC and the streaming runs terribly. I almost think the scenery looks just like MSFS 2020 or worse in some areas. The second thing is performance, I am scared to do any long form flights because I know the game will crash and since you cant save your position for some reason all of that flight will be a waste of my time (this will be a common theme in my problems). The third grief is career mode, this was heavily advertised content and I am extremely disappointed, the aircraft selection is bad, the missions are repetitive and I have every rating in career mode and I still majorly receive 172 flights which is insane. Also most of the actual missions I have attempted to complete do not work and I have to fail or quit the mission at the very end. The ATC hold short issues are bad, ATC approach procedures are bad, ATC handoffs are bad, everything ATC related is bad. I always get docked points for poor airline procedures which is B.S. because it doesn't work. Next gripe, many aircraft are just simply broken, F18 nosewheel steering, Airbus family avionics issues, 737 autopilot bugs, Bonanza audio and flap issues, tailwheel controllability, every single plane has some issue that hinders its use in a major way. Next issue landing challenges, many of the challenges are buggy and spawn you in a stall attitude at approach speed. Next gripe multiplayer, its buggy and broken, many times I cant see my friends or vice versa, and there are incorrect aircraft models. Last major, major, major issue that is unforgivable. You have wasted not only my time but my money as well as everyone else's. Whats funny is by the time I was able to play the game since the servers were down on launch I couldn't even request a refund. I actually cannot fathom how Microsoft could not afford to have a group of pilot playtesters, or even just one to help discover bugs. The game is in an unplayable state and I will not play it until it is worth my time and money. The way I think about it is if you released this game as a DLC to MSFS 2020 people #1 wouldn't buy it and #2 it would be a complete fail, but to release this as a stand alone game is gross. I know im not going to get my money back so I wont even bother but you have proved this week that you do not care about your customers time or money. So to wrap this up I thank you for wasting 52 hours of my life that I will not get back and 170$.

review_comment: I guess this simulation itself is fine, but many systems are just broken. Career mode is just an absolute joke. Once you finally do unlock what we all want, flying the big boy planes full of passengers, it is just broken. Most of the missions have you flying the 737, no Airbus love here. The systems work fine except for the autothrottle. The autothrottle has a mind of its own. After you struggle with that, normally just turning autothrottle off, you are then on your way to the destination. Guess what happens when you land? Congrats! You buttered that landing! Well now lets reward you.... The mission will not end. Pull up to the gates, shut down the engines, let the PAX out, well thats it.... you just get to sit here stuck. It will not end. The AI voices.... MY GOD the AI voices..... why???? I am okay with it, if it made sense. Half the time you are being stepped on by ATC, want the altimeter setting? Try to decipher the horrid AI voice. It cannot make sense of numbers and pauses in phrasing. I cannot recommend this in its current state. One time I landed, and instead of telling me to taxi ASAP, my copilot thinks "It's time to serve the passengers drinks and snacks" well damn, that sucks. Oh and now I am stuck at the gate, it wont end. No issue lets press the shortcut to skip. I am now on a 200 mile final... Wonderful. Do not waste your time on this right now. Turbulence has been improved but honestly, the systems are just as "good" as they were in 2020. There is still no weather radar. Even if you do bite the bullet and grind it out, you will crash your shiny new plane from a bug. I started in a Cessna 208 and was on top of the airport terminal.... so broken. This is just a joke of gameplay. Pure simmers, which I would consider myself, this is a slight improvement, but just avoid career mode. I promise you will rage quit.

review_comment: MFS 2024 was released too early! Excellent visuals but only when Microsoft servers work. Everything is streamed, even with a gigabit connection there are problems and slow texture loading. On slower connections I would not recommend playing. Would like to see an option added to be able to download the game data locally and stream only the highest resolution scenery data. You will need a very high end PC to see the best graphics even game being mostly streamed. I had some issues with controls, sometimes not working or bugging out. Marketplace is missing at launch (Coming soon) this is not acceptable for a game with such price tag. Currently Career mode is very broken and it needs time to be fixed to be enjoyable. It is not fun when every other mission has game breaking bugs, either can't complete a mission or get heavily penalised for things that are bugged. For instance to finish a mission you have to park your plane in a building which is impossible, some missions just randomly end and states that you crashed. If connections drops or disconnects, the game just exits to main menu, and you loose your mission progress. Photographer mode is great and relaxing, it encourages to visit places that you would have never thought of visiting. It is very hard to recommend this game at the moment, especially for the premium price. I would suggest waiting a year or two for most things to get fixed. Beware, if the streaming servers go offline you can't start the game and I would not be surprised if there is another new release in 4 years for a full price and no discount to previous version owners.

review_comment: So the scenery is unfortunately the best we have seen, however the building (at airports specifically) are lack luster and the same from 2020. But this doesn't justify it enough for more, DO NOT give into the hype. The clouds/weather?? Horrid, the higher clouds look 2D like they're a green screen, all asobo planes are the same, with minimal difference. Its the same "1:1" input from periphials (Honeycomb for me) but the yoke and plane it self actually interpulate the input weird and slow down and speed up making it IMPOSSIBLE to fight/fly in the wind, same as 2020. When it comes to these sims, I don't like to compensate for lack of thought and development, like the yokes (asobo planes mainly) not being a 1:1 input (Like Xplane!!) or having to buy am updated scenery (MSMapEnhancement) just to see an up to date map that is not gross Bing maps. Also the ATC, wow no improvement was made here, "Cessna November 12345" ????? WHAT? Also when doing the career, why is the game going to encourage Ctrl+E when you are supposed to be LEARNING HOW TO FLY? Ctrl+E SHOULD NOT be encouraged in a training/career/student pilot atmosphere. Career mode seems to me to be a target for younger and actual student pilots learning how to fly, (idk about yall but I cant Ctrl+E on my PPL checkride) Makes no sense. I still as of this moment prefer 2020 over this, however do not mistake this as me saying 2020 is great, I prefer XP12 over all, but thats not my point. Think and research before buying, happy flying.

It was a bit simplistic on career mode to get to commercial pilot where you can start earning credits for doing jobs, but if you are new to sims, its probably useful. Air Traffic Control is nothing like real ATC commands and it has you holding at strange places on the airfield. It's a fun sim and the graphics are fantastic. Good fun on the challenges trying the Mach loop and other races. 8.1 hrs continuous playing , no crash to desktop, very stable, good frame rates, no stutter, quick loading and I only saw one floating aircraft. Very enjoyable day and way above what I was expecting based on reviews I've read. Playing on a Lenovo laptop, i9 core, RTX 4080 2TB drive, so above recommended spec. Very happy so far. review_comment: I was really looking forward to this flight sim, as I have bought every single version since MSFS 98 and I must have spent thousands of hours "in the air". So, I thought this time, I would spend a LOT of money and I bought the Aviator version. I was a bit sad when I was uninstalling all of the previous add-ons and the MSFS 2020 itself, but I was also full of expectations of trying out the new 2024 sim. Despite the mostly negative reviews, I thought, that those were some small issues which could be fixed in a couple of days. And yet what did I get? A "game", which would not even launch at all? I am a software developer and I have very much understanding about what the whole team is going through right now, but I cannot remain silent, such things just must not happen. And I know there are always some issues when going live, but I would never ever offer this unprepared, unfinished, thoroughly untested product knowing, how much impact factor will it certainly have. I am trying to refrain from rude words, but this is a big mess, a HUGE fail. Someone made a VERY bad decision releasing it prematurely or even worse, maybe just in order to make this product to be tested by a paying community, since the number of testers' staff is missing. This is unacceptable. Yet, I am pretty sure the bugs will eventually be fixed and I might consider buying the stuff once again, but now I have just placed my request for a refund. I am sorry, but this is not what a paying customer deserves.
