IF you try to talk to tower they wont respond or the game won't let you respond to a request, then the game docs you points and you can't get your license. Try to taxi in KAVX and see the state of the taxi ways. Planes on the ground are missing landing gear and are literally floating on the tarmac. The list goes on and on. Hope they can fix the issues and some third party dev comes up with better ATC.. Not sure why clearance delivery is unavailable at certain airports so you cant get IFR clearance on the ground. This was available in the previous game. Lots of class D airports do not have tower operating for some reason. One positive is there are very few CTDs compared to fs2020. The main issue I’ve encountered is that VR is simply busted. If you want to fly in VR then good luck getting the VR toolbar pop up to work consistently; also, the mouse cursor simply stops working at random times, with the only workaround seeming to be to activate the VR controller and to trigger point at something. What the actual?? I’ve also had the in-game VR mission boxes (during career mode) just totally bug out with weird font styles and sizes. All of this is totally immersion breaking, and usually ends up with me quitting to go play something else (life’s too short for this nonsense). This game seems alright if you just want to play using a monitor, but if you’re a VR player then brace yourself for repeated frustration or (my recommendation) come back in a few months when they’ve fixed things that should never have been broken in the first place.

review_comment: I have around 800 hours in FS2020 and 2024, and much more in previous versions. 2020 finally got to be pretty darn good, but it was lacking a career mode, which was what made me excited for 2024, and really the only reason I bought it. The real problem, is that for some reason, the things that worked well in 2020 do NOT work in 2024, and it ruins career mode because you end up crashing or not flying properly and get docked points. Things like IFR, ATC (which was OK in 2020, not great), controller inputs don't work right, wind/turbulence is completely ridiculous, AP in the 737 just constantly sloshes the trim up and down and the plane violently bobs like its in the ocean, grass/dirt acts like snow/ice, especially with even a breath of wind. I can go on, but it's really unplayable and it just leads to frustration. This is really sad, and it's been radio silence on any acknowledgment of the issues, or planned fix schedule since release. review_comment: I am an avid flight simmer, and really liked FS 2020, but I also got it two years after it came out, so I did not live through the growing pains that sim had. When I started most of the "game ending" bug were squashed. Enter FS 2024. The release for it was terribly handled, mostly due to lack of preparation for the sheer number of people expected. Then there are the bugs in the sim itself, mostly around the more "gamey" parts of the sim. Parts such as Career mode, or activities, and other things like that. I run this sim in free flight. The integration of simbrief into the provided flight planner makes flight planning very easy. The included approach charts is also a gem of an addition. The visuals are spectacular once you have everything dialed in. Dlss4 is said to be a game changer, though at this time it has yet to be implemented in the sim. I am confident this sim will become the Gold Standard FS2020 was. One major thing I think needs rethinking is the streaming of so many things that should be stored locally such as aircraft files, but I also understand why that decision was made. review_comment: Firstly lets address the elephant in the room - Game or Sim? It's both actually. Eg I've spent most of my time in the career mode of MSFS 2024 and after acquiring my PPL I've been taking people up for sight seeing flights in the Cessna 172. Even though there's an element of reality to how things are done it feels like a game when flown as per the instructions. The simulator side of things is where MSFS 2024 really comes alive. I took the A320 V2 for a quick flight from YSCB to YSSY using Simbrief to import a flight plan and then, via the inbuilt flight planner, gained access to all of the required charts for each airport. By following correct procedures and utilising the included charts it's easy to forget that you're sitting in front of a PC. Sure, there are some bugs that need to be fixed but nothing game breaking for me thus far. If you're sitting on the fence go buy it. It'll only get better from here.

review_comment: After initially kneeling down under the launch rush, the servers seem to have stabilized somewhat and we can see the actual game. Make no mistake: there are a LOT of issues to fix. Career mode has a wide selection of glitches (runway direction issues, mis-spawns, connectivity issues), terrain generation logic could use some work (especially roads and water), framerates are still below my comfort zone, popular joysticks aren't recognized automatically and controls setup is a pain in the backside. Also whoever decided aircraft can't be downloaded to disk instead of being streamed still needs to be fired. Right now, it's a toss-up between recommended or not. What makes me lean towards the latter is how poor the performance is, especially in VR. Sub-10 FPS at 50% rendering scale should not happen on a 7800X3D/RTX 3080Ti combo, not in 2024 at least. Stuttering is horrible and ruins the experience.

review_comment: This game had possibly the worst launch in the history of games, but what can you expect when you have around a million people using all of your bandwidth for a cloud based game. Yeah there are still some issues such as in career mode some planes don't even have sound or some airports make the plane crash into thin air but, when you get passed these issues the game is amazing. Career mode brought life into something and it has actually become addicting to play now. The quality has had a massive improvement especially at night where lights look like actual lights. The world looks even more realistic than the previous MSFS 2020. While I do enjoy this game on single screen, (first world problem incoming) I would love to play this game with my triple screen setup, but it becomes the most unstable game possible. You would think a sim title would follow after 90% of other sim titles with triple screen support, but it is the same thing passed on from MSFS 2020, but worse. Still, I would recommend this game especially when they get all of their issues fixed.

review_comment: First let me start with this, DO NOT READ ALL NEGATIVE REVIEWS!!!, everyone of those reviews are related to day 1 launch issues of any anticipated title such as this one there is 0 game play experience related to it, now the download process was easy and quick a lot better then the previous game one and done through steam, once you launch the game it will load you directly into the main menu where it'll do your first initial stuff like signing into your xbox account, getting your presets and graphics set up, you know normal stuff with first launch of any new game, this is where it starts to get more interesting the visuals graphics are beautiful, sounds are good, i love the new main menu, what i am very disappointed in is that with "Career mode" it's not set into live weather, day/night cycle and dynamic seasons, not set with the online settings of seeing other players this is pretty much "offline" single player and that is very disapointing, they have a "Free fly" mode which majority of you will be familiar with compared to 2020 of picking a start location and end destination, picking a plane and just do what you want. missions i don't think are in free fly mode. oh another thing if you use a flight stick, be sure to be ready to sit there for a few hours to keybind every little thing since it won't auto do it for you like 2020 where you just plugged it in and was all set. i recommend the game because of the fact it's an upgrade from 2020 and the career mode is a proper gameplay loop of learning each and every aircraft, along with proper flight training, doesn't make you feel lost and overwhelmed of what to do and asking others for help when they will mostly tell you to oh just ALT-F4 that'll fix it kind of stuff. free fly does not have a progression system to unlock certain planes based off of their role, so if you have planes from 3rd party like PMDG and flybywire, fenix you should be able to use them no problem,

review_comment: It's rough around the edges for sure, but it can also be really amazing. Playing in VR is probably the closest I'll get to piloting a real plane. I certainly have a lot of "wow" moments. The flight model seems pretty good too, but not for every airplane. Live weather and traffic generally work well, and I also really like that you can "rewind" live weather up to 24 hours, since I normally play at night. And of course, the scenery is amazing; far and away better than you'll find in any other flight simulator. There are bugs. Sometimes controls and/or VR interactions frustratingly stop working temporarily, there can be weird glitches with live traffic, ATC, and graphics, but nothing game breaking for me. Overall I definitely recommend, though if you're reading this, note that I generally only fly GA aircraft in free flight mode.

review_comment: At this point, it is way too buggy to buy. My computer isn't the best, but it should be able to run this game fine. Even just booting up the game takes about 5 minutes. Then if I want to do a free flight I have to wait another 5. But then for some reason almost none of the planes even load in, it's just my pilot sitting in midair. The world around me is also almost never loaded in. If I still want to take off with my invisible 747, well... I have no control of the aircraft. There have been a couple times where the exterior of my plane (not the interior) loaded in and I was able to take off. But for some reason, a couple minutes after leaving the ground, I lose complete control of my throttle. Sometimes it has a mind of its own and it either goes all the way up or all the way down (usually the latter) and I end up crashing. The game will automatically put you back in the sky after crashing, which sounds good on paper, but not when you spawn at 0kts and 1000 feet above the ground. If I crash then I have to completely restart the flight every time. Well maybe I feel like not playing free flight, and playing some career mode. Well you may have guessed it already, it does not work. I cant even complete the second mission, because when I load in my pilot is floating above the ground a few feet from the aircraft, and the passenger is just walking in place. When I load in to the actual aircraft, I can't move. The only thing that actually worked for me was this one F/A-18 challenge mission that I had a decent amount of fun with because it was my first time actually being able to fly bug free. The same cant be said for the other challenges though. This may feel like a bit of a ramble but I wanted to detail some of the things you may encounter after paying $70 to play Microsoft bug simulator. If they take time to improve the game and make it bug free then I may actually change my rating, but at this point, it's unplayable. Just stick to 2020.

review_comment: I bought this game last night. I was expecting slow load times and graphics degradation based on the need to connect to a cloud service for high definition graphics. I live in Germany, and internet speeds here where I am are not nearly what they are in the rest of western world. What I found was quite different. The load time from hitting the "play" icon on the Steam page to receiving the "start" prompt was about 3:26. That's about where I was at with FS 2020. The time it took to load a free flight was about 45 seconds. It seems that once you load a location, the program caches the data for quicker loading the next time. I could tell I was experiencing some graphics degradation, but I strongly suspect that's due to the limits on my internet speed. What I can't stomach is the fact that Tobii Eye Tracker does not work well with this program. The views were all off. The system was definitely recognizing movement, but it did not align with the actual movement of my head. I went online to see if there was something I was doing wrong, and the Tobii website recommended downloading something called opentrack. I did this, and it killed Tobii altogether. I watched a few videos where people were going in, modifying test files, this sort of thing. Not really something I would expect to need to do with a Microsoft product in 2024. BL, if you're not a Tobii user, maybe it's OK. Maybe it works with track IR. Maybe I'll try it in VR. If someone has any tips on how to fix this...it could just be me.

review_comment: So everyone in the Flight Sim community has been waiting for the immensely hyped MSFS 2024. Well after almost 300 hours and some next-to-nothing update patches...I have to say I'm a bit disappointed. I, for one, was very much looking forward to Career Mode for it to give a bit more purpose to flying flights more than just scenery and the fun of setting up a flight, taking off, and then descending on an approach into an awesome looking location! Those are all still awesome to do but Career Mode gives that added sense of accomplishment and goal setting that MSFS2020 was missing. Well, unfortunately, Career Mode has so many bugs and mistakes that some missions are just more of an annoyance than enjoyable because the lack of any QA on the missions instantly kills the immersion and purpose of Career Mode altogether. If its not loading into the mission in the middle of trees or with the aircraft surrounded by buildings, people, and/or other aircraft so you can't move without hitting something, then its ATC telling you to taxi to a runway without clearance to cross the other runway which is required to get to the point they told you to go. So then you get yelled at and your overall score suffers because YOU screwed up! It really just feels like there was not enough, or any, Quality Assurance and verification on missions to make sure they worked the way they should. Then there is the whole factor about the aircraft themselves and how they, too, are all bugged and not working properly. I get it....its a new simulator and it took a bit for 2020 to be as good as it is but c'mon guys....you already knew what you were doing this time and you had 4 years to make it a killer sim! After all that being said, it is still worth getting and flying the free flights and activities! There are changes and fixes on the horizon, Im sure of it and my hope is that 2025 will bring the fixes and updates that MSFS2024 desperately needs to live up to its hype! Happy Flying! CYA!

review_comment: The career mode is competely full of bugs and glitches. The physics are very unrealistic, such as being able to fly the 172 at 20kts without stalling, and large heavy aircraft able to fly under 100kts without stalling, and glide down the entire runway. Game crashes randomly. The keybinds never save, and always have to keybind yokes/controllers/keyboard every time the sim loads. After adjusting the graphic settings to ultra, the graphic settings always get set back to default when the sim reloads, even though I have RTX4080, i9-14900, 64gb ram. Several of the aircraft are bugged with inoperable functions that are suppose to work, including autopilot that is bugged in several aircraft. Setting up the Thrustmaster Airbus Throttle Quadrant is a nightmare. When creating your pilot all of the hairstyles look like a wig. Mountains such as the Himalayas look more like tall round bumps rather than jagged mountains. Water effects with tires are non-existent unlike advertised, voices are all with American accent in international countries unlike what was advertised. Sim randomly crashes. Buildings are very generic and not much different from previews MSFS titles. Active forest fire smoke is not shown unlike in MSFS2020. Live weather always gets turned off when returning to menu. Honestly this currently isn't worth the pricetag that they are offering, and I feel lied to about the features advertised.

Most bugs though involve the AI assigning you a runway that doesn't make sense with the wind (add the choice for us to chose runway if we want especially on uncontrolled). AI ATC sending you through icing conditions in a 172, AI mission generation choosing military airports for civilian missions, AI path finding wanting you to slam on your brakes and turn at a taxi way 100FT or less from touchdown, AI......etc. They really need to fix what their AI is doing. review_comment: As a sim player, its fun. I like the career mode and its features. That is something I've been looking for for a long time. As a pilot irl, its awful. Flight mechanics are wrong, speeds are wrong, power settings are wrong (75% load in the DA40 NG should get you roughly 120Kts depending on conditions, NOT 70...), the "co-pilot" will dock you points for things that are perfectly normal, but that's just how simulators are. Anyone with a pilot's license knows that sims are never as accurate as the real thing, and often are FAR from the real thing. If you want to use MSFS 2024 to learn how to fly, take it with a grain of salt. If you're using it to improve or hone your real flying skills, go to a flight school and ask to use their sims or just go fly with a CFI. But if you want to have fun and experience getting paid fake money to fly various planes around for different jobs, or even just seeing what runways the Beluga can actually take off from while at max weight, this sim is PERFECT!!! Again, its not a 1-to-1 replication of real life... DO NOT TRY TO LAND A CESSNA CARAVAN AT 180 KNOTS IN REAL LIFE!!! Use the sim for that... but it is fun to try. (side note, TURN THE TURBULENCE DOWN IF YOU WANT TO HAVE FUN!!! It is automatically set to "realistic" and its just insane updrafts and the plane attempting to tailspin itself at cruise speed)

review_comment: OMG, guys...Asobo/MS. Not sure what happened here. I used to be a developer and 28 years in IT. I've been flying MSFS since 1983. The thin client vs rich client thing is one thing. That's an architecture decision and I commend you for the bravery to go there, even though mileage will vary greatly for different use cases (internet bandwidth especially). It's all over the place, like I'm a member of the alpha testing team or something. Don't get me wrong. I am the biggest fan of this franchise ever and have bought and owned every version I've been able get my grubby little paws on, over time. But this is definitely the worst initial release I've experienced. I know you guys will get it right eventually. It's just a bit of a shocker, dudes. I am about to don my Pimax Crystal and go for a relaxing "detox" VR flight in MSFS2020. IMHO, MSFS2024 was not even close to ready for prime time release, as it stands now. Too many missing features and instability. For now, if you already own MSFS2020, I would just stick with that for a while, until this thing gets fixed. Perhaps it's just me...

I dove into career mode. cutscenes and flying went smooth with a solid FPS with graphic set to mid. Looks amazing, flies amazing sounds great and its immersive as hell. Im on a potato and it was butter smooth. my pc is 4 years old so not great, it even handled VR well. i did encounter some bugs with missions randomly failing me which was very frustating but that stuff is fixable. Overall we have to look at what can be fixed and what is core game..........the core game here is great. Basically American Truck sim for aviation junkies like me. handles well on controller which i did use. I have a fairly expensive sim pit that i build for DCS but it worked well with my HOTAS also. The missions and the money making is a huge step up from the last one which was disappointing. I get that some people are having issues opening but I was able to download and install first try with almost everything working. Also a more integrated way for us all to make missions for each other would be cool. I'm only 11 hours in and love it. The other part I like and hate at the same time is the simplicity of controls, again, helicopter using the Logitech 3D Pro should have the collective/throttle intertwined automatically instead of having to go through the confusing menus trying to make it work for each and every helicopter. Anyways, I went with the Holy Grail version, and don't regret it because we all know Microsoft will make the updates. Give it time, if you need to wait for it to get the bugs out, do it! The overall negative review should not be there though.

review_comment: I would recommend Flight Simulator 2024. After 4 days of being unable to log on to my X-box account and unable to play the game. The glitch was finally fixed and now I can play the game without any further problems. Although in the beginning after completing my character, picking out my plane in free flight. After I picked my departure destination and then right after I clicked my arrival destination my game crashed right to the desktop. This happened 4 times. So I then went to career mode and started my flight training and so far my game has not crashed. Although they expect perfection during my flight training. The average person just wanting to be able to fly for fun might lose interest or be frustrated enough to find another game. Flight Simulator 2024 is not an FAA certified flight training program. So expecting perfection to obtain a private pilots licence from the average person wanting to fly for fun isn't really in their best interests to encourage someone to take an interest in flying. But so far I am really impressed with what Flight Simulator 2024 has accomplished and would agree it's the best flight simulator to date. I have owned every single flight simulator that Microsoft Flight Simulator has made all the way back to 1982. So I can say with a certain degree from personal experience they have made an excellent flight simulator. My concerns after Flight Simulator 2020 was not having a working Air Traffic Control System that would give you IFR course corrections and put you right in front of the runway for landing. Especially because in Flight Simulator 2020 they just gave you GPS to the airport and wouldn't give you course corrections and line you up in front of the runway. In Flight Simulator 2020 I couldn't use the bad weather for this very reason and the traffic controller would say "Go where we talked about". Instead of IFR course corrections to line you up in front of the runway in really bad weather conditions. I understand Flight Simulator 2024 has an awesome weather system and as long as they have a working IFR Air Traffic Control System as well. Then I will be a great fan of it. So after playing 20 hours of Flight Simulator 2024 I am so far impressed. Once they get all the bugs out and things start running smooth the way they want I think everyone will agree it's the best simulator out there. Again and I can't state enough as long as they have a working Air Traffic Control System that can line you up in front of any given runway and give course corrections in bad weather it will be the greatest simulator out there. Especially in career mode which is something that I have wanted and so many other flight simulator gamers and real pilots have wanted. It's opened up a real world of possibilities and added a new dimension to the flight simulator which I am really excited about. So I have high expectations for Flight Simulator 2024. I plan to dig deep inside this sim to see if all my expectations will come to fruition. I encourage others to come in to this flight simulator with an open mind. I hope it's everything they claim it will be and I will be checking to see if it has everything I was disappointed about in Flight Simulator 2020. So for now I am recommending Flight Simulator 2024 to everyone to try.

review_comment: I cannot recommend this sim as an improvement to MSFS 2020. The detail of the terrain is much better in 2024, but everything else is worse. I fly exclusively in VR and 2024 does not run as smoothly, even after weeks of tweaking and testing. The textures, clouds, sun and stars look far worse. The flight model doesn't feel as realistic. The planes seem to wander left and right on their yaw axis for no reason. Rudder control seems either too "locked in" when taxiing or you don't have any control at all. The career mode is a mess. Work hard to buy your own plane and start building your company only to find that sometimes there are no missions available at all. The economy is not well planned. Some missions don't pay enough while others are insanely lucrative. Same goes for the cost of new aircraft and maintenance. For example, a moderately bouncy landing (not a crash) in the X Cub might damage a $1200 tire along with a $40000 landing gear. I also had one instance where the X Cub was in fairly worn condition, but everything was serviceable, and it checked out fine during preflight. I lost all elevator control during a very straight and level flight, which by itself would be incredibly unlikely, but then I figured my only option would be to reroute to the nearest airport and land with only trim and throttle control, which I managed to do, but because I couldn't fly the plane and I couldn't fix the plane, the only option was to abort the mission. Things could be done much better. At this point, I have little hope that they will fix this sim and right now the fact is that MSFS 2020 is FAR better than this.

MSFS 2024 caught up to everything xplane was better at than 2020, and added amazing graphics, many more planes and aircraft types, it includes the whole world in beautiful photogrammetry, and it brings with it the amazing community, and addons that we all enjoyed in MSFS 2020. review_comment: Many improvements have been made since the dismal initial launch. The game is now at least playable. Career mode is an interesting change to what we had with MSFS 2020, but still needs some tweaks to improve the experience. The sim still has not, to my knowledge, been patched to the point that you can guarantee when launching a flight your aircraft won't spawn clipped into a building, or with a giant red "ERROR" message where your pilot avatar should be sitting in the cockpit, but things are moving in the right direction. I'm looking forward to the implementation of more features in the coming months (such as the marketplace going live) to flesh out the sim and add more depth and immersion. The AI still needs some work as, for example, the voices of passengers are really monotonous and boring, especially if you're spending time doing similar missions to increase your experience in career mode. Texture and terrain loading can still be patchy and slow, especially if you're flying over dense urban areas, but once you're at higher altitudes the sim certainly looks quite impressive in it's realism. The developers have made great strides in the past couple of months. Hopefully this trend is one which will continue!

They do realize that many people in the world don't have fast internet connections? Most of use have crap speeds, and overpay for that. I hope this cloud tech works, but it feels WAY too much like bleeding edge technology. This game is popular, but its not that popular. I don't think MS understands the audience of this software. What they want are dads who buy it, and then play it for 10 hours, and go away. The real audience is people who are interested in civilian aviation, people who want to spend time exploring the cool virtual globe. The virtual globe is absolutely the highlight of this game (its not a sim). The aircraft are interesting, and the flight models shows definite improvements over the simcade MS2020. review_comment: So far my experience in VR is very mixed. I'm using a 13900K/RTX4090 with Pimax Crystal, and it does look stunning. The trouble is that I just can't get it to run truly smooth. It's actually very odd. I can turn up settings that would have killed performance in 2020 with almost no degradation (like ambiant occlusion), but on the other hand, turning them down or even off in many cases produces very little meaningful improvement. So I'm kind of stuck with a kind of mediocre performance where everything looks great, but stutters enough to always be kind of annoying. It's still early days, and there are still many aspects of the settings whose consequences aren't exactly clear, so while going from MSFS 2020 to 2024 in VR is way, way better than my experience going from X-Plane 11.5 to 12 was, it really needs attention--and please, please, please give us DFR ASAP!

review_comment: I still cannot recommend buying Flight Sim 2024 over 2020.. Consistency is not there. ATC is not there. The walkarounds are not complete. Marketplace? Support for Thrustmaster Airbus throttles and hardware is slim. Calibration of hardware sensitivities is non-existent. Checklists aren't great. DLC aircraft have no co-pilot in the plane, so you don't hear your own ATC communication, only ATC's response. The pushback tug frequently push me back wherever they feel like it, and by the time I try to correct their wrong turn, I'm facing the wrong way anyway. Also, at idle, every plane moves. Unreal. Ever heard of "breakaway thrust?" You know, the amount of power required to make the plane start moving forward.. Also, the included aircraft seem to have issues following flight plans. Also, with a mouse, you cannot select manual modes by clicking the scroll wheel, nor can I find a way to program that.. The sim has no idea what key is bound to it currently, and neither do I.. Do note, I don't hate your game. I'm rooting for y'all. But I also paid $200 and studied 20+ hours of programming to still have high difficulty in FS2024 doing what I can CONSISTENTLY do in Flight Sim 2020. Hope this updated review can be helpful.
name: Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024
